title: My Fair Princess: The Pampered Imperial Concubine Chen and the Emperor’s Road to Redemption
author: Mo Qing Dai Ming
synopsis:
After transmigrating into the body of the Qianlong Emperor’s pampered Concubine Chen, she decided to just let it all go.
Jiang Rao opened her eyes to find herself as the most arrogant Concubine Chen in the harem, held in the palm of the Emperor’s hand, where he would give her the stars if she asked for the moon.
Until that day at the hunting grounds, when the Fifth Prince shot a girl with an arrow, and the Emperor tremblingly asked that question—
“Is your mother… Xia Yuhe?”
The grape in Jiang Rao’s hand went “plop” and fell.
Wait! Xia Yuhe from the banks of Daming Lake?!
Is this, for heaven’s sake, *My Fair Princess* (Huan Zhu Ge Ge)?!
Watching Xiao Yanzi enter the palace, Ziwei identify her father, and the Fragrant Concubine dance, the plot roared forward with great intensity.
Jiang Rao decisively chose: Eat melons, watch the show, and absolutely do not get involved!
But the Emperor insisted on provoking her—
“Rao’er, let me teach you how to read the memorials.”
“Rao’er, these pearls from the Southern Seas are only fit for you to wear.”
“Rao’er…”
Until the day Han Xiang entered the palace and the Emperor’s heart began to waver.
Jiang Rao sneered, packed her bags, and prepared to leave the palace: “Your Majesty, this concubine is tired.”
Qianlong finally panicked.
Later, the entire Forbidden City witnessed—
The Son of Heaven lurking outside Yongshou Palace every day:
“Rao’er, shall I tear down the Baoyue Pavilion?”
“Rao’er, look at the jasmine I just planted; doesn’t it look just like the one in your hair?”
“Rao’er… please don’t ignore me.”
Xiao Yanzi and the others were dumbfounded: So the pampered concubine was truly pampered, and the Emperor would actually kneel to win his wife back!

chapters.title: Do you still remember Xia Yuhe from the banks of Daming Lake?
chapters.content:
The autumn of the twenty-second year of the Qianlong reign, Mulan Hunting Grounds.

The sound of hooves thundered across the grass, and the shouts of the Eight Banners’ disciples startled a flock of birds. Qianlong, dressed in riding gear, sat on his horse, squinting at a deer that had been flushed out, his fingers gently stroking the bowstring.

“Your Majesty—” The voice was delicate and sweet, dragging out a long, lingering tone.

Qianlong didn’t need to turn around to know who it was. The corners of his mouth lifted involuntarily. He turned his head and, sure enough, saw Jiang Rao riding over to join him. She was wearing a red riding outfit today, her hair neatly combed, with a swaying butterfly hairpin tucked into her temple.

“What is it?” Qianlong’s tone carried a indulgence he hadn’t even noticed himself.

Jiang Rao pouted so hard one could hang an oil bottle from it: “Your Majesty promised to teach this concubine how to shoot! Yesterday I only pulled the bow three times, and I didn’t even get to touch an arrow!”

She had transmigrated here three years ago and had long since figured out this Emperor’s temper—the more you acted spoiled and unreasonable with him, the more he found you innocent and cute. Sure enough, Qianlong laughed and reached out to pinch her cheek: “Didn’t I tell you? Women have less strength; you can’t pull a heavy bow.”

“I can pull it!” Jiang Rao slapped his hand away—though she didn’t dare use any real force, just putting on a show. “Your Majesty is just looking down on me! Today, I must shoot a deer to show you!”

With that, she kicked her horse’s flanks, and the white steed bolted forward.

“Rao’er!” Qianlong’s expression changed slightly, and he hurriedly spurred his horse to chase after her. “Come back! It’s dangerous in the woods!”

Jiang Rao looked back and made a face at him, her red figure particularly eye-catching under the autumn sun. She didn’t care about the danger; she had been stifled in the Forbidden City for three years, and now that she was finally out to frolic, how could she possibly listen obediently?

She wasn’t running fast—the original owner’s horsemanship was average, and while she had learned a bit after transmigrating, it was limited to just “knowing how to ride.” Mostly, she was just putting on a show, waiting for Qianlong to chase her. Sure enough, it wasn’t long before she heard the sound of hooves approaching behind her.

“If Your Majesty can catch up to me, I’ll listen to you!” she shouted with a laugh, her voice scattering in the wind.

Qianlong was both annoyed and amused. He turned back and ordered Wu Shulai: “Have people follow and protect her well!”

“Yes, sir!” Wu Shulai replied with a bitter face. If this Concubine Chen really started making a scene, who could stop her?

The sound of hooves approached like a sudden downpour.

“Rao’er! Stop!”

When Qianlong’s shout came, Jiang Rao had just reined in her horse at the edge of the woods. She had actually slowed down long ago, calculating how to act spoiled and ask for a reward once Qianlong caught up, when she saw the scene in the clearing ahead—

Jiang Rao frowned and slowly approached on horseback. As soon as she dismounted, she heard Qianlong ask the unconscious girl in a trembling voice: “You… is your mother named Xia Yuhe?”

“……”

Jiang Rao’s foot slipped, and she nearly fell.

What?!

Xia Yuhe?! That Xia Yuhe from the banks of Daming Lake?!

She whipped her head around, staring fixedly at the girl’s face on the ground—it was dirty, but her features were indeed delicate. She looked at the painting; although she couldn’t see the details, she could roughly tell it was lotus flowers. The fan… there seemed to be a poem inscribed on the fan…

A “boom” went off in Jiang Rao’s brain.

Holy crap!

Holy, holy, holy crap!!!

Xia Yuhe! A fan! A painting! An injured girl! An arrow shot by the Fifth Prince!

Isn’t this *My Fair Princess*?!!

She had transmigrated for three years and always thought she had just arrived in the ordinary Qing Dynasty during the Qianlong era! Although she knew her name was Jiang Rao and she was a pampered Concubine Chen, she hadn’t thought about it in that direction at all! Which proper Qing harem would have a “Concubine Chen”? Did Qianlong have a Concubine Chen in history? No! She had thought it was the butterfly effect caused by her own transmigration!

And now they were telling her this was the world of *My Fair Princess*?! Would there be a Ziwei entering the palace later? A dancing Fragrant Concubine? Xiao Yanzi causing trouble? A group of people falling in love in such a dramatic way?!

Jiang Rao stood where she was, feeling like her whole world was falling apart.

“Rao’er?” Qianlong turned back, saw her pale face, and thought she was frightened, so he reached out to pull her. “What’s wrong? You look so pale.”

Jiang Rao came to her senses and stiffly forced a smile: “No… nothing. This concubine just… just thinks this girl is quite pitiful.”

Inside, she was screaming wildly: This is Xiao Yanzi! This is the female lead! This is the *Huan Zhu Ge Ge* who will turn the palace upside down in the future! What should I do now? Hug her thigh? Stay away from her? Pretend I don’t know?

Qianlong patted her hand: “She is pitiful. I must take her back to the palace for treatment.”

“Where does Your Majesty plan to place her?” Wu Shulai asked cautiously.

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao: “Yongshou Palace is spacious, how about…”

“No!” Jiang Rao blurted out.

Everyone looked at her in unison.

Jiang Rao’s heart skipped a beat. She quickly squeezed out a spoiled, willful expression and stomped her foot: “Your Majesty! This concubine is someone who needs to be taken care of herself; how would I know how to look after an injured person? If I don’t take care of her well and something happens to this girl, wouldn’t I be held responsible? I won’t do it!”

She grabbed Qianlong’s arm and started acting like a brat: “Your Majesty, you can’t do this, stuffing everything into Yongshou Palace. Isn’t Yanxi Palace quite good? Concubine Ling is meticulous and knows how to take care of people; putting her there is the most appropriate!”

Just kidding! She had read the plot! Once Xiao Yanzi entered the palace, she was a troublemaker who caused explosions wherever she went. She didn’t want to keep this ticking time bomb in her own palace! Let Concubine Ling deal with it; in the original story, Concubine Ling took her in anyway.

Qianlong was shaken by her until he had no choice, both annoyed and amused: “You’re the clever one! Fine, fine, fine, as you wish. Wu Shulai, send her to Yanxi Palace and have Concubine Ling take good care of her.”

“Yes, sir!”

Jiang Rao breathed a sigh of relief, and only then did she have the heart to carefully examine Xiao Yanzi. Hmm… she did look quite lively, though her face covered in blood was a bit scary right now. The arrow in her shoulder was still bleeding; it looked painful.

Yongqi was still kneeling, his face pale. Jiang Rao glanced at him and thought: Young man, you are currently shooting your future wife, do you know that?

On the way back to the capital, Qianlong held Jiang Rao on his horse. Jiang Rao leaned in his arms, her head still buzzing.

She had transmigrated into *My Fair Princess*.

She was now Concubine Chen, a character who didn’t exist in the original work.

Qianlong pampered her greatly, to the point of near-indulgence.

Concubine Ling probably already disliked her.

Xiao Yanzi had entered the palace.

Ziwei should still be waiting outside.

Later, there would be Han Xiang, Saiya, the Empress Dowager returning to the palace, the real and fake princesses…

Jiang Rao took a deep breath and suddenly felt that the future was very “bright”—the kind of bright that was chaotic and dramatic.

“What are you thinking about?” Qianlong asked, looking down.

Jiang Rao came back to her senses and immediately entered her role. She pouted: “Your Majesty, you promised to teach me archery, you can’t go back on your word!”

“Still thinking about archery?” Qianlong laughed. “Weren’t you scared enough today?”

“That’s not the same!” Jiang Rao said righteously. “I want to shoot a deer, not a person! Your Majesty must compensate me; teach me every day after we return to the palace, until I learn!”

“Teach you every day?” Qianlong raised an eyebrow. “Where would I find the time?”

“I don’t care!” Jiang Rao started acting like a rascal. “What Your Majesty promised must be done! Otherwise… otherwise I won’t talk to you anymore!”

This threat had no force, but she acted it out seriously, her eyes wide and her cheeks puffed out.

Qianlong fell for it, as expected, and said repeatedly: “Fine, fine, fine, I’ll teach you, every day. Whatever my Rao’er wants to learn, I will teach.”

Only then was Jiang Rao satisfied, leaning back into his arms. But in her heart, she began to calculate rapidly:

First, stay away from Xiao Yanzi, at least in the beginning. Let her mess around with Concubine Ling and the Empress.

Second, maintain the spoiled, willful persona. Qianlong loved this, so she couldn’t break character.

Third, observe secretly and push things along when necessary—she knew the plot by heart anyway.

Fourth, most importantly, never let Qianlong know that she knows the plot. Play dumb, she must play dumb.

When the imperial procession returned to the Forbidden City, it was already late. Xiao Yanzi was sent to Yanxi Palace. Jiang Rao didn’t know what expression Concubine Ling had when she received the order, but she could guess.

In Yongshou Palace, Suxin helped her change her clothes and asked in a low voice: “Your Ladyship, that girl’s background is unknown; why did you push her to Yanxi Palace? If it turns out to be an opportunity…”

“An opportunity?” Jiang Rao sneered. “That’s trouble. A massive amount of trouble.”

Suxin looked at her, puzzled.

Jiang Rao waved her hand, not explaining. She changed into her sleeping robes and lounged on the daybed eating grapes, her mind still running through the plot.

According to the original story, after Xiao Yanzi’s wounds healed, Qianlong would recognize her as the *Huan Zhu Ge Ge*. Then would come learning the rules, making a fool of herself, meeting Ziwei, the exposure of the real and fake princesses…

And she, Jiang Rao, a character who did not exist in the original story, how was she to survive in this narrative, and perhaps even thrive?

"Your Ladyship, will the Emperor be coming tonight?" Suxin asked.

"He will," Jiang Rao spat out a grape seed. "He definitely will."

Sure enough, just past the hour of the Dog (7:00 PM), word came from the Hall of Mental Cultivation: The Emperor was heading to the Hall of Eternal Longevity.

Jiang Rao immediately lay back down on the bed and closed her eyes, feigning sleep.

Footsteps approached from afar and stopped before the bed. She could feel Qianlong watching her; he watched for a long time.

Then, a hand gently stroked her face.

"Were you truly frightened today?" Qianlong asked in a low voice.

Jiang Rao opened her eyes "drowsily" and rubbed them. "Your Majesty... you’ve come?"

"Mm." Qianlong sat on the edge of the bed. "Did you have a nightmare?"

"I dreamt of an arrow..." Jiang Rao snuggled into his arms, her voice soft. "It came flying with a 'whoosh,' it scared me to death."

Qianlong held her tighter, resting his chin on the top of her head. "Don't be afraid, I am here."

Jiang Rao rolled her eyes in his arms.

"Don't be afraid," indeed. Her mind was currently filled with all the messy events to come.

But she still replied softly, "Mm... with you here, Your Majesty, I am not afraid."

Qianlong chuckled and kissed her forehead.

Jiang Rao kept her eyes closed, but in her heart, she thought: Xia Yuhe of Daming Lake... you truly have birthed a fine daughter.

This imperial palace is about to become lively.

And she, this "Consort Chen" who had intruded by accident, had to think carefully about how to play her role well in this grand drama.

Wilful and arrogant? That was a must.

Clever? She had to be a little bit of that, too.

Most importantly, she had to stay alive, and live well.

Jiang Rao adjusted to a comfortable position in Qianlong's arms and fell asleep.

In her dream, she saw Little Swallow (Xiao Yanzi) leaping over walls in the Imperial Garden, with a group of eunuchs and palace maids chasing after her.

Quite a racket, she thought.

But, it also seemed rather interesting.

chapters.title: Your Majesty, Your Filter Is Too Thick
chapters.content:
Little Swallow had been unconscious for two days.

During these two days, the Palace of Prolonged Happiness was brightly lit, imperial physicians took turns on duty, and Consort Ling personally watched over the decocting of medicine in the side hall. The news flew through the six palaces as if it had wings—the Emperor had brought back a seriously injured girl from the hunting grounds and placed her in the Palace of Prolonged Happiness, and the Emperor made it a point to visit her first thing every day after court.

In the Hall of Eternal Longevity, Jiang Rao was propping up her feet and eating candied fruit.

"Your Ladyship, aren't you going to take a look?" Suxin asked while pounding her legs.

"Look at what?" Jiang Rao spat out a date pit. "Look at someone who is unconscious? How boring."

In truth, she knew exactly what was going on. Little Swallow's injuries looked severe, but she wouldn't die. In the original story, she held on until she acknowledged her father before her "condition worsened," and then she recovered for quite a while. If she went to join the excitement now and was grabbed by Qianlong to help with the care, wouldn't that be asking for trouble?

"But the Emperor has been going to the Palace of Prolonged Happiness every day..." Suxin whispered. "Yesterday, he rewarded Consort Ling with a bushel of Eastern pearls, saying she had worked hard in her care."

Jiang Rao’s hand paused, and then she laughed out loud. "A bushel of Eastern pearls? The Emperor is certainly generous."

She counted on her fingers: Little Swallow would likely wake up today or tomorrow, then acknowledge her father, be granted the title of Gege, and rewards would flow into the Palace of Prolonged Happiness like water... Consort Ling had hit the jackpot this time.

But it didn't matter. Jiang Rao stretched; she wasn't lacking those few rewards. The things Qianlong had bestowed upon her over the past three years were enough to open a jewelry shop.

"Suxin, go find that bolt of cloud brocade that was offered as tribute from Jiangnan the other day." Jiang Rao suddenly sat up straight.

"Is Your Ladyship making new clothes?"

"No." Jiang Rao smiled slyly. "A gift."

She had to prepare a congratulatory gift in advance. With the "Huan Zhu Gege" (Princess Pearl) appearing out of thin air, all six palaces had to show some gesture. As the "most favored Consort Chen," her gift couldn't be too light, but it couldn't be too heavy either—too heavy would look like sycophancy, and too light would give people something to gossip about.

The cloud brocade was just right—precious, yet not overly flashy.

Just as she finished giving the order, a young eunuch came scrambling in: "Your Ladyship! The Palace of Prolonged Happiness... the girl in the Palace of Prolonged Happiness has woken up!"

Jiang Rao raised an eyebrow.

Oh? She’s awake?

Palace of Prolonged Happiness, side hall.

When Little Swallow opened her eyes, her brain was still a fog.

Her shoulder hurt terribly, as if it were being burned by fire. Drowsily, she saw that the canopy above her was embroidered with intertwined lotus flowers; the material was slippery and felt better than any quilt she had ever covered herself with. The room was spacious and bright, and the air held a faint scent of medicine, and also... an indescribable fragrance, sweet and delicate.

"I..." As she spoke, her throat felt incredibly hoarse.

"The young lady is awake?" A gentle female voice came.

Little Swallow turned her head and saw a woman dressed in Manchu attire sitting by the bed. The woman was about twenty-seven or twenty-eight, with gentle features and pearl flowers in her hair, looking at her with a smile.

"Are you..."

The, the palace?

...

...

...

Qianlong laughed heartily and turned to order: "Wu Shulai! Pass on my decree: rewards for everyone in the palace! Consort Ling has done well in her care; reward her with a pair of jade ruyi and twenty bolts of silk! Reward the entire Imperial Hospital with three months' salary!"

"Yes, sir!"

Little Swallow clutched her bundle, her mind still a blur.

She... she had just become the Emperor's daughter?

What about Ziwei?

Hall of Eternal Longevity.

Jiang Rao was trying on a new dress when Suxin hurried in, lowering her voice: "Your Ladyship, the news is confirmed—the Emperor has acknowledged that girl as his daughter and is going to grant her the title of Gege!"

"Oh?" Jiang Rao spun around in front of the mirror. "What title?"

"I heard it is... Huan Zhu Gege."

Jiang Rao’s hand paused, and then she laughed out loud.

Huan Zhu Gege. It really hadn't changed at all.

"What is the reaction from the other palaces?" she asked nonchalantly.

"The Empress broke a teacup, saying that a wild girl of unknown origin is not fit to be a Gege. Consort Ling is naturally happy; the Emperor has rewarded her with many things. The other consorts... are all preparing congratulatory gifts."

Jiang Rao walked to the window and reached out to pluck a chrysanthemum that was in full bloom.

"The show has begun." She twirled the petals, smiling with her eyes curved.

A fake Gege has entered the palace, while the real one is still outside.

What comes next? Little Swallow making a fool of herself while learning etiquette? Ziwei entering the palace as a maid? The Fifth Prince and Little Swallow developing feelings for each other?

Jiang Rao tucked the chrysanthemum into her hair and looked at herself in the mirror.

Mm, lovely.

"Suxin, wrap up the cloud brocade and add a pair of jade bracelets," she ordered. "Send them to the Palace of Prolonged Happiness first thing tomorrow to congratulate Huan Zhu Gege."

"Is Your Ladyship going in person?"

"No." Jiang Rao lazily lay back on the couch. "Sending the gift is enough; there is no need for me to go. Just say... I am feeling unwell and am afraid of passing my illness to the Gege."

She wasn't going to join that commotion. The Palace of Prolonged Happiness must be packed with people trying to curry favor right now, and Consort Ling was riding high. If she went, she would only be making herself unhappy.

Better to lie down in the Hall of Eternal Longevity and wait to watch the show.

In the evening, Qianlong arrived.

He wore a smile, and there was a light in his eyes; it was clear he was in an excellent mood.

"Rao'er, do you know? I have found Yuhe's daughter!" He grabbed Jiang Rao's hand as soon as he entered. "That child, her name is Little Swallow, and her personality is so lively, just like her mother when she was young..."

Jiang Rao rolled her eyes internally.

Like Xia Yuhe? Does Little Swallow have even a shred of resemblance to Xia Yuhe? Your Majesty, your filter is way too thick.

But she showed just the right amount of surprise on her face: "Really? That is truly wonderful news! Congratulations, Your Majesty!"

Qianlong sighed with emotion: "I have failed Yuhe, but now that I can compensate her daughter, I feel a little better."

Jiang Rao nodded obediently, though she thought to herself: You are compensating the wrong person, Your Majesty.

"I have titled her Huan Zhu Gege, and she will live in the Palace of Prolonged Happiness from now on," Qianlong continued. "That child is used to being wild and knows nothing of etiquette. Consort Ling says she will teach her personally, and I think that is excellent."

Jiang Rao blinked: "Your Majesty, that Gege... does she look like Xia Yuhe?"

Qianlong thought for a moment and smiled: "Her brows and eyes are somewhat similar, but their personalities are completely different. Yuhe was gentle and quiet, while Little Swallow is lively and spirited, like a real little swallow."

That’s because she isn't Xia Yuhe's daughter at all, Your Majesty!

Jiang Rao roared internally, but remained gentle on the surface: "Lively is good; the palace is just lacking such a lively person."

Qianlong hugged her: "Rao'er is still the most sensible."

Jiang Rao leaned into his arms, her fingers unconsciously playing with the buttons on his robe.

What would happen next?

Little Swallow learning etiquette, causing chaos.

Ziwei finding a way to enter the palace.

The Fifth Prince growing more fond of this "little sister."

Consort Ling relying on Huan Zhu Gege to consolidate her position.

The Empress fuming with rage.

And she, Jiang Rao...

"Your Majesty." She suddenly looked up, her eyes sparkling. "You promised to teach me archery; when will we start?"

Qianlong was taken aback, then laughed: "You’re still thinking about that?"

"Of course I am!" Jiang Rao sat up straight. "You’ve already acknowledged a daughter, you can't forget what you promised me! Let's start tomorrow, shall we?"

"Tomorrow I have to discuss important matters with Fuheng..."

"Then the day after!" Jiang Rao was persistent. "The day after, for sure!"

Qianlong, unable to resist her pestering, had to nod: "Alright, alright, the day after. I will definitely teach you the day after."

Only then was Jiang Rao satisfied, leaning back into his arms.

Archery or whatever, it didn't really matter to her.

She just wanted Qianlong to know—even with a new daughter, she, Jiang Rao, was still the Consort Chen who needed his attention and his affection.

In this deep palace, favor is like flowing water; it is in the east today, and might be in the west tomorrow.

She had to hold on tight.

The night grew deep, and Qianlong rested in the Hall of Eternal Longevity.

Jiang Rao lay beside him, listening to his steady breathing, but she couldn't sleep.

She rose gently and draped a robe over herself, walking to the window.

The moonlight was like water, spilling into the courtyard. The distant Palace of Prolonged Happiness was still lit, and faint laughter could be heard—it was probably Little Swallow, who had woken up and was talking to Consort Ling.

Jiang Rao looked at the lights and suddenly felt it was a bit funny.

She, a transmigrator, had become Qianlong's favorite consort.

Now a fake Gege had arrived, and soon the real one would enter the palace too.

This imperial palace was becoming more and more like a stage.

Interesting.

Truly intere Chapter 3: This is Huan Zhu Gege?

Hall of Eternal Longevity.

Jiang Rao had just woken up and was sitting before the mirror, letting Suxin comb her hair. A young eunuch entered holding a gift list: "Your Ladyship, these are the gift lists from the various palaces for Huan Zhu Gege. Please take a look."

Jiang Rao scanned them lazily.

The Empress had sent a pair of gold-inlaid jade ruyi and a set of pure gold head ornaments. Noble Consort Chun had sent two bolts of brocade and a pair of jade earrings. Concubine Qing had sent a box of southern pearls...

"What shall we send?" Suxin asked.

Jiang Rao took a pair of jade bracelets from her vanity box—the luster was excellent, a deep, watery green, though not the most extravagant. She then pointed to some cloud-patterned brocade that had been prepared earlier: "Just these two items. They follow protocol and do not overstep."

Suxin hesitated. "Your Ladyship, would that be too modest? I heard Consort Ling sent a full set of ruby head ornaments, and as for the Empress..."

"They send what they wish, and I send what I wish." Jiang Rao pinned a kingfisher-feather hair accessory into her hair while looking in the mirror. "With my rank as a consort, if I send something too lavish, others will say I am currying favor with the new Gege. If I send something too meager, they will say I look down on her. This is just right; no one can find fault with it."

She paused, then added, "And add a copy of *Admonitions for Women*."

Suxin: "..."

"What?" Jiang Rao raised an eyebrow. "The Gege has just entered the palace and doesn't know the rules. Isn't it fitting to send her a copy of *Admonitions for Women* so she can study?"

Suxin’s mouth twitched, and she went off to prepare it in silence.

Sure enough, when the gift arrived at Yanxi Palace, Consort Ling’s smile faded slightly as she looked at the brand-new copy of *Admonitions for Women*.

"Consort Chen is very thoughtful," she said softly. "The Gege truly should study the rules well."

Lamai muttered under her breath, "Isn't this clearly trying to belittle someone..."

And so, that afternoon, Xiaoyanzi, accompanied by Mingyue and Caixia, began her tour of paying respects to the six palaces.

The first stop was naturally the Empress’s Kunning Palace.

Xiaoyanzi knelt on the ground to kowtow, her movements clumsy, causing the pearl flowers in her hair to tilt askew. The Empress sat in the seat of honor, watching her with cold eyes. After a long while, she said indifferently, "Rise. Since the Emperor has acknowledged you, you are now a branch of gold and a leaf of jade. Your words and actions must reflect the dignity of a Gege. Do not bring those crude, common habits into the palace."

Xiaoyanzi was unconvinced in her heart, but she replied, "Yes, Your Majesty."

Once out of Kunning Palace, she let out a long sigh of relief. "That Empress is so fierce."

Caixia whispered a reminder, "Gege, you mustn't say such things carelessly."

Next, they visited Noble Consort Chun and Concubine Qing, both of whom were polite and went through the motions. Xiaoyanzi gradually relaxed, feeling that these consorts were not as terrifying as she had thought.

Until—

Yongshou Palace.

As soon as Xiaoyanzi entered the courtyard, she was stunned.

The courtyard of Yongshou Palace was different from the others. Instead of the opulent peonies and peonies, it was planted with a grove of green bamboo, with climbing roses on the walls—a few flowers were still blooming in this season. Birdcages hung under the veranda, with thrushes and parrots chirping inside. The air held a faint scent of sandalwood mixed with a hint of fruit.

A palace maid came out to greet them: "Gege, please wait a moment. Her Ladyship has just risen and is dressing."

Xiaoyanzi looked around curiously. She had heard that this Consort Chen was the Emperor’s favorite, favored to the point that the entire palace looked on with jealousy. In her imagination, she should have been a seductive woman draped in gold and silver.

Just as she was thinking this, the palace doors opened.

Jiang Rao wore a light green qipao, covered by a moon-white vest, looking so simple and elegant that she didn't look like a favored consort at all. She walked out slowly, sat down on a rattan chair under the veranda, and only then raised her eyes to look at Xiaoyanzi.

The two locked eyes.

Xiaoyanzi was dumbfounded.

She had never seen anyone so beautiful. It wasn't a heavy, gaudy beauty, but something cool and aloof, like pear blossoms under moonlight. Yet, those eyes were lively; as they shifted, there was an indescribable charm—a bit coquettish, a bit proud, and perhaps... a bit playful?

"So this is the Huanzhu Gege?" Jiang Rao spoke, her voice also cool and clear, like jade beads falling into a porcelain plate.

Mingyue gave Xiaoyanzi a gentle nudge.

Xiaoyanzi snapped out of it and hurriedly bowed. "Greetings to Consort Chen."

Her movements were still clumsy, but better than they had been at Kunning Palace.

Jiang Rao did not tell her to rise immediately; instead, she picked up the teacup at her side, blew on it gently, and took a sip.

Xiaoyanzi knelt on the ground, her heart beginning to drum. This Consort Chen... did not seem easy to deal with.

"Rise," Jiang Rao said after a long while, setting down her teacup. "Bring a seat."

Xiaoyanzi stood up and sat on a nearby embroidered stool, her eyes unable to stop glancing at Jiang Rao’s face.

Jiang Rao said nothing, continuing to drink her tea.

The atmosphere was a bit awkward.

Xiaoyanzi couldn't hold it in and blurted out, "Are you the Consort Chen that the Imperial Father favors the most?"

As soon as the words left her mouth, the expressions of Mingyue and Caixia changed. Suxin also frowned.

The entire courtyard fell silent.

Jiang Rao raised her eyes and looked at Xiaoyanzi.

Xiaoyanzi regretted it the moment she said it, but the words were out and couldn't be taken back. She braced herself and added, "You... you really are beautiful."

Jiang Rao suddenly laughed.

It wasn't a gentle, reserved laugh, nor a mocking one; it was light and airy. With a curve of her lips and a slight lift of her eyes, her whole face became vivid.

"The Gege is a straightforward person," she said, her voice filled with amusement. "No wonder the Emperor likes you."

Xiaoyanzi was stunned and laughed along. "I speak bluntly, please don't mind, Your Ladyship."

"I don't mind," Jiang Rao said, setting down her teacup. "I like straightforward people. All the twists and turns are just exhausting."

She beckoned, and Suxin brought over a brocade box.

"This is my gift for our first meeting," Jiang Rao said. "It’s nothing expensive, but it is elegant. You have just entered the palace, so take your time learning to use them."

Xiaoyanzi opened the box to find a set of the Four Treasures of the Study—Hu brushes, Hui ink, Xuan paper, and a Duan inkstone, all of top quality. Beside them lay a copy of *Admonitions for Women*.

"This..." Xiaoyanzi looked at the book, her expression stiffening.

"Don't misunderstand, Gege," Jiang Rao said calmly. "There are many rules in the palace. I studied them too when I first arrived. This book is just for you to look at for fun; you don't have to take it to heart. If you truly want to learn the rules, you must have Consort Ling teach you personally."

Xiaoyanzi breathed a sigh of relief, yet felt something was strange about the remark.

"Very well," Jiang Rao stood up. "I am tired, Gege, please return. When you have time, come by and sit often."

This was a dismissal.

Xiaoyanzi left Yongshou Palace in a daze. Only after walking a long distance did she ask Mingyue, "This Consort Chen... what exactly did she mean?"

Mingyue said cautiously, "Her Ladyship gave a gift and spoke polite words; she must... like you, Gege?"

"Like me?" Xiaoyanzi frowned. "Why did I feel like there was more to her words?"

Caixia whispered, "Gege, Consort Chen is famous for her proud temperament. She was actually very polite to you today. In the future... it is better to keep your distance."

Xiaoyanzi said "Oh," but in her heart, she felt a surge of curiosity about the cool and aloof Consort Chen.

Inside Yongshou Palace.

Suxin tidied the tea set and said, "Your Ladyship, why did you say those things to the Gege? What if it reaches the Emperor's ears..."

"And if it does?" Jiang Rao leaned back in the rattan chair, eyes closed. "Which word did I say wrong? Was it wrong to praise her for being straightforward? Was it wrong to give a gift? Was it wrong to ask her to visit often?"

"But that copy of *Admonitions for Women*..."

"Didn't Consort Ling send one too?" Jiang Rao opened her eyes and smiled. "If she can send it, why can't I?"

Suxin was speechless.

Jiang Rao closed her eyes again.

She had met Xiaoyanzi today and confirmed three things:

First, this girl was indeed reckless, but her recklessness was endearing.

Second, she was curious about "Consort Chen," but held no hostility—at least, not yet.

Third, Consort Ling had already begun to poison the well against her. That remark about "Consort Chen's proud temperament"—wasn't that exactly what Caixia had said? And Caixia was the one Consort Ling had assigned to Xiaoyanzi.

In the evening, the Qianlong Emperor came to Yongshou Palace.

As soon as he entered, he laughed. "I heard Xiaoyanzi went to pay her respects to you today?"

Jiang Rao was embroidering a pouch and did not look up. "Yes. The Gege has a lively personality; she is quite likable."

Qianlong sat beside her and picked up the pouch. "What are you embroidering?"

"A golden dragon," Jiang Rao said. "For the Emperor, a birthday gift."

Qianlong felt a warmth in his heart. "It’s still two months away; why prepare so early?"

"I want to finish it early so I don't have to rush and ruin it." Jiang Rao looked up at him. "Is the Emperor in a good mood today?"

"That child Xiaoyanzi went to pay respects to all the palaces today, and she learned the rules quite well," Qianlong said with a smile. "I was worried she wouldn't adapt to the palace, but it seems I was overthinking it."

Jiang Rao chuckled inwardly.

Learned them well? That was because he hadn't seen her pearl flowers tilting askew at Kunning Palace.

But she said aloud, "Consort Ling taught her well."

Qianlong nodded. "Consort Ling is indeed very attentive."

Jiang Rao lowered her head to continue embroidering, her stitches fine and dense.

"By the way," Qianlong said suddenly, "The Empress Dowager will be returning to the palace in a few days. Prepare yourself; you will accompany me to welcome her."

Jiang Rao’s hand paused. "The Empress Dowager... is returning?"

"Yes." Qianlong didn't notice her reaction. "The Empress Dowager has been worshiping Buddha at Mount Wutai for three years; it is time for her to return. She values rules above all else, so you..."

"I know," Jiang Rao interrupted, looking up with a coquettish smile. "I will certainly be on my best behavior and not bring shame to the Emperor."

Qianlong looked at her and suddenly sighed, reaching out to stroke her face. "Rao'er, these past few days... I have neglected you."

Jiang Rao’s eyelashes trembled.

"What is the Emperor saying?" She leaned into his arms. "The Emperor reclaiming his daughter is a joyous occasion. I am happy for the Emperor as well."

Qianlong held her tighter and said nothing.

In his arms, Jiang Rao’s lips slowly curved upward.

Neglected?

This is only the beginning.

When Ziwei enters the palace, when Hanxiang enters the palace, there will be plenty of time for you to neglect me.

The night grew deep, and the lights in Yongshou Palace were extinguished.

In Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi stared blankly at a room full of treasures. She picked up the Four Treasures of the Study that Consort Chen had sent, touched the delicate Xuan paper, and opened the copy of *Admonitions for Women*.

"Gege, it is time to rest," Mingyue reminded her softly.

Xiaoyanzi said "Mm," then suddenly asked, "Mingyue, what kind of person do you think... Consort Chen is?"

Mingyue thought for a moment. "Consort Chen... is very beautiful and very favored. Her temperament... is a bit proud, but she is not a bad person."

"Not bad..." Xiaoyanzi murmured.

She remembered that face she saw today—cool and aloof, yet beautiful when she smiled.

And that sentence—"I like straightforward people."

Xiaoyanzi tossed the *Admonitions for Women* aside.

Forget it! Anyway, she was a Gege now, the Imperial Father was good to her, and Consort Ling was good to her—that was enough!

She threw herself onto the bed, rolled around in the quilt.

Once her injuries healed, she would explore this palace properly!

The lights in the six palaces went out one by one, only Shufang Studio remained lit—Xiaoyanzi was too excited to sleep, busy fussing over her gifts.

Inside the windows of the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao sat at her table, draped in a robe, writing and drawing by the light of the moon.

She was sketching a relationship chart.

Qianlong, the Empress, Consort Ling, Xiaoyanzi, Ziwei (soon to enter the palace), the Fifth Prince, Er'kang...

And herself.

She drew a circle around the name "Jiang Rao" and traced it heavily several times.

chapters.title: Learning Etiquette
chapters.content:
Yongshou Palace.

Suxin returned from outside and recounted the events at the Shufang Studio in full detail.

Jiang Rao was busy pruning a pot of chrysanthemums. Her hands paused at the news: "The Empress certainly knows how to pick her moments."

"Your Ladyship, should we..." Suxin hesitated, leaving her sentence unfinished.

"Should we what?" Jiang Rao snipped off a withered leaf. "That is Consort Ling’s business. Why should I get involved?"

"But the Empress’s words were clearly aimed at Consort Ling. If something were to happen..."

"There are no 'ifs'." Jiang Rao set down her shears. "Consort Ling has been able to stand firm in this palace for so many years; she has her own ways. A trivial matter like this won't stump her."

As she spoke, an announcement came from outside that the Emperor had arrived.

Jiang Rao wiped her hands and went out to greet him. Qianlong walked in looking exhausted, not even having changed out of his court robes.

"What is the matter, Your Majesty?" Jiang Rao stepped forward to remove his court crown. "Are you troubled by state affairs?"

"State affairs are fine, actually." Qianlong sat down, rubbing his temples. "It’s Xiaoyanzi..."

Jiang Rao knew the situation perfectly well, but she feigned ignorance. "What is wrong with the Gege? Hasn't her injury healed yet?"

"The injury is healed, but she has started learning etiquette." Qianlong sighed. "I passed by the Shufang Studio today and heard such a ruckus inside. When I went in, the child was being scolded by two nannies; she couldn't even walk properly anymore."

Jiang Rao personally poured a cup of tea and handed it to him. "Learning etiquette is always like that. When I first entered the palace, didn't I spend three months learning it too?"

"That’s different." Qianlong took the tea. "You were a young lady of a noble house with a good foundation. Xiaoyanzi... sigh, her wild nature is hard to tame."

Jiang Rao sat beside him and gently massaged his temples. "Since Your Majesty has acknowledged her, you must have some patience. She grew up among the common folk until she was eighteen; she has her own world. Now that she has suddenly entered the palace and must learn all these rules and regulations, it would be difficult for anyone."

Qianlong took her hand. "Only you would say such things. The Empress went to the Shufang Studio today, implying in every word that Consort Ling doesn't know how to teach. Consort Ling came back and cried, saying she had failed your trust."

"Sister Ling has done her best." Jiang Rao’s voice was soft. "Your Majesty, don't be too harsh. If you ask me, with the Gege’s temperament, one cannot rush. Take it slowly, and she will eventually learn."

Qianlong turned to look at her, his eyes softening. "Rao'er is the one who understands my heart best."

Jiang Rao lowered her eyes, continuing to massage his forehead. What she was thinking, however, was quite different—this fuss made by the Empress had only drawn Consort Ling and Xiaoyanzi closer together. That was fine; let them huddle together, so they wouldn't come to bother her.

The two talked for a while longer, and Qianlong’s mood improved significantly. He had his evening meal at the Yongshou Palace, eating two full bowls of rice.

After Qianlong had fallen asleep, Jiang Rao quietly rose and walked to the outer room.

"Suxin, go to the Imperial Hospital tomorrow," she whispered. "Tell them I need some high-quality ointment for bruises and swelling. Get several boxes."

"Is Your Ladyship injured?"

"Keep it in reserve," Jiang Rao said. "There will always be a time when it’s needed."

She lay back down on the bed. Qianlong turned in his sleep, his arm draped over her waist.

Jiang Rao did not move.

She was thinking that the part about Xiaoyanzi learning etiquette was full of jokes in the original story. In the end, it seemed that Ziwei had helped out quite a bit in secret after entering the palace.

Ziwei...

That true daughter of Xia Yuhe must be pacing in circles outside the palace right now, mustn't she?

Soon.

Once Xiaoyanzi was firmly established in the palace, it would be time to find a way to bring Ziwei in.

Qianlong’s breathing rose and fell rhythmically beside her ear.

Jiang Rao gently moved his hand away and turned over.

In the Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi lay on her bed while Caixia applied medicine to her knees.

"Hiss—be gentle, be gentle!"

"Please endure it, Gege. This ointment was sent by Consort Ling; it’s very effective, and the bruising will be gone by tomorrow," Caixia said softly.

Xiaoyanzi buried her face in the pillow and muttered, "Caixia, am I particularly stupid? I can't even walk properly..."

"Gege is not stupid." Mingyue was tidying up clothes nearby. "Gege is just not used to it. Take it slowly, and you will learn."

"But the Empress said such things to Consort Ling today..." Xiaoyanzi lifted her head, her eyes red. "It’s all because I dragged her down."

Mingyue and Caixia exchanged glances, saying nothing.

They saw how well Consort Ling treated the Gege, but the Empress’s words... were indeed harsh.

"I must learn well!" Xiaoyanzi suddenly sat up and clenched her fists. "I cannot let Consort Ling lose face! Nor can I let Royal Father be disappointed!"

She spoke with great passion, but the next morning, when Nanny Qin asked her to practice walking again, that spirit had already deflated.

"Gege, today we will learn the greeting ritual," Nanny Sun said. "How to bow to the Emperor, how to bow to the Empress Dowager, and how to bow to the various Consorts—they are all different."

Xiaoyanzi’s head began to ache.

She remembered the snacks sent from the Yongshou Palace yesterday—Jiang Rao had sent them, saying they were newly made osmanthus cakes from the Imperial Kitchen for her to try. They were sweet and melted in her mouth.

That cold and aloof Consort Chen... perhaps she wasn't so hard to get along with after all?

As she was lost in thought, an announcement came from outside: "Consort Chen has arrived—"

Xiaoyanzi was startled and quickly stood up.

Jiang Rao walked in with Suxin. Today she wore a goose-yellow qipao with a pale purple vest over it, and only a single pearl hairpin in her hair; she looked simple yet elegant.

"Greetings to Consort Chen." Xiaoyanzi performed the ritual properly—though her movements were still stiff, they were much better than the previous days.

Jiang Rao nodded and looked at the two nannies. "I was passing by and heard the Gege was learning etiquette, so I came to take a look. Please continue; don't mind me."

Nanny Qin and Nanny Sun bowed. "Yes."

Xiaoyanzi stood ready, waiting for the nannies' instruction.

Nanny Sun began to explain the essentials of the greeting ritual: "Right hand over left, placed at the side of the waist, bend the knees, lower the head, and say 'Greetings to so-and-so.' When rising, be steady, do not sway."

Xiaoyanzi followed along, her movements as stiff as a wooden puppet.

Jiang Rao sat to the side, watching quietly.

After three attempts, Xiaoyanzi was sweating on her forehead. Nanny Sun still shook her head: "Gege, the depth of the knee-bend is wrong. Too deep looks servile, too shallow looks disrespectful. Come, watch this old servant do it once more."

Xiaoyanzi bit her lip, her eyes beginning to redden again.

Jiang Rao set down her teacup and suddenly spoke: "Gege, come here."

Xiaoyanzi was stunned and walked over.

"Extend your hand," Jiang Rao said.

Xiaoyanzi extended her hand. Jiang Rao held her wrist and gently pressed down: "Do you remember this angle?"

She then steadied her waist: "Bend your knees to here, do you feel it?"

Xiaoyanzi nodded blankly.

"Good, now do it once yourself," Jiang Rao said, releasing her.

Xiaoyanzi took a deep breath and performed the ritual according to the sensation she had just felt.

The movement was still not perfect, but it was much better than before.

Nanny Sun’s eyes lit up: "That’s it! That’s the feeling! Gege, remember this strength!"

Xiaoyanzi looked at Jiang Rao in pleasant surprise.

Jiang Rao had already risen: "I have other matters to attend to, so I will leave now. Gege, take your time learning; there is no rush."

With that, she left with Suxin.

She came and went in a hurry, like a gust of wind.

Xiaoyanzi watched her retreating figure, and the sense of grievance in her heart suddenly dissipated.

"Gege, shall we continue?" Nanny Qin asked.

"Continue!" Xiaoyanzi straightened her back. "I don't believe I can't learn this!"

As for Jiang Rao, who had walked out of the Shufang Studio, a faint smile played on her lips.

"Your Ladyship, why did you need to go there in person?" Suxin asked, puzzled.

"I had to show my face," Jiang Rao said. "Otherwise, the Emperor would think I don't care about his daughter."

She glanced back at the Shufang Studio.

Xiaoyanzi, oh Xiaoyanzi, the etiquette you are learning now will all be exposed in front of Ziwei in the future.

But that was a matter for another day.

For now, she had to think about the Empress Dowager’s return to the palace. That old lady was not easy to deal with.

chapters.title: I Am Stupid
chapters.content:
Outside the Yongshou Palace, Qianlong’s imperial carriage had just arrived when he heard a coquettish voice from within:

"The Emperor doesn't keep his word! You said you would teach me archery today, and it’s almost noon!"

Jiang Rao was dressed in a crisp riding outfit today, her hair tied up high, standing at the palace gate with her hands on her hips, looking as if she wouldn't go inside unless he came.

Qianlong laughed as he stepped off the carriage: "Haven't I come? State affairs must be dealt with first."

"Then can you teach me now?" Jiang Rao’s eyes lit up, and she immediately stepped forward to take his arm. "The target is already set up in the West Garden. I’ve even put on my arm guard!"

She raised her wrist, revealing a silver-threaded soft armor guard, which made her wrist look slender and snow-white.

Qianlong’s heart softened, and he pinched her cheek: "I will teach you, I will certainly teach you today. But let’s agree first: if you can't pull the bow, you aren't allowed to cry."

"Who’s going to cry!" Jiang Rao protested. "I haven't been idle these days; I’ve been practicing my arm strength in the courtyard every day!"

As the two were laughing and heading toward the West Garden, they didn't notice a head peeking out from the wall of the Shufang Studio.

West Garden Archery Range.

Jiang Rao was holding the light bow Qianlong had handed her, struggling to pull the string. She had indeed practiced her arm strength for a few days, but once she held the bow, she realized it was far heavier than she had imagined.

"Keep your arm steady." Qianlong stood behind her, one hand supporting her bow-holding arm, the other gripping her hand on the string. "Look at the bullseye, inhale, and release slowly—"

The arrow flew off with a "whoosh," missing by a mile, not even grazing the edge of the target.

Jiang Rao blushed: "This bow is no good, it’s too heavy..."

"It’s your strength that’s too weak." Qianlong chuckled, about to teach her again.

"Your Majesty." Jiang Rao suddenly spoke, her voice soft. "Since the Gege wants to learn, let’s teach her together. I’m quite tired and would like to rest for a moment."

As she spoke, she truly set down the bow, walked to a nearby pavilion, sat down, and picked up a teacup, sipping slowly.

Qianlong breathed a sigh of relief: "Very well. Xiaoyanzi, come over; I will teach you how to hold the bow first."

Xiaoyanzi happily hurried over.

Jiang Rao sat in the pavilion, watching Qianlong teach Xiaoyanzi how to hold the bow, her expression indifferent.

Suxin whispered in her ear: "Your Ladyship, why did you..."

"Let her learn," Jiang Rao sipped her tea. "I want to see what kind of tricks she can come up with."

In the arena, Xiaoyanzi learned extremely quickly. She was naturally agile and had the foundation of climbing trees and using a slingshot; in less than a quarter of an hour, she could steadily draw a bow. Although the arrows she shot were not accurate, they carried considerable force.

"Good!" Qianlong praised. "You child, you actually have some talent."

Xiaoyanzi proudly lifted her chin. "When I was among the common folk, I was very accurate with a slingshot! I could hit a sparrow in a tree every single time!"

"Oh?" Qianlong became interested. "Then let me test you. Do you see those red persimmons on the tree over there? Do you dare to shoot one?"

Xiaoyanzi looked in the direction he pointed. About thirty paces away stood a persimmon tree, with several bright red persimmons hanging from its branches.

"What’s there to be afraid of!" She nocked an arrow, drew the bow, and squinted one eye.

Jiang Rao set down her teacup and sat up slightly straighter.

Xiaoyanzi held her breath and focused, then released her fingers—

The arrow whistled through the air!

"Thwack!"

A persimmon fell at the sound, hitting the ground and splattering red juice everywhere.

"I hit it! I hit it!" Xiaoyanzi jumped up with joy.

Qianlong also clapped and laughed. "Good! You truly have some skill!"

Xiaoyanzi turned to look at the pavilion. "Consort Chen, did you see? I hit it!"

Jiang Rao stood up and walked over slowly, a faint smile on her face. "I saw. The Gege has good skills."

Xiaoyanzi felt even more smug. She handed the bow to Jiang Rao. "Niangniang, why don't you try? Archery is all about quick eyes and fast hands; having strength alone isn't enough—"

Before she could finish, she suddenly realized something, and her voice came to an abrupt halt.

Jiang Rao took the bow without a word, merely stroking the bowstring gently.

Seeing this, Qianlong hurriedly tried to smooth things over. "Rao'er, why don't I teach you again..."

"No need." Jiang Rao raised her eyes and looked at Xiaoyanzi. "The Gege just said that archery requires quick eyes and fast hands. Then I would like to ask: if one were in the hunting grounds and saw prey dash out, should one release an arrow immediately, or should one see clearly what it is before shooting?"

Xiaoyanzi was stunned.

Jiang Rao continued, "I have heard that the injury on the Gege's shoulder was caused by an accidental shooting in the hunting grounds. If the person shooting at that time had taken one more look to see whether it was a person or a deer, perhaps..."

She did not finish, but the implication was clear.

Xiaoyanzi’s face turned pale, and she instinctively covered her shoulder.

Qianlong frowned slightly. "Rao'er, there is no need to bring up the past."

"I was merely speaking my thoughts." Jiang Rao lowered her gaze and handed the bow back to Xiaoyanzi. "Since the Gege enjoys archery, it would be good to practice accuracy in the future. After all, in this palace, if you shoot off-target, it might not just be a persimmon that gets hurt."

Having said this, she bowed to Qianlong. "Your Majesty, I am feeling a bit tired; I will return to my palace to rest."

"Rao'er..." Qianlong wanted to stop her, but Jiang Rao had already turned and walked away.

Suxin hurried to follow.

Xiaoyanzi stood where she was, gripping the bow tighter and tighter. She looked at Qianlong and said aggrievedly, "Imperial Father, is Consort Chen angry with me? I didn't mean to..."

Qianlong sighed and patted her shoulder. "Consort Chen has a straightforward temperament and her words can be unpleasant, but don't take them to heart. She wasn't targeting you."

Although he said this, he felt a sense of irritation in his heart.

Jiang Rao’s words, while directed at Xiaoyanzi, were also a reminder of the incident at the hunting grounds. What made him even more unhappy was: how did a perfectly good archery lesson turn into this?

"Let's stop here for today." Qianlong also lost his interest. "You go back first and get some good rest."

"Imperial Father..." Xiaoyanzi wanted to say something more, but Qianlong had already waved his hand and turned to leave.

She stood in place, watching Qianlong’s retreating figure, then looked at the heavy bow in her hands, feeling both aggrieved and bewildered.

Mingyue stepped forward cautiously. "Gege, shall we head back too?"

Xiaoyanzi bit her lip and suddenly asked, "Mingyue, do you think... Consort Chen hates me?"

"How could that be..." Mingyue said in a low voice, "Consort Chen is just... just a bit cold in temperament."

Xiaoyanzi said "Oh" and looked down at the remains of the persimmon on the ground.

The bright red pulp mixed with juice looked like blood.

She suddenly remembered that arrow in the hunting grounds, and her shoulder began to ache faintly again.

Yongshou Palace.

As soon as Jiang Rao entered, she took off her arm guard and slumped onto the couch.

Suxin brought warm water. "Niangniang, why did you have to say those things just now? The Emperor looked quite displeased."

"He is displeased?" Jiang Rao sneered. "I am not pleased either. A perfectly good time for the two of us, and someone ignorant had to barge in."

"But the Gege is, after all, the daughter the Emperor just recognized..."

"Does being a daughter mean she doesn't have to follow the rules?" Jiang Rao sat up. "If I hadn't said those few words today, who knows how much trouble she would cause in the future. The Emperor dotes on her, and I cannot interfere with that, but she should not get in my way."

In the evening, Qianlong did indeed come to Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao was struggling with a light bow; after pulling it several times, her arms were too sore to lift.

Qianlong walked in and, seeing this, his heart softened by half. "Still practicing?"

"I am clumsy, so I must compensate with diligence." Jiang Rao did not look up.

Qianlong sat beside her and took her hand. "It was my fault today for neglecting you."

Only then did Jiang Rao look up at him, her eyes slightly red. "It is good that Your Majesty knows. I have been looking forward to this for days, finally waiting for Your Majesty to teach me archery, and then..."

She did not continue, but the grievance was all in her eyes.

Qianlong hugged her heart-achingly. "It is my fault. Tomorrow, tomorrow I will definitely teach you properly, without bringing anyone else—just the two of us."

"Really?"

"A monarch never breaks his word."

Only then did Jiang Rao break into a smile through her tears and lean into his embrace.

Qianlong stroked her hair, and the lingering displeasure in his heart dissipated.

However, he did not expect that the next day, outside the West Garden archery range, Xiaoyanzi was already waiting there early.

"Imperial Father! Consort Chen!" She smiled brightly. "I thought about it after I went back yesterday, and Consort Chen was right—archery shouldn't just be about speed; one must practice accuracy! So... can I join you and learn?"

The knuckles of Jiang Rao’s hand gripping the bow turned slightly white.

Qianlong looked at her, then at Xiaoyanzi, momentarily caught in a dilemma.

chapters.title: Consort Ling is Gentler
chapters.content:
Outside the West Garden archery range, the atmosphere turned somewhat stagnant.

Jiang Rao’s knuckles, gripping the bow, turned slightly white, yet she maintained a proper, faint smile on her face, her eyes gazing quietly at Qianlong. Qianlong looked at her, then at Xiaoyanzi, who was looking at him with eager eyes. Just as he was feeling troubled, he suddenly heard the sound of horse hooves approaching from afar.

"Imperial Father!"

"Your Majesty!"

Three figures rode over on horseback—it was the Fifth Prince Yongqi and the Fu brothers. The three dismounted and bowed neatly. Yongqi was dressed in a sapphire-blue riding outfit, with a light sheen of sweat on his forehead, clearly having just finished practicing riding.

"You have come just in time." Qianlong’s eyes lit up, as if he had found a way to resolve the situation. "Xiaoyanzi wants to learn archery, and I was worried about not being able to teach her alone. Yongqi, Erkang, Ertai, the three of you have excellent archery skills; you can teach the Gege on my behalf."

Upon hearing this, Xiaoyanzi immediately forgot her previous discomfort and cheered, "Fifth Prince! Erkang! Ertai! You are going to teach me archery?"

Yongqi was slightly taken aback. He glanced at Jiang Rao, who stood beside Qianlong with a calm expression, and then bowed. "This son obeys the decree."

Fu Erkang and Fu Ertai also hurriedly agreed.

Qianlong nodded with satisfaction and turned to Jiang Rao, saying gently, "Rao'er, let's go. I will focus on teaching you today."

Jiang Rao’s gaze shifted lightly between Xiaoyanzi and Yongqi’s group, the corners of her lips curving into a very shallow arc. "Then I shall trouble the Fifth Prince and the two Fu young masters." With that, she let Qianlong take her hand and walked toward another, quieter archery range.

Seeing Qianlong and Jiang Rao leave together, Xiaoyanzi finally let out a long sigh of relief. She patted her chest and whispered to the three men, "They finally left... that really scared me just now."

"Why does the Gege say that?" Fu Ertai, who had a lively personality, asked curiously.

Xiaoyanzi stepped closer, lowered her voice, and wore a look of lingering fear. "You don't know, Consort Chen is so fierce! I just hit a persimmon, and she started talking about 'accidental injury in the hunting grounds' and 'seeing clearly whether it's a person or a deer.' Isn't that deliberately stabbing me in the heart? And the Imperial Father even protected her!"

Yongqi frowned imperceptibly. Fu Erkang, being more composed, gently advised, "Gege, perhaps Consort Chen was just making a casual remark; it may not have had a deeper meaning."

"How could it not!" Xiaoyanzi pouted. "She is just unhappy that the Imperial Father is teaching me, thinking I’ve stolen the Imperial Father’s attention! Consort Ling is much better—gentle and generous, and she never gives me a cold look. Consort Chen is just too petty, relying on the Imperial Father’s doting."

"Xiaoyanzi," Yongqi spoke up, his tone gentle yet carrying a hint of a warning, "It is not appropriate to speak recklessly about palace matters."

Xiaoyanzi curled her lip but said no more. She simply pulled an arrow from the quiver and nocked it on the bow. "Let's not talk about her; it's boring. Fifth Prince, hurry and teach me! I must practice until I'm even better than her!"

On the other side, at the quiet archery range.

Qianlong was standing behind Jiang Rao, teaching her how to adjust her posture hand-in-hand. Jiang Rao had specifically changed into a softer arm guard today, and as Qianlong held her hands, he could feel her slender, cool fingertips.

"Lower your wrist a bit more... Yes, just like that." Qianlong’s breath brushed against her ear. "Keep your eyes on the bullseye, and keep your heart calm."

Jiang Rao aimed as instructed, and the feathered arrow left the string with a "thwack." Although it did not hit the bullseye, it landed firmly on the target.

"I hit it!" Jiang Rao turned back joyfully, her eyes shining as she looked into Qianlong’s.

Infected by her unreserved joy, Qianlong smiled and pinched the tip of her nose. "You’ve made progress. It seems my Rao'er is also a talent worth molding."

"Of course." Jiang Rao proudly lifted her chin, then tugged on Qianlong’s sleeve and shook it gently. "Your Majesty, will you come to teach me again tomorrow?"

"I will, how could I not." Qianlong pulled her closer. "A monarch never breaks his word."

Only then did Jiang Rao lean into his embrace, satisfied, playing with the tassel of the jade pendant at his waist. She said in a seemingly casual, light tone, "Just now... it was truly for the best that Your Majesty let Xiaoyanzi learn from the Fifth Prince and the others. The Fifth Prince has exquisite archery skills and will surely teach the Gege well. It also saves me from... being an eyesore to the Gege."

Hearing the faint, lingering grievance in her words, Qianlong felt even more pity. He lowered his head and kissed her hair lightly. "Nonsense. How could my Rao'er be an eyesore? It was my lack of consideration; I should have taught you alone from the start."

Jiang Rao said nothing more, only burying her face in his chest, a faint, triumphant smile flitting across her lips.

Yongshou Palace, nightfall had just begun to descend.

When the Qianlong Emperor arrived after finishing his memorials, Jiang Rao was leaning on a daybed by the window, browsing through a chess manual by candlelight. She had loosely pinned up her hair and was dressed in a simple, light-red house robe. Stripped of the spirited air she wore in her riding gear during the day, she appeared exceptionally languid and charming.

"What are you reading so intently?" Qianlong approached and plucked the book from her hands.

"Just flipping through it." Jiang Rao reached to take it back, but Qianlong took the opportunity to grasp her hand and pull her into his arms.

"Your Majesty..." Jiang Rao let out a soft cry as he swept her up horizontally.

"You were tired today; rest early." Qianlong carried her toward the inner chamber, his voice filled with a smile. "How about I finish court early tomorrow and take you to the western suburbs for a ride?"

"Really?" Jiang Rao wrapped her arms around his neck, her eyes shimmering. "Your Majesty must not break your word again."

"I will never break my word."

The palace attendants quietly extinguished the candles, and the bed curtains were lowered. The Yongshou Palace was filled with warmth and an endless sense of spring.

At this very moment, however, the Shufang Studio presented a different scene.

Xiao Yanzi was gesticulating wildly as she spoke: "...You didn't see it, the look on Consort Chen's face! It’s a good thing you, Fifth Prince, and the others arrived, or I wouldn't have known what to do."

Yongqi listened quietly, lifting and setting down his teacup. Fu Ertai chimed in with a few laughs, while Fu Erkang appeared lost in thought.

"If you ask me, Consort Ling is the best," Xiao Yanzi concluded. "She never puts on airs and is so patient with me. Unlike some people who, relying on the Emperor's favor, act as if their eyes are fixed on the top of their heads."

"Xiao Yanzi," Yongqi finally spoke, his tone calm and ripple-free. "Consort Chen has accompanied the Emperor for many years and is deeply loved and respected by the Imperial Father; she naturally has her own exceptional qualities. Some things are better left unsaid; speaking them aloud... might invite trouble."

Xiao Yanzi froze. Looking at Yongqi’s handsome yet distant profile, she muttered an "Oh" and lost her enthusiasm.

After leaving the Shufang Studio, Yongqi walked slowly along the palace path. Fu Ertai had already returned to the Imperial Guard quarters, yawning with fatigue, leaving only Fu Erkang to accompany him.

"Fifth Prince," Fu Erkang hesitated for a moment before saying in a low voice, "The Princess Huanzhu seems to hold a deep prejudice against Consort Chen."

Yongqi gazed at the thin strip of deep blue sky above the palace walls and said faintly, "She has just entered the palace; she doesn't understand the rules, nor does she understand the depths of this place. Consort Chen..." He paused. "To remain in the palace with such enduring favor is certainly not due to beauty alone. If Xiao Yanzi continues to be so unrestrained in her speech, she will suffer for it sooner or later."

"I only hope Consort Ling can offer her more guidance," Fu Erkang finally sighed.

Yongqi did not respond. He thought of the ever-gentle and proper Consort Ling in the Yanxi Palace, and then of the undisguised doting look in the Imperial Father's eyes when he gazed at Consort Chen.

Inside the curtains of the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao unconsciously snuggled closer to Qianlong in her sleep.

Qianlong, softened by her dependent little gesture, pulled her tighter and drifted into a deep sleep.

He did not know that the willful and temperamental young woman in his arms was currently dreaming of bizarre and disjointed images—strange, towering buildings, metal boxes that could run, and a version of herself from another era, holding a book and laughing heartily at a computer screen.

chapters.title: The Startled Bird in the Tree
chapters.content:
The autumn wind grew sharper, and the leaves in the Imperial Garden began to turn yellow.

With nothing to do on a clear afternoon, Jiang Rao took Suxin for a stroll in the garden. She favored the bamboo grove on the east side, which was secluded and quiet, with few visitors. As the mistress and maid passed through the moon gate, they heard a commotion—

"Princess! Please, come down!"

"Be careful!"

"Go get a ladder! Quickly!"

Jiang Rao looked up and saw an apricot-colored figure hanging from the branches of an old locust tree not far away, swaying precariously. Below the tree, eunuchs and palace maids knelt on the ground, their faces ashen. Mingyue and Caixia were stamping their feet in anxiety, their heads tilted back, on the verge of tears.

Who else could it be but Xiao Yanzi?

Suxin whispered, "Your Majesty, it is Princess Huanzhu..."

Jiang Rao paused, watching with interest for a moment. Xiao Yanzi was clutching the trunk with one hand while reaching into a bird's nest with the other, muttering, "Come out... don't run..."

"Princess! We beg you to come down! If you fall, we servants will be unable to atone for it even with our lives!" Caixia cried out with a sob.

Xiao Yanzi ignored her, leaning further out. The branch, already thin and weak, groaned under her weight until it snapped with a crisp "crack"—

"Ah!"

Xiao Yanzi swayed, her feet losing their footing, and she was left dangling in mid-air. She gripped the branch with both hands, but the wood was already splintering and on the verge of breaking.

A collective gasp rose from the crowd below.

Jiang Rao frowned and said to Suxin, "Go, tell them to bring a ladder. The longest one."

"Yes."

Suxin hurried off. Jiang Rao walked slowly to the base of the tree, looking up at Xiao Yanzi, who was hanging in the air with a face pale from fright. Her voice was clear and indifferent: "What is the Princess doing? Raiding a bird's nest?"

Xiao Yanzi looked down and saw it was her; she felt both embarrassed and anxious. "None of your business!"

"It is not my business," Jiang Rao replied calmly. "But if the Princess falls, broken bones are a minor matter, but all these servants in the garden will likely lose their heads. When the Emperor blames everyone, will the Princess be able to live with that?"

Xiao Yanzi bit her lip and said nothing. She hadn't thought that far ahead; she had just seen the nest and felt an itch to climb, and having been cooped up for so many days, she had acted on impulse.

Just then, the eunuchs arrived, panting, carrying a long ladder. Jiang Rao directed them to set it firmly, held one side of the ladder herself, and looked up. "Princess, please come down slowly."

Xiao Yanzi looked at the tall ladder and then at Jiang Rao’s expressionless face below; she felt incredibly awkward. But in the current situation, she dared not be stubborn. She had no choice but to slowly loosen her grip on the branch and tentatively move toward the ladder.

Her legs were already weak from fear, and after the earlier struggle, her foot slipped—

"Careful!"

Jiang Rao was quick-witted; she stepped forward and caught her by the waist. Xiao Yanzi tumbled into her arms, and both stumbled, though Suxin was there to catch them, preventing a fall.

Once they were steady, Jiang Rao immediately let go, stepped back half a pace, and smoothed her sleeves. Her movements were so quick it was as if she had touched something unclean.

Xiao Yanzi’s face turned bright red, whether from fear or anger, it was hard to tell. She stood firm, brushed the dust from her lapels, and stiffened her neck. "I—I could have come down myself!"

"Mm," Jiang Rao responded faintly, her gaze sweeping over the mud-stained cuffs of Xiao Yanzi’s sleeves. "The Princess is of noble blood; it would be best to avoid such dangerous activities in the future. If you were hurt, the Emperor would be heartbroken."

The words were polite, but to Xiao Yanzi, they sounded like sarcasm. Recalling what Jiang Rao had said at the archery range, her temper flared. "Stop acting so hypocritical! If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have..."

She swallowed the rest of her sentence halfway through.

Jiang Rao acted as if she hadn't heard the unfinished remark. She turned to the servants kneeling on the ground and said, "All of you, rise. No one is to speak of today’s events. If I hear even a whisper of gossip..."

She didn't finish, but the coldness in her eyes made everyone shudder.

"We wouldn't dare!"

Only then did Jiang Rao look at Xiao Yanzi, her tone returning to its previous indifference. "The Princess has had a fright; go back and rest early. Mingyue, Caixia, serve her well."

With that, she turned to leave.

"Wait!" Xiao Yanzi suddenly called out.

Jiang Rao stopped and turned her head.

Xiao Yanzi opened her mouth. The word "thank you" rolled around in her throat but never came out. In the end, she could only blurt out, "You... you sure know how to play the good person."

Her tone was still harsh, but beneath the stubbornness in her eyes, something else was clearly hidden.

Jiang Rao looked at her and suddenly smiled softly.

It wasn't the polite, distant smile, but a genuine one, with ripples of light in her eyes. It was as if she had seen something truly amusing.

Xiao Yanzi felt baffled by the smile, and a bit annoyed. "What are you laughing at?"

"Nothing." Jiang Rao suppressed her smile and shook her head. "I just think that the Princess's temperament... is truly rare."

Without another word, she turned and left with Suxin.

Xiao Yanzi stood in place, watching the light green figure drift further and further away until it vanished at the end of the bamboo path. She couldn't quite name the feeling in her heart.

"Princess, shall we go back?" Mingyue stepped forward cautiously.

Xiao Yanzi gave a soft "Mm" and looked up at the bird's nest in the tree. The startled bird had already returned and was standing by the nest, looking around vigilantly.

"Let's go." She brushed the dust off her hands, suddenly feeling that raiding bird's nests wasn't all that interesting after all.

On the way back to Yongshou Palace.

Suxin whispered, "Your Majesty, why did you have to catch her yourself? You could have let the servants do it."

Jiang Rao walked with a light, steady pace, idly twirling a half-bloomed osmanthus branch in her hand. "If I hadn't caught her and she had truly fallen, and the Emperor had blamed everyone, how many heads in this garden would have been enough to pay the price?"

"But Princess Huanzhu doesn't seem to appreciate it..."

"Why would I need her appreciation?" Jiang Rao brought the osmanthus to her nose and inhaled, her lips curling slightly. "It was just amusing to watch."

She truly found it amusing.

The Xiao Yanzi of the original story was a troublemaker who feared nothing. But seeing her in person, she realized that beneath the recklessness, there was something else—like the way she put on a brave front despite being afraid, the way she insisted on being sharp-tongued even after being helped, and the fleeting panic and helplessness in her eyes that she probably hadn't even noticed herself.

Like a small, baring-its-teeth beast that was actually quite soft inside.

"However," Jiang Rao changed the subject, "today's incident reminds me of something else."

"What does Your Majesty mean?"

"The Emperor mentioned yesterday that the Empress Dowager will return to the palace next month." Jiang Rao handed the osmanthus branch to Suxin. "With the Princess's current temperament, she is bound to suffer greatly once she is in front of the Empress Dowager."

Suxin was startled. "Then..."

"It has nothing to do with me," Jiang Rao said indifferently. "Isn't Consort Ling the best at teaching rules? Let her worry about it."

She just suddenly remembered that in the original story, Xiao Yanzi caused quite a stir after the Empress Dowager returned. Now that she was a variable in the equation, she wondered how things would unfold.

Thinking about it, she was actually quite looking forward to it.

In the Shufang Studio, Xiao Yanzi had bathed and changed her clothes, sitting by the window in a daze.

Mingyue brought in hot tea. "Princess, have some tea to calm your nerves."

Xiao Yanzi took it but didn't drink. She stared at the darkening sky outside the window and suddenly asked, "Mingyue, do you think... Consort Chen helped me on purpose today?"

Mingyue thought for a moment and said cautiously, "Consort Chen is kind-hearted. Seeing the Gege in trouble, it is only natural for her to reach out and help."

"But she clearly disliked me before..." Xiaoyanzi muttered.

"Her Ladyship never said she disliked you," Caixia chimed in softly from the side. "I heard that Consort Chen’s temperament is just like that—indifferent to everyone. Even toward the Emperor... she sometimes dares to show a bit of temper."

Xiaoyanzi recalled the day at the archery range, when Jiang Rao dared to give her a cold look right in front of Qianlong. The awkwardness in her heart suddenly dissipated.

That was true. That Consort Chen didn't seem to be particularly polite to anyone. If she dared to throw tantrums even at the Emperor, it seemed... quite normal for her to be cold toward a Gege who had appeared out of nowhere.

"Forget it, forget it. I won't think about it anymore," Xiaoyanzi shook her head. "Anyway, I'll just stay away from her in the future."

Although she said this, the vague, indescribable feeling in her heart had been quietly planted like a seed.

Yangxin Hall.

After Qianlong finished reviewing the last memorial, Wu Shulai stepped forward at the right moment: "Your Majesty, where shall dinner be served?"

"Yongshou Palace." Qianlong replied without hesitation. He paused, then asked, "Is there any fresh news from the harem today?"

Wu Shulai hesitated for a moment.

"Speak."

"Yes... This afternoon, Huanzhu Gege was climbing a tree in the Imperial Garden and almost fell. Fortunately, Consort Chen was passing by; she ordered someone to fetch a ladder and personally helped the Gege down."

Qianlong’s brush paused: "Climbing a tree?"

"Yes... she was raiding a bird's nest."

Qianlong laughed in spite of himself and shook his head: "This child... her wild nature is truly hard to change." After laughing, he asked with concern, "Was she hurt?"

"No. Consort Chen handled it properly, and the Gege was only a little frightened."

"Hmm." Qianlong set down his vermilion brush, a hint of approval in his eyes. "Although Rao'er has a somewhat delicate temperament, she is never confused when it comes to major matters."

He stood up and stretched his limbs: "Let’s go. To Yongshou Palace. I must thank her properly."

The night grew darker.

Yongshou Palace was brightly lit. Hearing that Qianlong was coming, Jiang Rao had specifically instructed the small kitchen to prepare several dishes he enjoyed. At this moment, she was facing the mirror, adjusting her makeup and pinning a newly acquired pearl tassel hairpin to her temple.

The woman in the mirror had features as beautiful as a painting, and in the movement of her eyes, there was a sense of detachment that saw through everything.

She knew that the incident in the Imperial Garden today would soon reach Qianlong's ears. And what she wanted was precisely this impression of being "sensible" and "magnanimous."

In this deep palace, favor is certainly important, but a reputation for "virtue" is sometimes more useful than favor.

Especially since the Empress Dowager was about to return to the palace.

chapters.title: You Are Wrong, Wrong to an Outrageous Degree
chapters.content:
Dinner was laid out in the main hall of Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao personally served dishes to Qianlong, while Suxin waited on them. There were four small plates and six bowls, each exquisite, yet all were the light, refreshing flavors Qianlong usually preferred. A bowl of clear-stewed squab soup was simmered to perfection, the broth clear and fragrant.

"Your Majesty, try this." Jiang Rao ladled a small bowl of soup and handed it over. "It is dry in autumn; this soup is best for moistening the lungs."

Qianlong took it, tasted it, and nodded in praise: "The small kitchen in your palace still has the best skills." He set down his spoon and looked at Jiang Rao, his eyes gentle. "I heard about the incident in the Imperial Garden today. You handled it properly."

Jiang Rao lowered her eyes, her long lashes casting shallow shadows in the candlelight: "Your concubine just happened to be passing by. Huanzhu Gege is young, and it is natural for her to be playful. As long as she is unharmed, that is all that matters."

"Only you would say that." Qianlong sighed. "That child, I always worry that she won't be able to adapt to the rules of the palace."

"Your Majesty is overthinking." Jiang Rao picked up a pair of chopsticks and served him some stir-fried shrimp. "The Gege is clever, and with Consort Ling’s careful guidance, given time, she will surely develop the demeanor of a lady of status."

These words were flawless, praising both Xiaoyanzi and Consort Ling.

Qianlong’s brow smoothed out as expected: "Speaking of which, I was just about to tell you—the Imperial Board of Astronomy has calculated a good day, the eighth. I intend to take Xiaoyanzi to the Imperial Ancestral Temple that day to offer sacrifices to the ancestors and formally announce to the world that she is a Gege of my Aisin Gioro clan."

Jiang Rao’s hand holding the chopsticks paused imperceptibly.

The eighth... the sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple...
