The plot of the original story flashed through her mind—it was during this very sacrifice that Ziwei would see Xiaoyanzi’s glory among the crowd, have an emotional breakdown, and shout, "You are wrong! I am the real Gege," only to be heard by Fu Erkang and taken back to his residence.

The plot was finally reaching this point.

"Rao'er?" Qianlong called out, seeing her lost in thought.

Jiang Rao came back to her senses, a gentle smile blooming on her face: "The eighth... is indeed a good day. Your Majesty is thoughtful; it is time to let the Gege formally acknowledge her ancestors." She paused and added, "However, the rituals for the grand sacrifice are complex. Since it is the Gege’s first time participating, she might be nervous. Your Majesty should be a little more patient."

"I know." Qianlong patted her hand. "Consort Ling will be stepping up her etiquette training these next few days. If you have time, please help guide her as well."

"Your concubine obeys the decree."

After dinner, the servants cleared the dishes and served tea.

Qianlong was in a very good mood tonight, chatting with Jiang Rao about interesting matters at court. Jiang Rao nestled beside him, occasionally responding with a soft smile.

The candlelight flickered, casting a warm glow throughout the hall.

As the night deepened, Qianlong naturally stayed the night at Yongshou Palace.

The red candles warmed the curtains, and the passion flowed like red waves. When the passion moved her, Jiang Rao clung to Qianlong’s shoulders, her eyes filled with coquettish charm. Qianlong loved this side of her dearly.

After the intimacy subsided, Jiang Rao leaned in Qianlong’s arms, listening to his steady breathing, and slowly closed her eyes.

In the blink of an eye, it was the eighth.

The sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple was a major state affair.

Before dawn, the palace was already bustling. Xiaoyanzi rose at the hour of the Tiger (3-5 AM), bathed and dressed, changing into the officially designated Gege ceremonial robes—a stone-blue robe embroidered with a golden phoenix, wearing a seven-pheasant crown, the pearls and gemstones on which shimmered brilliantly in the candlelight.

"Gege, please be very careful today." Mingyue whispered as she straightened her collar. "Consort Ling taught you the sacrificial etiquette yesterday; please don't make any mistakes."

Xiaoyanzi’s palms were sweating from nervousness, but she forced herself to remain calm: "I know."

The imperial procession left the palace, the honor guard strict and solemn.

The streets on both sides had already been cleaned with water and paved with yellow earth. The commoners knelt on both sides, shouting "Long live." Sitting in the carriage, looking at the dense crowd outside through the gauze curtains, her heart beat like a drum.

She did not know that in the crowd, two pairs of eyes were staring fixedly at her carriage.

That night, Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao leaned by the window, looking at the heavy night outside the palace walls. The sacrifice had been over for most of the day, and everything in the palace was as usual, though one could vaguely hear some commotion from the direction of Shufang Studio.

Suxin draped a cloak over her: "Your Ladyship, it is late, you should rest."

"No rush." Jiang Rao said softly. "Today’s sacrifice... it must have been very lively."

The corners of her lips curved slightly, her eyes reflecting the sparse stars outside the window.

What was meant to happen, should have happened.

Ziwei had entered the Fu residence, Erkang had developed feelings, and Xiaoyanzi was likely sitting on pins and needles at Shufang Studio right now.

Jiang Rao turned and walked toward the inner chamber, her skirt sweeping across the clean floor.

These days were truly becoming more and more interesting.

chapters.title: Words of Truth and Falsehood
chapters.content:
Inside the guest room of the Fu residence, the lights were bright.

Ziwei sat on the couch, ointment already applied to her ankle, which was carefully wrapped in white cloth. Jin Suo stood guard nearby, watching Fu Erkang, who sat opposite them, with vigilance.

Fu Erkang’s expression was grave; the scene on the street during the day was too shocking, and he had to treat it with caution. After the maid served tea and withdrew, he finally spoke slowly: "What you said earlier, Miss, is truly shocking. You say you are the daughter of Xia Yuhe, but do you have any proof?"

Ziwei took an old handkerchief from her bosom. After unfolding it, inside was a jade pendant and a neatly folded piece of paper.

"This jade pendant was given to me by my mother before she passed away." She handed the jade pendant to Fu Erkang. "She said this was a token left behind by the Emperor back then."

Fu Erkang took the jade pendant and examined it closely. It was a piece of top-quality mutton-fat white jade, carved with a coiled dragon pattern, and on the back was a small character "Hong"—the very name Qianlong used before ascending the throne.

His heart shook, and he unfolded the paper. The handwriting on the paper was elegant, written as a poem:

The signature was Xia Yuhe, and the date was the seventh year of Qianlong.

"And this." Ziwei took a scroll from her bundle and slowly unfolded it.

Ziwei’s eyes turned red, her voice choked with sobs: "This is a long story..."

She took a deep breath and recounted the cause and effect.

He thought of the Huanzhu Gege who climbed trees and raided bird nests in the Imperial Garden, and shot arrows happily at the archery range. Such a frank and lively personality—if one were to say she was a calculated imposter, it was truly hard to believe.

Perhaps, as Miss Xia said, it was just a misunderstanding caused by a twist of fate?

"Big Brother."

Fu Ertai pushed the door open and, seeing his grave expression, asked: "What’s wrong? That girl on the street today..."

Fu Erkang briefly explained the situation.

After hearing it, Fu Ertai was dumbfounded: "This... how is this possible? Is Huanzhu Gege a fake?"

"Keep your voice down." Fu Erkang signaled him to be quiet. "There is no conclusion to this matter yet. But the token in Miss Xia’s hand is indeed exactly the same as the one Huanzhu Gege presented to the Emperor."

"Then... what should we do?" Fu Ertai was anxious. "If it really is a mistake, this is a massive issue!"

Fu Erkang rubbed his temples: "I intend to enter the palace tomorrow to first probe Huanzhu Gege’s reaction."

"Ask her directly?"

"Naturally, it must be more subtle." Fu Erkang said. "If it really is a misunderstanding, perhaps Huanzhu Gege... is also helpless in this situation."

The two brothers discussed it until late at night, still without a foolproof plan.

And at this moment, at Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi was also unable to sleep all night.

She lay on the bed, her mind filled with the image of Ziwei’s tearful eyes looking at her in the crowd.

Mingyue was keeping watch in the outer room and came in upon hearing her: "Why is the Gege still not asleep?"

Xiaoyanzi sat up, hugging her knees: "I can't sleep. Today on the street, I think I saw Ziwei... she looked at me, that look... I feel so terrible."

Mingyue lit the candle and persuaded her softly: "Gege, don't overthink it. If that Miss Xia is truly an old friend of yours, she would be nothing but happy to see you in such glory."

"But she doesn't know I'm a fake..." Xiaoyanzi covered her mouth as soon as she said it.

She remembered the day she swore sisterhood with Ziwei, when the two of them knelt before the moon in the courtyard, promising to share both blessings and hardships.

But now, she was enjoying this immense wealth, while Ziwei was wandering outside...

"No." Xiaoyanzi suddenly sat up. "I must find a way to see Ziwei."

"Gege!" Mingyue was startled. "That won't do! With your current status, how can you just leave the palace to see someone?"

Xiaoyanzi hesitated.

That night, the Fu residence and the Shufang Studio were both lit with lamps, and both were sleepless.

In the Yongshou Palace, however, Jiang Rao slept soundly.

A smile curled, unconsciously, at the corners of her lips.

chapters.title: A Night Visit to Shufang Studio
chapters.content:
The following afternoon, Fu Erkang found an opportunity to "accidentally" encounter the Fifth Prince, Yongqi, who was just returning from the archery range.

"Fifth Prince." Fu Erkang bowed, his expression grave.

Seeing that his demeanor was unusual, Yongqi dismissed his attendants and asked, "Erkang, is something the matter?"

Fu Erkang lowered his voice: "Let us step aside to talk."

The two walked to a secluded spot, and Fu Erkang recounted everything he had seen on the street the day before, as well as what Xia Ziwei had said at the Fu residence. Finally, he said in a low voice, "Fifth Prince, this matter is of great importance. The token in that young lady's possession is authentic, and her words and manners do not seem feigned. If she is truly the daughter of Xia Yuhe, then the Huanzhu Gege..."

Yongqi’s face changed drastically, and he grabbed Fu Erkang’s arm: "What did you say? Xiao Yanzi is a fake?"

"I dare not make such a judgment," Fu Erkang said cautiously. "But the matter is grave and must be investigated. I believe we should first sound out the Huanzhu Gege."

Yongqi let go of his arm and paced under the veranda, his mind in turmoil.

Xiao Yanzi is a fake?

The Xiao Yanzi who was shot by an arrow at the hunting grounds, who climbed trees in the Imperial Garden, and who shot arrows joyfully at the archery range—is she an impostor?

No, he did not believe it.

But Erkang spoke with such certainty, and those tokens could not be fake...

"Fifth Prince," Fu Erkang said in a low voice, "this matter cannot be delayed. If what that young lady says is true, dragging it out will only lead to endless trouble."

Yongqi took a deep breath: "You are right. This matter... must be cleared up." He paused. "Tonight, you and I will go to Shufang Studio together. Let’s call Ertai as well; the more people, the better the support."

That night, the moon was bright and the stars were sparse.

Inside Shufang Studio, Xiao Yanzi was staring blankly at the candlelight. Earlier that day, Consort Ling had come to test her studies, but she had been absent-minded and was scolded for it; now, her heart was even more troubled.

Just as she was lost in thought, a knock came at the door.

"Who is it?" Caixia went to open the door.

As the door opened, Yongqi, Fu Erkang, and Fu Ertai stood outside.

Xiao Yanzi was startled: "Fifth Prince? Erkang? Ertai? Why are you here?"

Yongqi entered the room, closed the door behind him, and said with a serious expression, "Xiao Yanzi, we have something to ask you."

As Yongqi listened, his heart was filled with mixed emotions.

He was shocked by this absurd misunderstanding, yet he felt pity for Xiao Yanzi’s panic and helplessness, and was even more worried about the consequences once this was exposed.

Fu Erkang said in a deep voice, "Gege, do you know what the consequences will be if this is exposed? The crime of deceiving the Emperor is no trivial matter."

"I know... I know..." Xiao Yanzi cried, "That’s why I didn’t dare to say... Erkang, I beg you, don’t tell the Emperor... Where is Ziwei? Where is she? I want to see her, I want to explain to her..."

"Miss Xia is currently at my residence," Fu Erkang said. "She injured her ankle and is recuperating."

Xiao Yanzi grabbed Yongqi’s sleeve: "Fifth Prince, will you take me to see Ziwei? I will tell her that I will return the identity of the Gege to her... I don’t want to be a Gege anymore, I really don’t..."

Xiao Yanzi froze.

She had only thought about returning the identity to Ziwei, but she hadn't considered this aspect.

"Then... then what should I do?" She looked at the three of them helplessly. "I can’t keep occupying Ziwei’s identity forever... She is Xia Yuhe’s daughter; she is the one who should be recognized as the Gege..."

Fu Erkang and Yongqi exchanged a glance.

"But I..."

"Listen to me." Yongqi pressed her shoulders, his eyes firm. "I will find a way. There will always be a solution that satisfies everyone."

Xiao Yanzi looked at the reassurance in his eyes, gradually calmed down, and nodded.

Fu Erkang added, "Gege, there is one more thing. When you and Miss Xia swore an oath of sisterhood, were there any tokens or proof? Or perhaps details that only the two of you knew?"

Xiao Yanzi thought for a moment: "Yes... when we swore our oath, we kowtowed to the moon and said, 'We share blessings and we share hardships.' I also gave her my amulet, and she gave me her jade pendant..."

As she spoke, she took a jade pendant from her bosom: "It’s this one. Ziwei said this was left to her by her mother and is her most precious possession."

Fu Erkang took the jade pendant and examined it closely; it was similar in style to the one Xia Ziwei had, only the patterns were different.

At this point, the whole truth was revealed.

When they left Shufang Studio, the three were heavy-hearted.

Fu Ertai sighed: "This is going to be troublesome. On one side is the true daughter of the Emperor, and on the other is the mistaken Huanzhu Gege... How are we to explain this to the Emperor?"

Yongqi remained silent.

He remembered Xiao Yanzi’s red, teary eyes from just moments ago, and her words, "I didn't mean to," and the bit of blame in his heart gradually turned into pity.

That girl, she too was a victim of circumstance.

"Let’s go back to the residence first," Fu Erkang said. "This matter... still needs to be discussed with my father."

The three of them, each lost in their own thoughts, disappeared into the night.

Inside Shufang Studio, Xiao Yanzi sat on the bed, hugging her knees, unable to stop her tears.

Mingyue pushed the door open gently and, seeing her like this, whispered: "Gege, please don't cry. If there is anything, any grievance, just say it, or go to Consort Ling. Consort Ling dotes on you; she will surely find a way for you."

Xiao Yanzi was stunned.

Tell Consort Ling?

That gentle and kind Consort Ling who treated her like her own daughter?

If Consort Ling knew she was a fake... would she still be so good to her?

She dared not think about it.

That night, the lights in Shufang Studio burned until dawn.

In the Yongshou Palace, as Jiang Rao sat before her mirror to dress in the morning, she listened to Suxin’s whispered report of the activity at Shufang Studio last night, and a faint smile curled at the corners of her lips.

She picked up a pearl hairpin and slowly inserted it into her hair in the mirror.

The woman in the mirror had delicate features and clear eyes, yet no one could see what kind of heart was hidden beneath that clarity.

chapters.title: Consort Ling Knows the Truth
chapters.content:
Yanxi Palace.

Consort Ling was lost in thought while looking at a pot of newly bloomed chrysanthemums, while Lamei reported trivial palace matters nearby. Suddenly hearing the announcement that the Huanzhu Gege had arrived, Consort Ling was somewhat surprised.

"Let her in."

Xiao Yanzi walked in, her eyes red and swollen, her expression panicked. As soon as Consort Ling saw her, she immediately dismissed the attendants and pulled her to sit by her side: "What is the matter? Who has bullied you?"

"Consort Ling..." As soon as Xiao Yanzi spoke, tears began to fall. "I, I have done something wrong... a terrible mistake..."

Consort Ling was startled, but her face remained gentle: "Tell me slowly. No matter how big the matter is, I am here."

Xiao Yanzi sobbed and recounted the whole story, from the oath of sisterhood in Jinan, to the misunderstanding at the hunting grounds, to the visit from Fu Erkang and the others yesterday... She cried as she spoke, and by the end, she was incoherent.

As Consort Ling listened, her expression gradually grew grave.

After Xiao Yanzi finished, she remained silent for a long time—so long that Xiao Yanzi’s heart grew cold, thinking she would surely be furious.

To her surprise, Consort Ling let out a long sigh and pulled her into her arms: "Silly child... such a big matter, why didn't you say so sooner?"

Xiao Yanzi was stunned: "Consort Ling... you aren't angry with me?"

"Why would I be angry with you?" Consort Ling gently stroked her back. "You were also a victim of circumstance. Injured at the hunting grounds, your life in danger—it is understandable that you couldn't speak clearly then. Later... you were just afraid, weren't you?"

Xiao Yanzi nodded vigorously, her tears soaking Consort Ling’s lapel: "I was afraid... afraid that if the Emperor knew I was a fake, he would have my head... and afraid, afraid that if you knew, you wouldn't love me anymore..."

"Nonsense," Consort Ling said softly. "I love you for who you are, not for the identity of 'Gege.' You are sincere and kind; these past few days, I have truly loved you as my own daughter."

Hearing this, Xiao Yanzi cried even harder.

Consort Ling waited until her emotions had calmed slightly before saying gently: "Since things have come to this, regret is useless. The most urgent task is to think of a solution that satisfies everyone."

"A solution that satisfies everyone?" Xiao Yanzi raised her teary eyes. "Can there still be such a solution?"

"We must try," Consort Ling mused. "That Miss Xia... is she currently at the Fu residence?"

Xiao Yanzi nodded: "Erkang said she injured her foot and is recuperating at the Fu residence."

Consort Ling pondered for a moment and said: "This matter concerns the royal bloodline and cannot be handled rashly. The identity of that Miss Xia must be verified clearly. If she is truly the daughter of Xia Yuhe... then this matter will be tricky."

She paused and added: "You just said that the Fifth Prince and the Fu brothers all know?"

"Yes," Xiao Yanzi said in a low voice. "They came to find me yesterday, and that was when I told them..."

Consort Ling’s eyes flickered, and she already had a plan in mind: "Since that is the case, tomorrow you will go and invite the Fifth Prince over. This matter... still needs to be discussed at length."

"Invite the Fifth Prince?" Xiao Yanzi was puzzled.

"The Fifth Prince is a prince, and the Fu family are high-ranking officials. Since this matter has already involved them, it cannot be handled privately," Consort Ling said slowly. "We must find a safe way to reveal the truth without damaging the Emperor’s dignity."

Xiao Yanzi nodded, half-understanding.

Consort Ling instructed: "For these few days, act as you always do in the palace; do not show any signs of change. Especially in front of your Imperial Father, you must be careful and cautious."

"I understand," Xiao Yanzi replied, though her heart remained anxious.

The next day, Xiao Yanzi followed her instructions and invited Yongqi to Shufang Studio.

Consort Ling was already waiting in the side hall. Yongqi was somewhat surprised to see her, but he still bowed respectfully: "Consort Ling."

"Fifth Prince, there is no need for such formalities," Consort Ling said gently. "Xiao Yanzi has already told me about last night. I invited you here today to discuss a strategy."

Yongqi looked at Xiao Yanzi, and seeing that her eyes were still somewhat red and swollen, he couldn't bear it and said: "This matter... is indeed tricky. After I returned, I thought about it for a long time, but it is difficult to find a solution that satisfies everyone."

Xiao Yanzi nodded, tears welling up in her eyes again.

Fu Residence.

After hearing the message from Consort Ling passed on by Yongqi, Fu Erkang pondered for a moment and said: "Consort Ling is very thoughtful. However... I do not know if Miss Xia is willing."

Yongqi said: "This matter concerns Xiao Yanzi’s life, and also whether Miss Xia can be successfully recognized by her father. I believe Miss Xia is a woman of great principle and will surely understand."

Fu Erkang thought of Ziwei’s gentle and resilient demeanor and nodded: "I will go and speak with Miss Xia now."

In the guest room, Ziwei listened to Fu Erkang’s words and remained silent for a long time.

Jinsuo said anxiously from the side: "Miss, how can this be? You are the real Gege; why should you pretend to be a palace maid to enter the palace? This is too much of a grievance for you!"

Ziwei raised her head, and although there were tears in her eyes, they shone with determination: "If I can save Xiao Yanzi from a death sentence, what does it matter if I suffer a little grievance?"

She looked at Fu Erkang: "Master Fu, I am willing. But... after I enter the palace, may I see Xiao Yanzi?"

"Naturally," Fu Erkang replied. "Miss Xia, you will enter the palace under the pretext of being a companion to the Princess Pearl. It is only natural for sisters to meet."

Ziwei nodded: "Very well. I will enter the palace."

Fu Erkang looked at her calm face, a complex emotion surging within him. This young woman, who should clearly be the golden branch and jade leaf held in the palm of one's hand, was willing to suffer grievances for the sake of another...

"Miss Xia," he said gently, "rest assured. Since the Fifth Prince and Consort Ling have already intervened, they will surely make proper arrangements. When the time is ripe, justice will be served to you."

Ziwei smiled faintly: "Thank you, Master Fu. Ziwei... trusts you all."

The matter was thus settled.

A few days later, Consort Ling spoke to the Qianlong Emperor, saying that the Princess Pearl felt lonely in the palace and wished to find a kindred spirit for company. The Emperor, who was currently granting every request of his young daughter, immediately agreed. Thus, Xia Ziwei was brought into the palace as a "palace maid" and settled in the Shufang Studio.

All of this was done in secret, without a sound.

Meanwhile, in the Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao heard that a new palace maid had arrived at the Shufang Studio. Her surname was Xia, she was delicate and lovely, and her speech was quite refined...

She sat before the mirror, slowly pinning a jade hairpin into her hair, a knowing smile curling the corners of her lips.

What should enter the palace, had finally entered.

chapters.title: Recognition in the Deep Palace
chapters.content:
When the Fu family's carriage stopped before the palace gate, Ziwei lifted a corner of the curtain and gazed at the high, vermilion walls. Jinsuo, by her side, gripped her cold hands tightly.

"Miss..." Jinsuo's voice trembled.

"Since we have decided, do not be afraid," Ziwei said softly, though tears shimmered in her eyes.

Fu Erkang personally escorted them to the Yanxi Palace. Consort Ling was already waiting in the main hall. Seeing Ziwei enter, she looked her up and down, a flash of admiration crossing her eyes—though the girl was dressed plainly, her bearing was elegant and refined, with a scholarly air about her brows and eyes; she was certainly not the daughter of an ordinary family.

"Your servant Xia Ziwei pays her respects to Consort Ling." Ziwei bowed according to etiquette; though her movements were slightly stiff, she possessed an inherent composure.

"Rise," Consort Ling said gently. "Master Fu has already told me of your situation. From this day forward, you shall serve in the Shufang Studio. In name, you are a palace maid, but in truth..." She paused, "I will look after you well."

Ziwei lowered her head: "Thank you for your grace, Your Ladyship."

"I have already made the arrangements for the Shufang Studio." Consort Ling signaled for Lamei to bring over a set of palace attire. "These are clothes prepared for you. Later today, I will take you to see the Princess Pearl."

Ziwei took the clothes, her fingertips trembling slightly.

Finally... she was going to see Xiao Yanzi.

Shufang Studio.

Xiao Yanzi had been restless since the afternoon. Mingyue had urged her several times, but she still couldn't help but look toward the door.

"Princess, please set your heart at ease," Mingyue whispered. "Since Consort Ling has made the arrangements, she will surely bring Miss Xia here."

"I know... I just..." Xiao Yanzi clutched the corner of her dress. "I'm afraid Ziwei is angry with me, afraid she won't forgive me..."

Just as she was speaking, an announcement came from outside: "Consort Ling has arrived—"

Xiao Yanzi jumped up, nearly knocking over a teacup.

Consort Ling walked in with Ziwei. Ziwei had changed into a pale green palace gown, her hair styled like a maid's, adorned only with a simple silver hairpin. She kept her head lowered, her expression unreadable.

The moment Xiao Yanzi saw her, her eyes turned red.

Consort Ling dismissed the attendants, leaving only Mingyue and Caixia to guard the door. Once only the three of them remained in the hall, she said softly: "Xiao Yanzi, she is here. You two... have a good talk."

With that, she turned and went to the side hall, leaving the main hall to the sisters.

The hall doors closed.

Xiao Yanzi looked at Ziwei standing there; her lips moved, but no sound came out. Ziwei slowly raised her head, her eyes already brimming with tears.

Their gazes met, both pairs of eyes blurred with tears.

"Ziwei..." Xiao Yanzi choked, walking forward step by step. "I'm sorry... I'm truly sorry..."

Ziwei shook her head, tears falling: "No... it is not your fault..."

"It is my fault!" Xiao Yanzi grabbed her hands. "I was useless, I was injured and couldn't speak clearly... I was cowardly, afraid to tell the Emperor the truth... I usurped your position and caused you to suffer outside the palace..."

She cried incoherently, and Ziwei was also streaming with tears. The two embraced, sobbing uncontrollably.

"Xiao Yanzi... I don't blame you..." Ziwei sobbed. "I know you didn't mean it... That arrow at the hunting grounds, the wound was so severe... It is a miracle you survived..."

"But I took your identity..." Xiao Yanzi wept. "You are Xia Yuhe's daughter, you are the one who should be recognized as the princess... Yet I wore your clothes, wore your crown, and went to the Ancestral Temple to offer sacrifices... Ziwei, I'm sorry, I'm truly a terrible person..."

Ziwei held her tightly: "Don't say such foolish things... We are sworn sisters, to share in blessings and hardships alike... As long as you are safe, I am happier than anything..."

The two cried for a long time before they gradually calmed down.

Xiao Yanzi pulled Ziwei to sit on the couch and looked at her closely: "You've lost weight... You must have suffered a lot these days, right?"

Ziwei wiped her tears and shook her head: "It's fine. Master Fu treated us very well."

"Erkang?" Xiao Yanzi remembered something and asked hurriedly, "How is your foot? That day on the street, I saw you fall..."

"It's no longer a problem," Ziwei said. "Master Fu called a doctor, and after applying medicine for a few days, I can walk now."

Xiao Yanzi was relieved, but then thought of another matter: "Ziwei, don't worry, I will definitely return your identity to you! I'll go tell the Emperor right now—"

"No!" Ziwei hurriedly pulled her back. "Consort Ling said this matter requires careful planning. If we expose it rashly, your life will be in danger!"

"But I can't keep usurping your identity!" Xiao Yanzi said anxiously. "You are the real princess; you are the one who should return to your ancestors!"

Ziwei held her hands and said gently: "Xiao Yanzi, listen to me. This matter concerns the dignity of the Imperial family; it cannot be solved simply by saying 'it was a mistake.' The Emperor has already announced to the world that you are the princess. If we suddenly say you are a fake, how would the Emperor face this? What would the world think?"

Xiao Yanzi was stunned. She had never thought of these things.

"Then... what should we do?" she asked helplessly.

"Consort Ling and the Fifth Prince are already thinking of ways," Ziwei comforted her softly. "Let us remain still for now and make plans when the time is ripe."

Xiao Yanzi looked at her calm face, feeling even more guilty: "Ziwei... why are you so kind... I stole your father, I stole your identity, yet you don't blame me..."

"Because we are sisters," Ziwei said with tears in her eyes, yet smiling. "On the day we swore our oath at the Great Courtyard, we agreed to share blessings and hardships. Now that you have found happiness, I am happy for you."

Xiao Yanzi began to cry again: "I don't want to enjoy happiness alone... Ziwei, stay, will you? Stay in the Shufang Studio, let us sisters be together..."

"Consort Ling has already arranged for me to serve in the Shufang Studio," Ziwei said.

"That's wonderful!"

The two talked for a while longer. Ziwei detailed her experiences since entering the palace, and Xiao Yanzi told her about the situation in the palace. When mentioning Consort Ling, Xiao Yanzi said: "Consort Ling is a very good person; she treats me like her own daughter. After she learned the truth, not only did she not blame me, but she also helped us find a way..."

Ziwei nodded: "Consort Ling is indeed magnanimous. It is a blessing that we have her help."

As they were speaking, Consort Ling came over from the side hall. Seeing that both their eyes were red, she said gently: "Have you said everything you needed to?"

Xiao Yanzi nodded vigorously, holding Ziwei's hand: "Thank you, Consort Ling!"

Consort Ling sat down with a smile: "Since that is the case, I shall take my leave."

"Respectfully sending off Consort Ling!" Xiao Yanzi said loudly.

"There is just one thing," Consort Ling said with a serious expression. "In front of the Emperor, you must not show any traces. Ziwei's identity is known only to us few; before the truth comes to light, you must not let a sixth person know."

Xiao Yanzi and Ziwei nodded in unison.

Consort Ling gave a few more instructions and then left completely.

Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao woke from her afternoon nap and was adjusting her makeup in the mirror when Suxin came in from outside and whispered: "Your Ladyship, two new palace maids have arrived at the Yanxi Palace, one named Xia Ziwei and one named Jinsuo. Today, Consort Ling took them to the Shufang Studio, and they spoke with the Princess Pearl for a long time."

Jiang Rao's hand holding the hairpin paused slightly, then she pinned it into her hair as if nothing had happened: "Oh? The Princess Pearl and the new palace maids are very compatible?"

"The young eunuchs at the Shufang Studio say that the two were locked in the hall for a long time, and when they came out, their eyes were red," Suxin said. "Also... that maid surnamed Xia is extremely beautiful, not like an ordinary palace maid."

Jiang Rao examined the position of the hairpin in the mirror, a faint arc curling the corners of her lips.

Ziwei had entered the palace.

She had recognized Xiao Yanzi.

"Your Ladyship seems... to be in a very good mood?" Suxin noticed the smile on her lips.

"Yes,"

chapters.title: Good Intentions with Bad Results
chapters.content:
Shufang Studio study.

Ziwei was lowering her head, organizing the books on the shelf. Her movements were light and meticulous, placing each book neatly by category. Jinsuo was wiping the desk nearby, and both remained silent.

Since the day she recognized Xiao Yanzi, Ziwei had moved into the Shufang Studio as a palace maid. In name, she was a maid serving the Princess's writing needs, but in reality, she and Xiao Yanzi addressed each other as sisters and spent their days together. However, in front of others, they still had to maintain the etiquette of mistress and servant.

Footsteps were heard outside, and Mingyue hurried in, whispering: "Miss Ziwei, the Emperor is coming this way."

Ziwei's hand trembled, nearly knocking over the book she was holding. She steadied herself, returned the book to the shelf, lowered her head, and stepped aside.

When the Qianlong Emperor walked into the study, he saw a delicate palace maid standing by the bookshelf, her eyes lowered and her demeanor respectful. His gaze lingered on her for a moment, and he asked: "Are you new?"

Ziwei bowed: "Replying to the Emperor, your servant is Xia Ziwei, sent by Consort Ling to serve the Princess's writing needs."

Her voice was gentle, her articulation clear.

The Qianlong Emperor nodded, asked no more, and turned to look at the bookshelf: "How have Xiao Yanzi's studies been these past few days?"

Caixia hurriedly said: "The Princess has been very diligent; she even practiced calligraphy for the whole day yesterday."

Just as she was speaking, Xiao Yanzi ran in from outside. Seeing the Emperor, her eyes lit up: "Imperial Father!"

She ran too fast and nearly tripped over the threshold. Ziwei instinctively reached out to steady her, then quickly withdrew her hand and stepped back half a pace.

Qianlong saw this and raised an eyebrow: "You girl, you are always so rash."

Xiaoyanzi stuck out her tongue and stood up straight: "Why does Huang Ama have time to come over today?"

"To check on your studies." Qianlong sat down at the desk, picked up the calligraphy she had written yesterday, and looked it over: "There is improvement."

Having received praise, Xiaoyanzi beamed, her eyes curving into crescents. But suddenly remembering something, her smile faded slightly, and she cast a furtive glance at Ziwei, who was standing to the side.

Ziwei kept her eyes lowered, her expression calm, as if she were merely an ordinary palace maid.

Qianlong tested Xiaoyanzi on a few points of her studies and urged her to study diligently before rising to leave. As he left, his gaze swept over Ziwei inadvertently. Seeing her keep her head bowed and her demeanor modest and proper, he nodded inwardly—the person Consort Ling had chosen was indeed not bad.

After Qianlong left, Xiaoyanzi finally breathed a sigh of relief and pulled Ziwei aside: "Ziwei, you scared me to death just now... Huang Ama didn't recognize you, did he?"

Ziwei shook her head and said softly: "The Emperor only took me for an ordinary palace maid."

"That's good then..." Xiaoyanzi patted her chest, then remembered something and frowned: "But Huang Ama has been... staying at Yongshou Palace for the past few days."

She had heard this from Mingyue. Mingyue had been in the palace for a long time and was well-informed about the news in various palaces. She had mentioned in passing during a chat these past few days that the Emperor had been with Consort Chen for several consecutive days.

Hearing this, Ziwei’s eyes flickered, but she only said gently: "The Emperor has his own arrangements. As servants, we should not presume to discuss them."

Xiaoyanzi, however, felt a bit indignant: "But Consort Ling is so kind... Why doesn't Huang Ama go to see her more often?"

She thought of how well Consort Ling treated her, and then of the sadness that had flashed in Consort Ling's eyes that day, and the sense of injustice in her heart grew even stronger.

Mingyue whispered from the side: "Gege, matters of the inner palace... it is better if we do not inquire."

Xiaoyanzi pursed her lips and said nothing, but the matter still weighed on her mind.

Kunning Palace.

Nanny Rong brought in a tea tray and, seeing the Empress lost in thought while staring at a pot of flowers, whispered: "Your Majesty, this old servant heard something... The Fu family sent two maids to Yanxi Palace a few days ago."

The Empress raised her eyes: "The Fu family?"

"Yes." Nanny Rong leaned closer: "They say they were new maids bought by the manor, clever and capable. Consort Ling took a liking to them and kept them... She even assigned them to Shufang Studio to serve Huanzhu Gege."

The Empress took the teacup and took a light sip: "Consort Ling certainly knows how to conduct herself. The Fu family are the Emperor's favorites; with this move, she has both won over the Fu family and pleased Huanzhu Gege."

"Your Majesty, this old servant also heard..." Nanny Rong’s voice dropped even lower: "One of the maids sent to Shufang Studio is surnamed Xia. She is exceptionally beautiful and speaks with great refinement, not like someone from an ordinary family. Huanzhu Gege has been with her often these past few days and they get along very well."

"Surnamed Xia?" The Empress frowned slightly.

"Yes. It happened just these past few days." A trace of suspicion flashed in Nanny Rong’s eyes: "Your Majesty, do you think... could there be something suspicious about this?"

The Empress pondered for a moment and set down the teacup: "It's just a maid, what could be suspicious? Consort Ling is accustomed to these ways of buying people's hearts. It is the Emperor, however..."

She paused, her tone turning cold: "I heard the Emperor has been staying at Yongshou Palace for several days in a row?"

Nanny Rong’s expression darkened: "Yes. Consort Chen has been... enjoying great imperial favor these past few days."

A flash of ferocity crossed the Empress's eyes, and she slammed her handkerchief onto the table: "Vixen!"

Yongshou Palace had indeed been lively these past few days.

Qianlong had stayed here for several nights in a row, keeping Jiang Rao busy every night, but rewards were also flowing in like water. One day it was a box of South Sea pearls, the next a few bolts of cloud brocade from Jiangnan, and the day after that, newly offered fruits and pastries.

Jiang Rao accepted everything that came her way, yet she was never overly ostentatious. Whenever she received rewards, she would always distribute some to the various palaces, especially to the Empress and the high-ranking consorts; she never lacked in etiquette.

On this day, as she was contemplating what kind of dress to make with a bolt of cloud brocade, Suxin entered from outside and whispered: "Your Majesty, over at Kunning Palace... another set of tea sets was broken today."

Jiang Rao did not even look up: "The Empress has quite a temper."

"And Yanxi Palace..." Suxin paused: "I heard Consort Ling has not been in a good mood these past few days."

Only then did Jiang Rao look up, her lips curving slightly: "The Emperor has been with us these past few days; it is only natural that Sister Ling is unhappy."

In Shufang Studio, Xiaoyanzi finally could not hold back.

When Qianlong came to check her studies that day, she asked as if inadvertently: "Huang Ama, are you... very busy these past few days?"

Qianlong was looking at her calligraphy and raised his eyes upon hearing this: "Why do you ask?"

"It's just... I feel like you rarely go to Yanxi Palace anymore." Xiaoyanzi said cautiously: "Consort Ling treats me so well, and I hope she can be happy too..."

Qianlong frowned slightly and put down the paper: "Xiaoyanzi, matters of the inner palace are not for you to inquire about."

Although his tone was flat, it carried displeasure.

Xiaoyanzi was startled and realized she had said the wrong thing. She hurriedly knelt: "Huang Ama, please forgive me... I didn't mean to..."

Qianlong looked at her panicked expression, his heart softening a little, but he still said: "Get up. Remember, which palace I visit is my own business."

"Yes..." Xiaoyanzi whispered, her eyes turning red.

Just then, an announcement came from outside the hall: "Consort Chen has arrived—"

Jiang Rao wore a moon-white qipao with a light purple vest over it, looking pure and elegant. She walked in gracefully, and seeing the stagnant atmosphere in the hall, her eyes shifted slightly. She stepped forward with a smile: "Is the Emperor checking on Huanzhu Gege's studies?"

Seeing her arrive, Qianlong’s expression softened: "Why has Rao'er come?"

"Your servant heard the Emperor was here, so I came to see." Jiang Rao’s gaze fell on Xiaoyanzi’s reddened eyes, and she paused before saying softly: "What is the matter with Gege? Did you not do your studies well and make the Emperor angry?"

Xiaoyanzi bit her lip and said nothing.

Qianlong said indifferently: "It is nothing. The child is ignorant and said some things she shouldn't have."

Jiang Rao understood but did not press further, only smiling as she took Qianlong’s arm: "Emperor, please don't be angry. Gege is young, and it is inevitable that she might be thoughtless at times. Your servant has just obtained a jar of good tea; would the Emperor like to go to Yongshou Palace to taste it?"

Her voice was sweet and soft, and her eyes held a hint of coquettishness.

Distracted by her, Qianlong’s displeasure dissipated, and he nodded: "Very well."

Jiang Rao then looked at Xiaoyanzi and said warmly: "Gege, rest well. Take your time with your studies, there is no rush."

With that, she walked out of Shufang Studio, arm in arm with Qianlong.

Xiaoyanzi stood in place, watching their retreating figures, her heart filled with mixed emotions.

Ziwei, who had been standing quietly by the bookshelf, finally raised her head, looking in the direction Jiang Rao had left, a complex emotion flashing in her eyes.

Mingyue stepped forward cautiously: "Gege..."

"Did I say the wrong thing?" Xiaoyanzi asked in a low voice.

Mingyue sighed: "Gege meant well, but matters of the inner palace... indeed should not be inquired about."

Ziwei walked over and advised softly: "Gege, do not blame yourself. The Emperor did not severely punish you, which is already a sign of his generosity. From now on... just be careful with your words and actions."

Xiaoyanzi nodded, but she remained unhappy.

Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao personally brewed tea for Qianlong. Amidst the curling tea fragrance, she looked up at him: "Was the Emperor... angry with Gege just now?"

Qianlong took the teacup and shook his head: "That child has no filter. When it comes to which palace I visit, when is it her turn to dictate?"

"Gege meant well." Jiang Rao said warmly: "She hasn't been in the palace long, and she was taught by Sister Ling. It is only natural that she is close to her. Seeing that the Emperor has been with me these past few days, she spoke up for Sister Ling out of a pure and innocent heart."

She spoke cleverly, both exonerating Xiaoyanzi and pointing out the closeness between Consort Ling and Xiaoyanzi.

Qianlong heard this, but his displeasure did not fully vanish. He only said indifferently: "Consort Ling teaches her the rules; she should have taught her to be cautious in her words and actions."

Jiang Rao lowered her eyes and smiled, saying no more, only pushing the teacup toward him: "Emperor, try this tea."

In Yanxi Palace, Consort Ling listened to the faint sound of the zither coming from Yongshou Palace, her expression desolate.

Lamei stepped in and whispered: "Your Majesty, news just came from Shufang Studio... Huanzhu Gege spoke up for you in front of the Emperor, which displeased him."

Consort Ling was startled, then gave a bitter smile: "That child... is truly foolish."

"But Gege also meant well..."

"Good intentions leading to bad results, that's all." Consort Ling sighed: "The Emperor dislikes interference in palace politics the most, and even more so when someone interferes with his whereabouts. With Xiaoyanzi speaking up like this, I fear the Emperor will harbor resentment toward me."

She looked toward the direction of Yongshou Palace, her eyes complex.

Consort Chen... what a clever strategy.

Without a sound, she made Xiaoyanzi act as her blade.

Shufang Studio study.

Ziwei was copying scriptures by candlelight. Xiaoyanzi lay on the table nearby, saying gloomily: "Ziwei, am I very stupid? I always do the wrong thing..."

Ziwei’s pen tip paused, and she said warmly: "Gege is simply pure-hearted and lacks those devious thoughts. In this deep palace... being simple is not necessarily a bad thing, but one cannot be too simple."

"Then what should I do to be right?"

Ziwei put down her pen and looked at her earnestly: "Gege only needs to remember that the Emperor is the Sovereign and the Father. The affairs of the Sovereign and Father are not for us, as subjects and daughters, to inquire about. Consort Ling treats you well; keep that in your heart, and accompany her privately—that is the best way to repay her."

Xiaoyanzi nodded, as if she understood, yet not quite.

At this moment in Kunning Palace, the Empress heard Nanny Rong’s report and a cold smile curled her lips: "Consort Ling wanted to use the Fu family to please Huanzhu Gege, but didn't expect to be countered by that girl. Consort Chen is even more brilliant; without any effort, she has caused Consort Ling to harbor resentment in the Emperor's heart."

Nanny Rong whispered: "Your Majesty, should we..."

"No rush." The Empress said indifferently: "Let them fight. We shall... wait and see."

chapters.title: Your servant has missed you
chapters.content:
The fact that Qianlong had been staying at Yongshou Palace for several consecutive days finally caused a ripple in the outer court. After the morning court session that day, several old officials gathered together to whisper, their words all implying that "the inner palace should be treated with equal favor." Although they did not say it explicitly, how could Qianlong not understand their meaning?

After finishing the memorials in the Hall of Mental Cultivation, Qianlong paused and said to Wu Shulai: "Today... we go to Yanxi Palace."

When the news reached Yanxi Palace, Consort Ling was teaching Lamei how to arrange flowers. Upon hearing that the Emperor was coming, the branch of begonia in her hand trembled slightly, nearly snapping.

"Your Majesty..." Lamei called out softly.

Consort Ling steadied herself, placed the flower branch into the vase, and said indifferently, "Go and prepare some of the snacks the Emperor likes."

Though she appeared calm on the surface, her heart was surging like a tide. Since the day Little Swallow’s outburst displeased the Emperor, she had not seen the Imperial countenance for several days. Now that the Emperor was suddenly coming, was it out of lingering affection, or... did it hold a deeper meaning?

In Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao heard that the Qianlong Emperor had gone to Yanxi Palace. She merely gave a faint "Oh" and continued to fiddle with the embroidery frame in her hands.

Su Xin whispered, "Your Ladyship, the Emperor went to Yanxi Palace today..."

"I know," Jiang Rao said without looking up. "Where the Emperor chooses to go is his own business. Am I to stop him?"

Despite her words, the stitches in her hands became noticeably uneven. Seeing this, Su Xin dared not say more.

Jiang Rao set down the embroidery frame, walked to the window, and looked toward Yanxi Palace, a cold sneer curling her lips.

Let him go. She wanted to see how long Consort Ling could remain smug.

Yanxi Palace.

By the time Qianlong arrived, Consort Ling had already prepared tea and snacks. She wore a lotus-pink qipao today, with only a single pearl flower pinned in her hair—simple and gentle. Seeing Qianlong enter, she curtsied gracefully: "Your servant greets the Emperor."

"Rise." Qianlong helped her up, his gaze lingering on her face for a moment. "I haven't seen you for a few days; you’ve grown thinner."

Consort Ling lowered her eyes and smiled faintly: "Perhaps it is the dryness of autumn; I have had little appetite. What brings the Emperor here today?"

"To see you." Qianlong sat on the couch and took the tea she offered. "These past few days... has the palace been peaceful?"

Consort Ling’s heart stirred, but she showed nothing on her face: "Everything is well. Princess Huan Zhu has made much progress in her studies lately, and Sister Chen Fei often sends over fruits and snacks. The sisters get along harmoniously."

Her words were comprehensive, mentioning both Little Swallow and flattering Jiang Rao.

Qianlong nodded, but then added, "That child, Little Swallow... her nature is straightforward. You must put more effort into guiding her."

The words were plain, yet they made Consort Ling’s heart tighten. She looked up at Qianlong and, seeing his expression remained unchanged, said softly, "The Princess has a pure and kind heart, but she is young and sometimes thoughtless. Your servant will guide her well."

Qianlong said no more, slowly sipping his tea. The hall fell into silence.

Consort Ling stood by, the small spark of joy in her heart gradually cooling. The Emperor’s visit today seemed... not as simple as merely reminiscing about old times.

Sure enough, after sitting for a while, Qianlong rose and said, "I still have memorials to review. I shall return now."

"Your servant respectfully sends off the Emperor." Consort Ling curtsied. Only after Qianlong had departed did she slowly straighten up, her eyes filled with desolation.

La Mei stepped forward and whispered, "Your Ladyship, why did the Emperor leave after sitting for such a short time..."

Consort Ling shook her head, walked to the window, and watched Qianlong’s retreating figure, saying softly, "The Emperor’s visit was merely a show for the imperial court. Why should I... take it to heart?"

Shufang Studio.

When Little Swallow heard that Qianlong had gone to Yanxi Palace, she was so happy she nearly jumped up: "Really? Imperial Father went to see Consort Ling?"

Mingyue nodded with a smile: "It is true. The Emperor sat in Yanxi Palace for half an hour."

"That’s great!" Little Swallow clapped her hands. "I knew it! Imperial Father wouldn’t forget Consort Ling!"

Ziwei was tidying up books nearby; hearing this, she looked up, wanting to say something but stopping herself.

Little Swallow, however, was already chattering away to Mingyue: "I told you! Consort Ling is so wonderful, how could Imperial Father not like her? He must have been too busy these past few days to visit Yanxi Palace..."

"Princess," Ziwei interrupted her softly, "these words... let us keep them to ourselves. Do not spread them."

Little Swallow stuck out her tongue: "I know, I know. Ziwei, don't you think Consort Ling must be very happy right now?"

Ziwei lowered her eyes and said softly, "Perhaps."

She recalled what Mingyue had said—that the Emperor had left after only half an hour. If he truly cared, how could he have been in such a rush?

Kunning Palace.

Nanny Rong reported the events at Yanxi Palace to the Empress, adding in a low voice, "Your Ladyship, the Emperor stayed at Yanxi Palace for only half an hour before returning to the Hall of Mental Cultivation."

The Empress was removing her makeup in front of the mirror; hearing this, she sneered: "Merely a show for the court. If the Emperor truly cared, would he have stayed for only half an hour?"

She pulled out the last hairpin and looked at her no-longer-youthful reflection in the mirror, a flash of cruelty in her eyes: "What about Chen Fei? Any movement there?"

"Yongshou Palace has been very quiet today," Nanny Rong said. "Consort Chen Fei stayed in her palace all day and did not go out."

The Empress nodded: "She is certainly composed."

"Consort Ling and Chen Fei," the Empress said coldly, "one wants to secure favor through Princess Huan Zhu, the other relies on the Emperor’s deep affection. Let them fight. I want to see who will have the last laugh."

That night, Hall of Mental Cultivation.

Qianlong finished reviewing the last memorial and rubbed his temples. Wu Shulai stepped forward at the right moment: "Your Majesty, it is late. Tonight, you..."

"Yongshou Palace." Qianlong replied without hesitation.

Wu Shulai was stunned: "The Emperor is not going to Yanxi Palace..."

"I have already been there today," Qianlong rose. "Prepare the carriage for Yongshou Palace."

When the imperial carriage arrived at Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was leaning against the window, watching the moon. Hearing that the Emperor had arrived, a flicker of surprise crossed her eyes, but she quickly returned to normal and rose to welcome him.

"Why has the Emperor come?" Her voice was soft and coquettish, filled with a hint of pleasant surprise. "Your servant thought... the Emperor would spend the night at Yanxi Palace."

Qianlong wrapped his arm around her shoulders: "What? Are you not welcoming me?"

"How would your servant dare?" Jiang Rao leaned into his embrace, her fingers tracing circles on his chest. "It’s just that I heard the Emperor went to Yanxi Palace today, and I thought the Emperor would be keeping Consort Ling company."

The hint of jealousy in her tone was perfectly measured.

Qianlong chuckled and pinched her cheek: "Am I not here to keep you company now?"

Jiang Rao finally beamed and pulled him into the hall: "Your servant has prepared wine and food. Would the Emperor like to taste them?"

Candlelight flickered, and the aroma of wine permeated the air.

After a few cups of wine, Jiang Rao’s cheeks were flushed, and her eyes were filled with charm. Qianlong was moved; he swept her up in his arms and headed toward the inner chamber.

Red candles warmed the curtains, and the bed swayed.

In the height of passion, Jiang Rao clung to Qianlong’s shoulders, panting softly in his ear: "Your Majesty... you haven't come for days, I have missed you so much..."

Qianlong looked down at her: "Really?"

"Of course it is true." Jiang Rao’s eyes shimmered with moisture. "Your servant hoped for your arrival every day... but I dared not disturb you..."

The words were aggrieved, yet they softened Qianlong’s heart. He kissed her forehead, his movements becoming gentler: "I have... been quite busy these past few days."

"Your servant knows." Jiang Rao buried her face in his chest. "The Emperor is the Son of Heaven, with a thousand things to attend to. Your servant should not be so greedy. It’s just... my heart felt heavy..."

Looking at her slightly reddened eyes, the displeasure Qianlong felt due to the discussions at court gradually dissipated.

Never mind. It was just the noise of old ministers. He was the Son of Heaven; did he need to look at others' faces to decide which consort to favor?

That night, the lights in Yongshou Palace burned until very late.

The next day, the news spread to all the palaces.

In Yanxi Palace, when Consort Ling heard that the Emperor had spent the night at Yongshou Palace again, the flower branch she was arranging snapped with a "crack."

La Mei hurried forward: "Your Ladyship..."

Consort Ling waved her hand, signaling her to step back. She walked to the window and looked toward Yongshou Palace for a long time before saying softly, "I should have understood long ago."

Talk of equal favor or court discussions—in the Emperor’s heart, none of it compared to a single smile from Chen Fei.

The favor in this deep palace had always been so unfair.

Shufang Studio.

When Little Swallow heard that Qianlong had gone to Yongshou Palace again last night, she wilted: "How could this be... Didn't Imperial Father go to see Consort Ling? Why did he go to Yongshou Palace again?"

Ziwei was grinding ink for her; hearing this, she said softly, "Princess, the Emperor has his own considerations. We... should not ask."

"But Consort Ling..." Little Swallow’s eyes reddened. "She must be very sad..."

Ziwei was silent. She remembered seeing Consort Ling at Yanxi Palace that day and the inescapable desolation in her eyes.

Which woman in this deep palace was not the same? Favored today, out of favor tomorrow; the rise and fall all depended on a single thought from the Son of Heaven.

And she and Little Swallow... what would become of them?

chapters.title: Vixen!
chapters.content:
A few days later, Qianlong was feeling dizzy from reviewing memorials in the Hall of Mental Cultivation. No sooner had the reports on the Jiangnan floods been dealt with than reports on military provisions for the Northwest arrived. He irritably threw down his vermilion brush and rubbed his temples.

"Your Majesty, take a rest." Wu Shulai carefully offered ginseng tea.

Qianlong took the cup and suddenly remembered the new palace maid at Shufang Studio. He had only seen her briefly that day and thought her modest and well-behaved, but he hadn't looked closely. Since he was feeling frustrated today, he might as well test if that girl was as talented as Little Swallow claimed.

"Prepare the carriage for Shufang Studio."

In Shufang Studio, Little Swallow was frowning at an embroidery frame. Mingyue was instructing her from the side: "Princess, the needle must go through here..."

"I know, I know!" Little Swallow was in a flurry; one stitch later, the thread was tangled in a knot. She threw the embroidery frame down in anger. "I’m not doing it! This is harder than archery!"

Ziwei was tidying books nearby; hearing this, she smiled: "Princess, don't be anxious, take it slowly."

"Ziwei, you come and embroider it for me..." Little Swallow pleaded with a bitter face.

"That won't do," Ziwei said gently. "The Princess must complete her own lessons."

Just as they were fussing, an announcement came from outside: "The Emperor has arrived—"

Little Swallow was startled, and the needle in her hand dropped to the floor with a "clack." Ziwei immediately put down the books and retreated to the side with her head bowed.

Qianlong walked in and saw Little Swallow bowing in a panic, the embroidery frame rolling at her feet. He couldn't help but laugh: "What are you doing?"

"Im-Imperial Father..." Little Swallow stammered, "Your daughter is... learning to embroider."

Qianlong glanced at the crooked stitches and shook his head: "You, with your restless nature, learning this is a struggle for you." His gaze shifted to the slender figure by the bookshelf. "You are Xia Ziwei?"

Ziwei curtsied, her voice clear and gentle: "Replying to the Emperor, this servant is Xia Ziwei."

"I heard you can read?" Qianlong walked to the desk and flipped through the calligraphy copybook Little Swallow had been practicing. The characters were of uneven size and slanted; he frowned as he looked at them.

Ziwei lowered her eyes: "I know a few characters."

Qianlong pulled a copy of the *Book of Songs* from the shelf, flipped to a page at random, pointed to "Guan guan go the ospreys, on the islet in the river," and asked, "How do you explain this?"

Ziwei looked up and replied softly, "This line uses the osprey's cry as an opening. The male and female osprey are devoted to each other, never parting. The poem uses this to symbolize a gentleman’s longing for a virtuous lady. As the opening piece of the *Classic of Poetry*, it speaks of the feelings between men and women, which arise from nature and conform to ritual."

Her explanation was not only accurate but also highlighted the profound meaning of "arising from emotion, yet stopping at ritual." Qianlong raised an eyebrow, flipped to the *Xiaoya* section, and pointed to "Long ago, when we departed, the willows were swaying," asking her to interpret it.

Ziwei pondered for a moment and said, "This is a poem about a soldier longing for his hometown. When he left home in the past, the willows were swaying and the spring breeze brushed his face; but today, upon his return, the rain and snow are falling thick and fast, and the journey is arduous. As time flows, things remain but people have changed; all the sorrow of parting is contained within."

Her voice was gentle, and when she said "things remain but people have changed," a faint glimmer seemed to flicker in her eyes. Qianlong listened, entranced, and followed up with several lines from *Li Sao* and the *Analects*. Ziwei answered fluently, not only explaining their meanings but also citing their origins and even offering her own insights.

Xiaoyanzi stood by, dumbfounded. She knew Ziwei was talented, but she had no idea she was this brilliant. Even the lines Emperor Father asked about, which she had never even heard of, Ziwei could answer with ease.

The admiration in Qianlong's eyes grew stronger. He set down the book and looked at Ziwei: "You have read quite a lot."

"When my mother was alive, she would teach me to read and write in her spare time to pass the days," Ziwei lowered her eyes, her long lashes casting shallow shadows on her cheeks.

"Your mother was a woman of insight," Qianlong nodded, suddenly intrigued. "Do you know how to play chess?"

Ziwei was startled, then said softly, "I know a little."

"Set up the board."

The chessboard was placed on a low table under the study window. Ziwei took the white pieces, and Qianlong took the black. Mingyue hurriedly brewed fresh tea, while Xiaoyanzi leaned in curiously—she couldn't understand Go, only finding the black and white pieces moving back and forth dizzying.

For the first few moves, Ziwei played with extreme caution, step by step, focusing on defense. Qianlong initially treated it as a pastime, playing casually, but after seven or eight moves, he began to sense something was wrong. This palace maid, seemingly gentle and decorous, had a formidable style of play. Her layout was dense, each move concealing a hidden counter-strategy, and before he knew it, she had subtly formed a surrounding formation.

Qianlong sat up straight, his expression turning serious. He pondered for a moment and placed a piece, breaking one of Ziwei's corners.

Ziwei did not panic; she picked up a white piece with her fingertips and placed it down gently. This move was ingenious; it seemed insignificant but quietly closed the gap Qianlong had just opened.

"A good move," Qianlong praised, a flash of surprise in his eyes.

The game lasted for an hour. Outside the window, the sky grew dark, and Caixia came in to light the lamps. The candlelight flickered, reflecting on the chessboard and Ziwei’s calm profile. She was very focused while playing, her brows lowered, and occasionally, when lost in thought, her fingertips tapped the edge of the board unconsciously. The candlelight danced on her long lashes, her silhouette gentle.

Qianlong watched her, and a strange feeling suddenly welled up in his heart. The way this girl carried herself while playing, the talent in her conversation, even the way she lowered her head... it reminded him of a woman he had discussed poetry and painting with by Daming Lake in Jinan many years ago.

"Your mother..." he paused, "taught you very well."

Ziwei’s fingertips trembled slightly, and the white piece almost went astray. She steadied herself and replied softly, "My mother often said that although a woman does not need to take the imperial examinations to serve in office, she should still be well-read and sensible, so as not to live this life in vain."

The words were plain, yet they stirred Qianlong’s heart. Xia Yuhe had once said something similar. He looked at Ziwei; this girl was only seventeen or eighteen, yet she possessed such insight and talent. Her mother must have been no ordinary woman.

The game ended with Qianlong winning by half a piece. He set down his piece and laughed, "Your chess skills are exquisite. It has been a long time since I encountered such an opponent."

Ziwei smiled faintly, "Your Majesty is too kind. It was Your Majesty who was letting me win."

"I did not," Qianlong said, in high spirits. "Another game?"

This game lasted even longer. Xiaoyanzi had long since fallen asleep, yawning, and was quietly led away to the outer room by Mingyue. Only Qianlong and Ziwei remained in the study, the candles crackling and autumn insects chirping outside the window.

Midway through the game, Qianlong suddenly asked, "Since you have read the *Classic of Poetry*, which piece do you like best?"

Ziwei placed a piece and said softly, "I like *Jianjia*. 'The reeds are lush and green, the white dew turns to frost. The one I long for, is on the other side of the water.'"

"Oh? Why?"

"The imagery of this poem is distant and profound—the longing for what cannot be attained, filled with both melancholy and persistence." Ziwei looked up at Qianlong, the candlelight dancing in her eyes. "It is just like... some people, some things, clearly within reach, yet as far as the ends of the earth."

Qianlong’s heart stirred again. He looked into Ziwei’s clear eyes and suddenly felt as if there were a thousand words hidden within them.

"Can you write poetry?" he changed the subject.

Ziwei nodded. Qianlong ordered someone to bring paper and brush. "Use an autumn night as the theme."

Ziwei picked up the brush, pondered for a moment, and let the tip touch the rice paper. Her posture was upright, her wrist light, and in just a moment, a seven-character quatrain was finished:

"The jade dew withers the maple forest,The Wushan and Wuxia gorges are bleak and somber.Cold garments urge the knife and ruler everywhere,High in Baidi City, the evening fulling blocks sound in haste."

The handwriting was elegant and neat. Although the poem borrowed lines from Du Fu, it possessed a unique, chilly atmosphere. After reading it, Qianlong’s admiration grew even deeper: "A fine poem. For someone of your young age to have such insight is rare."

Ziwei lowered her eyes, "I dare not accept such praise."

Qianlong continued to discuss poetry and songs with her, and Ziwei responded with ease. When they spoke of Li Bai, her eyes sparkled: "Li Taibai’s poetry and wine were romantic and unrestrained; the line 'Heaven has made me talented, I must have a use' speaks the hearts of so many."

"With such talent, it is a pity for you to be a palace maid," he sighed.

Ziwei shook her head gently, "To be able to serve the Gege and be accompanied by books, I am already content."

Just then, Wu Shulai’s voice came from outside: "Your Majesty, it is past midnight, it is time to rest."

Qianlong was startled to realize that two hours had passed. He stood up and said, "Let us stop here for today."

"Respectfully sending Your Majesty off," Ziwei bowed in farewell.

Qianlong walked out of Shufangzhai. The cool autumn night breeze brushed his face, and he took a deep breath, feeling refreshed. It had been a long time since he had talked and played chess with someone so freely. This Xia Ziwei was truly a remarkable person.

Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao had not yet slept. Suxin entered on tiptoe and whispered, "Your Ladyship, the Emperor is at Shufangzhai... he played two games of chess with that palace maid Xia, discussing poetry and history until midnight before leaving."

Jiang Rao was removing her makeup in front of the mirror; her jade comb paused at these words: "Oh? The Emperor appreciates her very much?"

"I heard the Emperor praised her for her exquisite chess skills and extraordinary talent," Suxin lowered her voice. "Your Ladyship, if that palace maid wins the Emperor's heart, will she..."

"Will she what?" Jiang Rao looked into the mirror, leisurely taking off her earrings. "The more the Emperor appreciates her, the more opportunity she has to acknowledge her father. I am hoping for her to succeed soon."

She set down the comb, walked to the window, and looked toward Shufangzhai, a faint smile curling her lips.

Ziwei, oh Ziwei, you must work harder. This play in the deep palace would not be interesting without you, the real Gege.

Shufangzhai Study.

Ziwei sat alone before the chessboard, her fingertips gently stroking the spot where Qianlong had placed his piece. Jin Suo brought in the calming tea and, seeing her like this, whispered, "Miss, it is late, you should rest."

"Jin Suo," Ziwei looked up, her eyes shimmering with tears, "today... I spoke so much with Emperor Father today."

"Miss..." Jin Suo felt a lump in her throat.

"He praised my chess, he praised my poetry," Ziwei’s voice choked. "He even said my mother... taught me very well."

She recalled the expression on Qianlong’s face when he said those words, that gentle, approving gaze that almost made her weep. That was her father; she was so close to him, yet she could not acknowledge him.

"Miss, do not be sad," Jin Suo held her hand. "Today is a good start. Since the Emperor appreciates you, he will surely come often in the future. One day, you will be able to reclaim your identity."

Ziwei nodded, wiping the tears from the corners of her eyes. She looked out at the deep night, her heart gradually firming.

This road was long and difficult, but she would walk it step by step. For her mother’s eighteen years of waiting, and for herself.

The night deepened, and the candles in Shufangzhai were finally extinguished.

In the Hall of Mental Cultivation, Qianlong lay on the couch, unable to sleep. The image of Ziwei’s focused expression while playing chess and her lively eyes while discussing poetry surfaced in his mind. This girl’s talent and insight were truly not like those of an ordinary palace maid.

He recalled her expression when she mentioned her mother, that line, "A woman should also be well-read and sensible," so similar to what Xia Yuhe had said back then.

"Xia Ziwei..." Qianlong murmured the name, feeling a strange sensation in his heart, though he could not say what it was.

Forget it, she is just a talented palace maid. He turned over and closed his eyes.

Kunning Palace.

Nanny Rong reported the events of Shufangzhai to the Empress in detail. The Empress listened and sneered, "Consort Ling is quite good at picking people, sending such a talented girl to serve the Huanzhu Gege. What, is she trying to use that girl’s talent to show that she has taught her well?"

"Your Ladyship, I also heard..." Nanny Rong leaned closer, "the Emperor played chess with that palace maid Xia until midnight, and they talked very happily."

A flash of severity crossed the Empress’s eyes: "A mere palace maid, daring to bewitch the master?"

"Your Ladyship, should we..."

"No rush," the Empress said lightly. "Let us wait and see. If that girl is truly restless, there are rules to deal with her."

She looked out the window, cold light flickering in her eyes.

This inner palace has never tolerated palace maids who are too outstanding.

chapters.title: Jealousy and Coquetry
chapters.content:
Qianlong went to Shufangzhai for two consecutive days.

The first day was for chess and poetry, and the second day was to examine her calligraphy—the girl was not only good at chess but also wrote with great elegance. On a whim, Qianlong had her copy the *Lantingji Xu* while he offered guidance. This guidance lasted for the better part of the day.

When the news reached Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao was embroidering a pouch. After Suxin finished her low-voiced report, the needle in her hand paused, then she continued embroidering the half-bloomed lotus, saying only faintly, "I see."

But the stitches were clearly not as even as usual.

By evening, Qianlong finally emerged from Shufangzhai. Wu Shulai carefully asked, "Your Majesty, tonight..."

"Yongshou Palace," Qianlong replied without hesitation. Although discussing poetry and art with that palace maid for the past two days had been pleasant, he still had to go and soothe Rao'er.

When the imperial carriage arrived at Yongshou Palace, the hall was quiet. Suxin came out to greet him, her expression somewhat troubled: "Your Majesty, Her Ladyship... she is feeling unwell and has already retired."

Qianlong raised an eyebrow: "So early?"

He walked straight into the inner chamber. Jiang Rao was indeed lying on the couch, facing the wall, covered by a silk quilt, not moving at all.

"Rao'er?" The Qianlong Emperor sat down by the side of the couch.

Jiang Rao did not answer.

Qianlong reached out to touch her forehead. "Where are you feeling unwell? Have you summoned the imperial physician?"

As soon as his hand touched her, Jiang Rao shrank inward, dodging his touch.

Qianlong was startled, then immediately understood. He waved his hand, dismissing the attendants. Once the palace servants had retreated, he leaned over and whispered into Jiang Rao's ear, "Are you sulking at me?"

Jiang Rao still said nothing.

Qianlong patiently coaxed her, "It is my fault for not coming to see you these past two days. But I haven't gone anywhere else; I’ve been at the Shufang Studio, testing Little Swallow on her studies."

It would have been better if he hadn't said that. At his words, Jiang Rao suddenly sat up, her eyes rimmed with red. "Your Majesty is lying! Your concubine has heard everything. How is Your Majesty testing the Princess's studies? It is clear you have been playing chess and discussing poetry with that new palace maid for the better part of the day!"

As she spoke, tears began to fall. "Your Majesty would now rather spend time playing chess with a little palace maid than keep your concubine company!"

Seeing her weeping like a flower in the rain, Qianlong’s heart softened. He reached out to wipe her tears, but Jiang Rao slapped his hand away and turned her back to him, ignoring him.

"Rao'er," Qianlong wrapped his arms around her from behind, his voice softening. "I merely saw that the maid had some talent and asked a few questions. What is this? Is my Rao'er actually jealous of a little palace maid?"

"Your concubine *is* jealous!" Jiang Rao broke free from him, turned back, and glared at him, tears still clinging to her lashes. "When Your Majesty went to the Shufang Studio these past two days, did you ever think of your concubine waiting here in the palace? I was longing for you, yet Your Majesty was having such a grand time playing chess with someone else that you forgot all about me!"

She sounded so aggrieved that her tears fell even harder. Qianlong felt a pang of heartache and reached out to hold her, but Jiang Rao pulled away. Qianlong simply pulled her into his arms, refusing to let go no matter how she struggled.

"Let go!" Jiang Rao pushed him.

Qianlong lowered his head and kissed her lips directly.

Jiang Rao was stunned, then struggled even more violently. Qianlong held the back of her head, deepening the kiss. This kiss carried an irresistible force, yet contained a gentle, soothing quality. At first, Jiang Rao pounded on his shoulders, but gradually, her hands softened.

After a long while, Qianlong released her. He pressed his forehead against hers and chuckled softly, "Are you still going to make a scene?"

Jiang Rao’s cheeks were flushed, her breathing unsteady, yet she still glared at him. "Your Majesty is a bully..."

"If I don't bully you, who would I bully?" Qianlong pinched her cheek. "No matter how talented that maid is, she is still just a maid. My Rao'er is the one who holds the place in my heart."

Jiang Rao pursed her lips, her eyes reddening again. "Is Your Majesty speaking from the heart?"

"A monarch does not speak in jest." Qianlong held her tighter. "I have been negligent these past two days. I will spend more time with you from now on, alright?"

Only then did Jiang Rao break into a smile. She leaned into his chest, her fingers tracing circles on his robe. "Then Your Majesty... must stay with your concubine and not go anywhere else."

"Very well, I won't go anywhere," Qianlong promised readily.

Satisfied, Jiang Rao called for the servants to come in and attend to them. When dinner was served, she personally served dishes to Qianlong and chatted about interesting things that had happened in the palace over the past two days, laughing and smiling as if she were not the same person who had been crying and making a scene just moments before.

Watching her charming, smiling face, the slight displeasure Qianlong felt over her jealousy vanished. Women, after all, showing a little temperament only proved how much they cared for him.

After dinner, Jiang Rao pestered Qianlong to play chess with her. Qianlong naturally agreed. The two played by the window; Jiang Rao’s chess skills were mediocre, and she played without any strategy, constantly taking back moves or acting spoiled. Qianlong, however, was not annoyed and let her have her way.

"Your Majesty, let your concubine win..." Jiang Rao held a chess piece, blinking her eyes at him.

Qianlong laughed. "Fine, fine, I’ll give you a three-move handicap."

The game was a chaotic mess, but Jiang Rao was delighted. After the game, she pulled Qianlong to listen to her play the zither. Her skill was also ordinary, and she missed several notes, but she was completely unaware, playing with total immersion.

Qianlong leaned against the couch, watching her focused profile in the candlelight, his heart softening. This kind of charming, lively spirit was his true Rao'er. That palace maid, though talented, was too quiet and lacked this spark.

Late at night, Jiang Rao finally grew tired and yawned in Qianlong’s arms.

"Sleepy?" Qianlong asked softly.

"Mm..." Jiang Rao closed her eyes, her voice slurred. "Your Majesty must not leave..."

"I won't leave. I'll stay with you." Qianlong carried her to the bed and laid her down gently.

Jiang Rao refused to let go, clutching his neck tightly. "Your Majesty must promise your concubine... to go to the Shufang Studio less often in the future."

Qianlong was taken aback.

Jiang Rao opened her eyes, which were shimmering with moisture. "Your concubine knows I shouldn't say this, but... but my heart hurts. If Your Majesty likes those with talent, your concubine can learn too. Will you teach me? Please don't go see others..."

As she spoke, tears welled up again. Seeing her like this, Qianlong’s heart softened, and he sighed, "Very well, I promise you."

Only then did Jiang Rao smile and kiss his lips. "Your Majesty is the best."

That night, the red candles in the Yongshou Palace burned warm, and the spring atmosphere was boundless.

Meanwhile, at the Shufang Studio, Ziwei was lost in thought, staring at a solitary lamp. Jinsuo was doing needlework nearby and said softly, "Miss, the Emperor has come both these past two days. Do you think... this is a good sign?"

Ziwei shook her head. "The Emperor merely appreciates my talent. We are still a long way from... recognizing each other."

"But it is a good thing nonetheless," Jinsuo said. "Since the Emperor likes talking to you, he will surely come often. As time goes on, he will eventually discover the truth."

Ziwei did not speak, only gazing at the flickering candlelight. The Emperor hadn't come today, and she felt a strange sense of emptiness. She knew she shouldn't, but that longing for fatherly love coiled around her heart like a vine.

Just as she was thinking this, Little Swallow's voice came from outside: "Ziwei! Ziwei, are you asleep?"

Ziwei hurried to open the door. Little Swallow ran in wearing a coat, closed the door mysteriously, and lowered her voice. "Ziwei, I heard... that since the Emperor has been coming here these past two days, that person in Yongshou Palace is unhappy and was throwing a tantrum at the Emperor today!"

Ziwei was startled. "Who did you hear that from?"

"Mingyue heard it from a little eunuch in Yongshou Palace." Little Swallow curled her lip. "If you ask me, she's too narrow-minded. The Emperor was just playing chess and discussing poetry with you, and she got jealous. Consort Ling is much more magnanimous..."

"Princess, be careful with your words," Ziwei interrupted quickly. "You cannot say such things lightly."

Little Swallow stuck out her tongue. "I know, I'm just telling you." She leaned closer and whispered, "But Ziwei, you must be careful. I heard that Concubine Chen... is not someone easy to deal with."

Ziwei nodded. "I understand."

Yanxi Palace.

Consort Ling had also heard about the incident at Yongshou Palace. After Lamei finished whispering her report, she said cautiously, "Your Ladyship, with Concubine Chen being so jealous, will the Emperor..."

Consort Ling shook her head. "The Emperor will not. Haven't you noticed that the Emperor has been going to the Shufang Studio these past two days to avoid the gossip of the court? Those old ministers keep saying the Emperor favors Yongshou Palace too much, so he is just going elsewhere to put on a show."

She paused, a bitter smile curling her lips. "I just didn't expect Concubine Chen to be unable to tolerate even that."

"Then that palace maid, Xia..."
