The day before the match, Jiang Rao tried on her altered riding outfit in Yongshou Palace.

It was a lotus-root-colored short outfit; the fabric was light, and the cuffs and trouser legs were cinched, making it convenient for movement without losing decorum.

Suxin helped her adjust it, worried: "Your Ladyship, are you really going to play? What if..."

"What if what?" Jiang Rao spun around in the mirror. "Don't worry, I know my limits."

She did know her limits—as a transmigrator, she knew Xiaoyanzi would shine in this match, and all she had to do was perform appropriately on the field, neither stealing the spotlight too much nor appearing too useless.

Most importantly... she really wanted to have some fun.

In Cining Palace, the Empress Dowager also heard the news.

"Consort Chen is participating in the cuju match?" The Empress Dowager twirled her prayer beads. "She certainly knows how to join in the fun."

Mother Sun said: "Empress Dowager, should this old servant go..."

"No need," the Empress Dowager said indifferently. "Let her go. I want to see what kind of tricks she can pull."

On the day of the match, the east lawn of the Imperial Garden was bustling with activity.

The stands had been set up long ago, and the consorts from various palaces arrived one after another. The Empress sat in the main seat accompanying the Empress Dowager, and Consort Ling, Consort Qing, and others were also present.

On the sidelines, the "Princess Team" and the "Prince Team" were warming up.

When Xiaoyanzi saw Jiang Rao arrive, she ran over excitedly: "Consort Chen! You really came!"

Jiang Rao was indeed dressed neatly today; the lotus-root-colored riding outfit accentuated her upright posture, and her hair was simply tied up with a white jade hairpin, looking fresh and elegant.

"Since I promised, I naturally wouldn't break my word," Jiang Rao laughed. "But the Princess will have to look after me, as I don't know how to play."

"Your Ladyship, don't worry!" Little Swallow patted her chest. "Just stand on the field; when the ball comes, just pass it to me!"

On the other side, the "Prince Team" was led by Yongqi, with Erkang and Ertai in the ranks, along with several guards skilled in wrestling.

Qianlong had also arrived. Seeing Jiang Rao in this attire, a flash of astonishment crossed his eyes, but he immediately frowned: "Rao'er, do you really have to go on the field?"

"The Emperor has already given his permission; you can't go back on your word now." Jiang Rao revealed a rare, mischievous smile.

Qianlong shook his head helplessly and took his seat in the main position.

The match was about to begin.

Little Swallow grabbed Jiang Rao's hand: "Your Ladyship, don't be nervous, just follow my lead!"

Jiang Rao nodded, though she felt a bit excited inside. In the three years since she had transmigrated, she had never been this "unrestrained."

As the referee gave the order, the match officially began.

chapters.title: A Good Show Begins, Surprise!
chapters.content:
On the east lawn of the Imperial Garden, the atmosphere had reached its peak.

The two teams stood on opposite sides. For the Princess Team, Little Swallow took the lead, followed closely by Ziwei. Jiang Rao was positioned slightly further back, flanked by Mingyue and Caixia. Liu Hong and several palace maids who knew some martial arts stood guard around Jiang Rao—this was per Qianlong's specific instructions to ensure the safety of Consort Chen.

Opposite them, the Prince Team was led by Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai, with several guards from the Imperial Wrestling Camp rubbing their hands in anticipation. Yongqi looked at Little Swallow with eyes full of smiles, then nodded slightly toward Jiang Rao as a greeting.

A gong sounded, and the match began!

Little Swallow charged out like a wild horse off its tether. Yongqi, prepared, moved to block her path. The two began to scramble for the ball, their movements so fast they were dazzling.

Jiang Rao stood in her position, following Little Swallow's prior instructions, moving her feet only slightly while keeping her eyes locked on the bouncing ball. The cheers and applause from the sidelines surged like waves. She took a deep breath, feeling a sense of excitement she hadn't experienced since her days on the school sports field.

"Your Ladyship, the ball is coming!" Liu Hong suddenly shouted.

It turned out that Little Swallow had made a feint, managed to steal the ball from under Yongqi's feet, and sent a long pass. The ball flew straight toward Jiang Rao, perfectly aimed. Everyone on and off the field was stunned—no one had expected Little Swallow to actually pass the ball to Consort Chen.

Jiang Rao was also startled, but her body reacted faster than her brain, and she instinctively lifted her foot to receive it. The ball hit her instep with a "thud," causing a slight sting, but it stopped steadily.

"Good!" someone shouted.

Jiang Rao didn't have time to think. Seeing Little Swallow charging forward, she mimicked the *cuju* moves from her memory, lightly flicking the ball with her instep toward Little Swallow. Though not professional, it was quite a decent attempt.

"Great pass, Your Ladyship!" Little Swallow cheered, caught the ball, and turned, only to have her path blocked by Erkang.

On the viewing stand, Qianlong had been gripping the armrests nervously, but seeing Jiang Rao's skillful reception and pass, he finally relaxed, a hint of a smile appearing in his eyes. The Empress sat beside the Empress Dowager, watching coldly, her handkerchief tightly clenched in her hand.

The match continued. Little Swallow truly gave it her all; at one point, she dove to save the ball and fell heavily to the ground, causing Yongqi's face to change with concern. Jiang Rao watched clearly from the field, sighing inwardly at the deep affection between these two bickering lovers.

When it was the Prince Team's turn to attack, Erkang launched a powerful shot. The ball flew straight toward the back of the Princess Team—exactly where Jiang Rao was standing. Jiang Rao instinctively tried to dodge, but heard Ziwei cry out: "Your Ladyship, watch out!" Ziwei then dove over, using her body to block the ball.

"Ziwei!" Little Swallow rushed over to help her up.

Jiang Rao hurried to crouch down: "Ziwei, are you alright?"

Ziwei shook her head, though her face was pale. The impact had been quite hard.

On the sidelines, seeing Ziwei injured, Erkang lost his composure, and his subsequent defense had several openings. Little Swallow seized the opportunity, bypassed two people, and made a beautiful final shot—

The ball hit the net!

"It's in! It's in!" The Princess Team cheered.

The gong signaling the end of the match sounded; the Princess Team had actually beaten the Prince Team. Little Swallow hugged Ziwei, laughing and jumping, while Yongqi, Erkang, and the others shook their heads with smiles and came forward to offer congratulations.

Jiang Rao stood in the crowd, breathing slightly hard, her cheeks flushed from the exercise. She raised a hand to wipe the fine sweat from her forehead, and as she turned, she met Qianlong's smiling gaze. She pursed her lips and smiled, a long-lost sense of exhilaration welling up inside her.

After the match, everyone moved to the viewing stand.

Little Swallow suddenly bowed to Qianlong with a mysterious air: "Imperial Father, the match is over, but we have another 'surprise' to present to you!"

Qianlong laughed: "Oh? What other tricks do you have?"

Little Swallow clapped her hands. More than twenty palace maids appeared, dressed in red, green, yellow, and blue, each holding a long colorful silk ribbon, running toward the field from all directions. They moved with light, well-trained steps and took their positions in the center of the field.

Music began to play softly, and the maids danced to the rhythm. The silk ribbons flew in the air, sometimes like a rainbow piercing the sun, sometimes like drifting clouds. Just as the crowd was dazzled, the maids suddenly gathered and then dispersed—

The ribbons were pulled taut, forming a giant character for "Longevity" (Shou) in the center of the field!

The "Shou" character had a red silk base with gold-threaded edges, shining brilliantly under the sun. The maids knelt and shouted in unison: "Wishing the Emperor a long and prosperous life!"

The entire arena was silent for a moment, then erupted in exclamations of wonder.

Qianlong was stunned. He looked at the giant "Shou" character made of silk, then at the sincere faces of the maids, and finally his gaze landed on Little Swallow and the others. These children must have put so much thought and training into this surprise for him.

The Empress Dowager was also moved. She nodded slowly and said softly: "I finally understand why the Emperor likes Little Swallow so much."

Consort Ling said gently: "Empress Dowager, although Princess Huanzhu is mischievous, her filial piety is sincere. Look at this performance she arranged; it is lively yet solemn—she truly put her heart into it."

Qianlong stood up, tears glistening in his eyes. He walked down from the stand to the field and personally helped Little Swallow and Yongqi, who were still kneeling, to their feet.

"Good children, your intentions, Imperial Father has received them." He added, "This is the most special birthday gift I have ever seen."

Little Swallow's eyes sparkled: "Does Imperial Father like it?"

"I like it, I like it very much." Qianlong looked at the giant "Shou" character. "This gift is more precious than any gold, silver, or jewelry."

Ziwei said warmly: "Your Majesty, these palace maids trained for ten full days. Little Swallow supervised them personally every day, not allowing a single mistake."

Qianlong patted Little Swallow's shoulder and turned to the crowd: "Today's *cuju* match was well-organized, and this birthday gift is even better! Seeing you brothers and sisters in harmony and the monarch and subjects of one mind—this is the true spirit of our Great Qing!"

Everyone shouted "Long live" in unison. Little Swallow smiled brightly, Ziwei's eyes filled with tears, and Yongqi, Erkang, and the others also wore smiles.

Jiang Rao stood among the concubines, looking at the giant silk "Shou" character, her heart filled with emotion. This was the most classic scene from *My Fair Princess*; no matter how many times she saw it, it was moving.

That night, Yongshou Palace.

Jiang Rao had just finished bathing and changed into a moon-white silk nightgown. Her long hair was loosely pinned up, and she was leaning on a couch, letting Suxin massage her legs.

"Is Your Ladyship tired today?" Suxin asked with a gentle touch. "I saw you running around quite a bit on the field."

"My legs are a bit sore," Jiang Rao said, closing her eyes. "But it felt great."

Just as she was speaking, an announcement came from outside: "The Emperor has arrived!"

Jiang Rao hurried to rise, but Qianlong had already strode in, waving his hand to excuse her from the formalities: "Stay seated. You're exhausted today, no need for ceremony."

He sat beside her and naturally took over Suxin's work, massaging her legs himself. Suxin tactfully withdrew.

"Your Majesty..." Jiang Rao felt a bit embarrassed.

"Don't move." Qianlong's technique was actually quite good. "On the field today, I saw you receive that ball; it was quite impressive."

Jiang Rao pursed her lips and smiled: "That was just a blind cat stumbling upon a dead mouse." She tilted her head to look at him: "Is the Emperor still angry at me for being so reckless?"

"Angry? Of course I'm angry." Qianlong deliberately put on a stern face. "A consort, running and jumping in front of so many people—what kind of decorum is that?"

Jiang Rao leaned closer, her voice soft: "Then punish me, Your Majesty."

Qianlong was amused by her expression and pinched her nose: "Punish you with what? Punish you by making you play another match for me tomorrow?"

"That won't do." Jiang Rao leaned into his arms: "My legs are still sore... Your Majesty, you don't know, it really hurts when the ball hits your feet."

Qianlong held her and said gently: "You're the one to blame, insisting on playing when you don't even know how. What if you had gotten hurt?"

"Isn't the Emperor here to protect me?" Jiang Rao said in a sweet, soft voice. "Besides, I've been stifled in the palace for so long; it was a rare opportunity to stretch my limbs... Your Majesty, you don't know, hearing everyone cheer today and seeing Little Swallow and the others so full of spirit, I felt like I had become several years younger myself."

Hearing this, Qianlong felt his heart soften. It was true; she had been in the palace for three years, always acting as the proper Consort Chen, and he had almost forgotten that she was just a girl in her early twenties.

"Very well, as long as you are happy." He sighed softly. "But in the future, if you want to exercise, just play in the courtyard of Yongshou Palace; there's no need to go out in public."

Jiang Rao rubbed against his chest: "I understand."

The two embraced quietly for a moment, and Jiang Rao suddenly remembered something and looked up: "Oh, right, Your Majesty, I also have a gift for you."

"Oh?" Qianlong raised an eyebrow. "Didn't I already receive a gift today?"

"That was Little Swallow and the others' intention; this is mine." Jiang Rao took a brocade box from the small drawer by the couch and handed it to Qianlong.

Qianlong opened it, and inside was a pair of glass paperweights. The glass was crystal clear, with fine gold foil swirling inside, shining brilliantly in the candlelight. Even more wonderful was the tiny inscription at the bottom of the paperweights; looking closely, it was a couplet:

*The four seas are at peace, bearing the purple aura,**The prosperous age of the nine provinces is bathed in the spring breeze.*

The handwriting was elegant and neat, clearly written by Jiang Rao herself.

"I made these a few days ago," Jiang Rao said softly. "The glass was scrap material I asked the Imperial Household Department to find, and the gold foil was melted down from old jewelry... I carved the characters myself; I ruined three pairs before I finally succeeded with this one."

Qianlong stroked the paperweights; they felt warm and smooth to the touch. As the Son of Heaven, he had seen every rare treasure imaginable, but this small pair of paperweights, made by her own hands, was more precious than any tribute.

"What made you think of making this?" his voice was gentle.

Jiang Rao leaned against his shoulder, her sleepiness gradually taking hold, and her voice became slurred: "The paperweight you use when reviewing memorials is getting old... These bright ones might be easier on your eyes, Your Majesty... And 'Peace Throughout the Four Seas,' 'Prosperity Across the Nine Provinces'—these are my wishes for you..."

As her voice trailed off, she had already fallen into a deep sleep.

Qianlong sat by the side of the couch, watching her for a long time. In the candlelight, her sleeping face was serene and beautiful, her eyelashes casting soft shadows beneath her eyes. He recalled how she looked on the polo field during the day—the lotus-root-colored riding habit accentuating her upright posture, the flash of surprise in her eyes when she caught the ball, and now, the slight upturn of her lips in her dreams.

He carefully placed the glass paperweight back into its brocade box, set it by her pillow, and then gently lifted her and placed her onto the bed.

The bed curtains were lowered, and moonlight filtered through the window lattice, spilling onto the pair of glass paperweights. The gold foil shimmered faintly in the darkness, as if holding the glimmer of the entire starry sky.

Qianlong lay down and pulled Jiang Rao into his arms. She leaned into him unconsciously, her breathing steady and long.

The sound of the watchman’s drum drifted from afar outside the window; the night was deep.

Yongshou Palace was tranquil, with only the moonlight flowing silently, guarding the warmth of the room.

chapters.title: Always Need to Collect Some Interest
chapters.content:
Inside the Imperial Study, the candles were burning bright.

Qianlong sat behind the sandalwood desk, several memorials spread out before him, though he did not hold the vermilion brush. High officials like Ji Xiaolan, Fuheng, and E'min stood in attendance, with Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai also present.

"I have been reviewing reports from various regions these past few days, and I keep feeling..." Qianlong tapped his fingertips lightly on the desk, "that the phrase 'the country is prosperous and the people are at peace' is written too easily."

Ji Xiaolan stroked his beard and said, "Your Majesty is wise. What is presented in the memorials is all filtered through layers of bureaucracy. Without visiting these places in person, it is truly difficult to glimpse the real state of the common people."

Fuheng bowed, "Is Your Majesty intending to go on an inspection tour?"

Qianlong raised his eyes, his gaze sweeping over the group: "I do have that intention. Not a grand Southern Inspection Tour, but a private visit to see the true state of the Qing Empire in the vicinity of the capital."

E'min hurriedly said, "Your Majesty is of golden stature; this matter requires careful deliberation..."

"My mind is made up." Qianlong waved his hand to interrupt, "Erkang, tell me, if we were to travel privately, how should it be arranged?"

Erkang stepped forward and pondered, "In reply to Your Majesty, I believe we could pose as wealthy merchants from the capital. Your Majesty would naturally be the Master, the Fifth Prince could pose as the Young Master, and Ertai and I could act as personal bodyguards. Little Swallow and Princess Ziwei could pose as maids. Master Ji is knowledgeable and could pose as a private secretary. We could also select a dozen imperial experts to pose as house guards and servants."

Qianlong nodded, "That is a sound proposal. Let it be arranged as such. We shall depart in three days for the area around Tanzhe Temple, west of the capital."

Yongqi’s eyes shone with excitement, "Imperial Father, will you be taking... which consort from the harem along? If we are to pose as a wealthy merchant family, it is only natural for the wife to accompany him."

Erkang added, "Indeed. Having female family members along would make it look more like an ordinary wealthy household."

A hint of a smile flashed in Qianlong’s eyes, but he deliberately mused, "This... I have my own considerations. I will certainly take one; you will know who it is when the time comes."

Ji Xiaolan laughed, "Your Majesty is keeping us in suspense."

"You may all go and prepare now." Qianlong waved his hand, "Remember, this matter is confidential and must not be leaked. Affairs of the court will be temporarily handled by Prince He."

"We obey your decree."

As the group withdrew, Yongqi couldn't help but ask Erkang in a low voice, "Who do you think Imperial Father will take? Consort Ling?"

Erkang shook his head, "The Emperor's heart is hard to fathom. However, Consort Ling has a gentle nature and is close to Little Swallow and the others, so she would be the most suitable candidate."

In Shufang Studio, Little Swallow was playing chess with Ziwei.

"Oh no, I lost again!" Little Swallow pushed the chess pieces away, "Ziwei, you are too amazing, you win every time!"

Ziwei smiled gently, "It is because you are too impatient, always trying to win in a single move."

As they were laughing and talking, Yongqi rushed in, his face full of joy, "Little Swallow! Ziwei! There is wonderful news!"

Little Swallow jumped up, "What good news? Is Imperial Father going to reward us?"

"Better than a reward!" Yongqi lowered his voice, "Imperial Father is going on a private inspection tour! And he is taking us with him!"

"Leave the palace?!" Little Swallow shrieked, then covered her mouth, her eyes wide, "Really? We can leave the palace?"

Ziwei also stood up excitedly, the chess pieces falling to the floor, "Fifth Prince, is this true?"

"Absolutely!" Yongqi laughed, "Imperial Father will pose as the Master, I will be the Young Master, Erkang and Ertai will be the guards, and you and Ziwei will pose as maids. Oh, right," he paused, "Imperial Father is also taking a consort to pose as the mistress."

Little Swallow’s eyes lit up, "Consort Ling! It must be Consort Ling! Consort Ling loves us the most!"

Ziwei nodded as well, tears welling in her eyes, "If Consort Ling can come with us, the journey... the journey will surely be well-cared for. And..." she held Little Swallow’s hand, "once we are out of the palace, we will be one step closer to our goal."

Little Swallow nodded heavily, "Right! Don't worry, Ziwei, this time out of the palace, I will definitely find a way to help you..."

"Little Swallow!" Ziwei hurriedly stopped her, glancing at Yongqi.

Yongqi smiled, "I understand. Don't worry, I will keep an eye out during the trip as well." He said seriously, "But this matter is confidential; do not let word get out. We depart at the hour of the rabbit in three days from the side gate of the Shenwu Gate."

Little Swallow was so happy she spun around the room, "We're leaving the palace! We're leaving the palace! Jinsuo! Jinsuo, come quickly! We're leaving the palace!"

Jinsuo came in from the outer room, and upon hearing they could leave the palace, she was so happy she wiped away tears.

Yongqi gave a few more instructions before leaving. As soon as he left, Little Swallow grabbed Ziwei’s hand, "Ziwei, this is a rare opportunity, we must seize it!"

Ziwei nodded firmly, her eyes full of determination.

In Yongshou Palace, Jiang Rao had just finished listening to Suxin’s report.

"A private inspection tour?" She put down her embroidery hoop, a glint in her eyes, "The Emperor is leaving the palace?"

"Yes, departing in three days, heading west of the capital." Suxin whispered, "I heard the Fifth Prince, Princess Huanzhu, and the others are all going. He is also taking a consort to pose as the mistress."

Jiang Rao stood up and walked to the window. In the night, the silhouette of the palace walls looked exceptionally stern under the moonlight.

She knew the original story—in this private tour, Qianlong did not take any concubines. But things were different now; she was the Noble Consort Chen, the most favored consort of the past three years. And... she really wanted to see the world outside the palace.

Having been in the palace for three years, this Forbidden City was like a magnificent cage. Every day was spent paying respects, admiring flowers, and watching plays—the life was wealthy but dull. What was the world outside the palace walls like? The clamor of the marketplace, the wind in the fields, the smoke and life of ordinary people... these were things she only had in her memories.

"Suxin," she turned around, her eyes shining with resolve, "Has the Emperor flipped a name tablet tonight?"

"Not yet. But Eunuch Li just sent word that the Emperor will come by later."

Jiang Rao nodded and walked to the vanity to sit down.

"Bring me that water-red nightgown." She said softly.

"Your Ladyship..." Suxin hesitated, "Are you planning to..."

"I am going." Jiang Rao looked at herself in the mirror, a hint of coquettishness flashing in her eyes, "Since the Emperor didn't say he was taking a consort, I will make him take me."

At the third quarter of the hour of the dog (8:45 PM), Qianlong stepped into Yongshou Palace.

As soon as he entered, he smelled a faint scent of jasmine. Turning past the screen, he saw Jiang Rao leaning against the couch, wearing a water-red satin nightgown that made her skin look like snow. Her long hair was loosely pinned up with a jade hairpin, and a few strands fell by her neck. She held a book in her hand, her profile soft and beautiful in the candlelight.

"Your Majesty is here." She raised her eyes, her gaze full of charm.

Qianlong sat beside her and naturally wrapped his arm around her shoulders, "What are you reading?"

"Just a casual book." Jiang Rao leaned into his arms, her fingertips tracing circles on his chest, "Does Your Majesty have something on your mind today?"

Qianlong took her hand, "I am leaving the palace in three days."

Jiang Rao raised her eyes, showing surprise at the right moment, "Leaving the palace? Where is Your Majesty going?"

"A private inspection, to see the area west of the capital." Qianlong looked at her, "Why, do you want to go too?"

Jiang Rao sat up, her eyes full of longing, "I do! I dream of leaving the palace to see the world!" She tugged at Qianlong’s sleeve, her voice soft and sweet, "Take me with you, Your Majesty, please? I promise to be good and will never cause trouble."

Qianlong deliberately put on a stern face, "Nonsense. I am going to observe the lives of the people; what kind of decorum would it be to bring a consort?"

"Why can't you?" Jiang Rao wouldn't give up, pressing herself against him and wrapping her arms around his neck, "You are posing as a Master, and I will pose as the Mistress—isn't that only natural? Besides," she leaned into his ear, her breath like an orchid, "can you bear to leave me alone in the palace?"

Qianlong felt a surge of heat, but he kept his composure, "There are so many concubines in the palace; if I take you and not others, it will inevitably invite gossip."

"Then you can take me secretly." Jiang Rao’s lips were almost touching his earlobe, "I can dress as a man, or as a maid... as long as I can leave the palace with you, anything will do..."

Her hand wandered into his robes, her fingertips warm. Qianlong’s breath hitched, and he grabbed her wrist, "You girl, you are becoming more and more daring."

"It's because you spoil me." Jiang Rao smiled coquettishly, simply straddling his lap and holding his face in her hands, "Take me with you... I am so bored in the palace, I’m almost sick from it... Please indulge me, Your Majesty, won't you?"

In the candlelight, her eyes were shimmering, her red lips slightly parted, and the ribbons of her nightgown had loosened at some point, revealing her fair shoulders and neck.

Qianlong’s Adam’s apple bobbed, and finally, he couldn't hold back, laughing in a low voice, "If I say no, will you make a scene all night?"

"Then I will keep begging until you agree." Jiang Rao said, leaning down to kiss his lips.

The kiss was deliberately provocative, soft and lingering. Qianlong held her waist and deepened the kiss. When it ended, both were breathless.

"Fine." Qianlong pressed his forehead against hers, his voice hoarse, "I actually... intended to take you all along."

Jiang Rao was stunned, "You intended to take me from the start?"

"What else?" Qianlong took a piece of paper from his sleeve, "Look, this is the identity I prepared for you—Madam Ai, the wife of the wealthy merchant Master Ai from the capital. The clothes have already been made."

Jiang Rao took the paper, looking at the elegant handwriting, both surprised and delighted, "Your Majesty... you were teasing me!"

"You were the one who started teasing me first." Qianlong laughed and pinched her nose, "But since you delivered yourself to my door..." He picked her up, "I must collect some interest."

The bed curtains fell, and the room was filled with spring.

The next day, Shufang Studio.

Xiao Yanzi was excitedly packing her luggage when Yongqi arrived again, this time with a rather strange expression on his face.

"Fifth Prince, what is it this time?" Xiao Yanzi asked.

Yongqi scratched his head. "Well... the choice for the 'Madam' has been made."

"It’s Consort Ling, right?" Xiao Yanzi said without looking up. "I’ve already thought it through. I have so much to talk to Consort Ling about on the road, and I want her to tell me stories from outside the palace..."

"It’s not Consort Ling," Yongqi interrupted. "It’s Consort Chen."

"What?!" Xiao Yanzi jerked her head up. "Consort Chen? How could it be Consort Chen?"

Ziwei also put down the clothes in her hands, looking somewhat surprised. "Fifth Prince, is this the Emperor’s decision?"

Yongqi nodded. "His Majesty decided personally. He said Consort Chen is young, so she is more suitable to play the role of the Madam. Consort Ling must remain in the palace to assist in managing the affairs of the six palaces."

Xiao Yanzi plopped down and pouted. "How could this happen... Although I think Consort Chen is a nice person after the cuju match, but... but we are much closer to Consort Ling. Consort Ling is so gentle and treats us so well, just like a real mother..."

Ziwei gently persuaded her, "Xiao Yanzi, don't say that. Consort Chen is also a very good person. Since the Emperor chose her, he must have his reasons. Besides," she paused, "the fact that Consort Chen was willing to help us during the cuju match shows that she is kind-hearted. We should just get along well on this journey."

"I know..." Xiao Yanzi sighed. "I’m just a little disappointed. I had hoped to get closer to Consort Ling on the road, and now it’s been changed to Consort Chen... Although she is quite nice, I just feel there’s a barrier between us."

Jin Suo whispered, "Gege, Consort Chen is actually quite amiable. When I ran into her in the Imperial Garden last time, she even asked if Ziwei Gege’s injuries had healed."

"Really?" Xiao Yanzi’s eyes lit up. "She still remembers that Ziwei was injured?"

"She remembered it very clearly, and even had Aunt Suxin send over some high-quality ointment for bruises," Jin Suo said.

Xiao Yanzi’s expression softened a little. "Well... that’s not bad. Anyway, it’s only for a few months, we’ll just get along."

Yongqi smiled. "That’s right. Consort Chen’s personality is actually quite lively; you’ll know once you spend more time together."

Three days later, at the first quarter of the Mao hour (5:00 AM).

The side gate of the Shenwu Gate opened quietly. Three green-tented carriages drove out one after another, each escorted by several guards.

In the lead carriage, the Qianlong Emperor wore a dark blue silk robe with a black vest over it, looking every bit the wealthy merchant. Sitting beside him was a young lady in a lotus-root pink cheongsam embroidered with lotus vines, covered by a moon-white vest. Her hair was styled in a lazy bun, adorned with a kingfisher-feather hairpin—it was Jiang Rao.

She gently lifted a corner of the curtain, watching the palace walls recede, her eyes shining with excitement.

In the carriage behind, Xiao Yanzi, Ziwei, and Jin Suo were disguised as maids. The three of them crowded by the carriage window, curiously watching the street scene outside. Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai rode alongside as guards, Ji Xiaolan sat in the third carriage, and a dozen imperial guards disguised as bodyguards and servants followed.

Xiao Yanzi looked at the carriage in front and whispered to Ziwei, "Look, Consort Chen’s outfit really makes her look like a wealthy merchant’s wife."

Ziwei smiled. "The Consort is naturally beautiful with a graceful temperament, so she naturally looks the part when dressed up."

The procession drove out of the Imperial City and passed through the Inner City, where the hustle and bustle of the Outer City gradually reached them. The cries of breakfast vendors, the sound of wheels rolling over stone slabs, the chatter of early risers... all wove together into a lively symphony of city life.

Jiang Rao lowered the curtain and turned to look at the Qianlong Emperor, her eyes sparkling. "Your Majesty, we have really left the palace."

The Qianlong Emperor squeezed her hand and smiled. "Call me 'Master'."

"Yes, Master." Jiang Rao followed suit, her eyes filled with smiles.

The carriage passed through the city gate. In the morning light, the official road west of the capital unfolded before them. Distant mountains held hints of dark green, nearby waters were veiled in mist, and the spring breeze carried the scent of soil and flowers, blowing against their faces.

A journey in disguise had officially begun.

And as for what kind of stories this journey would bring, at this moment, it had only just begun.

chapters.title: Beating Drums in Meihua Town
chapters.content:
The procession traveled along the official road west of the capital for half a day, arriving at a lively small town by midday.

The stone tablet at the entrance of the town was carved with three large characters: Meihua Town (Plum Blossom Town). Although it was not the season for plum blossoms to bloom, plum trees could be seen everywhere in the town; one could imagine it must be a magnificent sight in winter.

"Master, Madam, ahead is Meihua Town," Ji Xiaolan reported from outside the carriage. "There seems to be a temple fair in the town today, it’s very lively."

The Qianlong Emperor lifted the carriage curtain to look. He saw people coming and going in the town, with vendors gathered everywhere—it was indeed the atmosphere of a temple fair. He turned to look at Jiang Rao. "Would you like to go down and walk around?"

Jiang Rao’s eyes sparkled. "Yes!"

The procession stopped in a quiet spot outside the town. Everyone changed into more ordinary clothes. The Qianlong Emperor remained dressed as a master, while Jiang Rao changed into a lotus-root pink cotton dress with a moon-white vest, wearing only a silver hairpin in her hair, making her look even more elegant and simple. Xiao Yanzi, Ziwei, and Jin Suo remained dressed as maids, Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai were dressed as young gentlemen, Ji Xiaolan played the role of an old steward, and the guards dispersed to protect them from the shadows.

As soon as they entered the town, Xiao Yanzi looked around like a wild horse let loose. The street vendors selling sugar figurines, blowing sugar art, and molding dough figures were all new and exciting to her. Although Ziwei was also curious, she kept to the rules and followed closely behind the Qianlong Emperor’s group.

Suddenly, deafening gongs and drums sounded from ahead.

"What’s that sound?" Xiao Yanzi stretched her neck to look.

They saw a simple stage set up in the open space in the center of the town. The crowd was packed three layers deep around the stage, and a dozen men on the stage were beating large drums, the sound thunderous. Even better, there was a team of women at the side of the stage holding small waist drums, dancing and beating them in time with the rhythm, their movements uniform and quite beautiful.

"This is the waist drum dance!" Ji Xiaolan stroked his beard and smiled. "Meihua Town always has this performance during temple fairs. Originally, it was to pray for good weather, but now it has become a form of entertainment."

Xiao Yanzi was eager and pulled Ziwei’s hand. "Ziwei, look! They are playing so energetically! Shall we go and try it too?"

The Qianlong Emperor smiled. "If you want to go, go ahead, but don't cause any trouble."

"Thank you, Master!" Xiao Yanzi pulled Ziwei and tried to squeeze into the crowd.

Jiang Rao was also moved. The waist drums were played joyfully, the rhythm intense, making one want to move along with the beat. She quietly tugged at the Qianlong Emperor’s sleeve and whispered, "Master, this concubine... I also want to go and see."

The Qianlong Emperor raised an eyebrow. "You know how to play the drums too?"

"If I don't know, I can learn." Jiang Rao’s eyes were filled with pleading. "It’s rare that we’re out..."

Seeing her eager look, the Qianlong Emperor found it amusing. "Go ahead, be careful."

Jiang Rao was overjoyed and said to Xiao Yanzi, "Xiao Yanzi, let’s go together!"

Xiao Yanzi didn't expect this Consort Chen to be so open-minded. She was stunned for a moment, then smiled. "Okay, okay! Madam, come quickly!"

The three of them squeezed into the crowd. The women playing the waist drums at the side of the stage saw several well-dressed ladies and young misses approaching, and hearing that they wanted to learn, they enthusiastically made room and handed them waist drums.

"Hold it like this, that’s right," an older sister taught Jiang Rao the posture for holding the drum. "Your wrists need to be flexible, beat like this..."

Jiang Rao learned earnestly. Although she had never played a waist drum, she had learned some dance in a university club before crossing over, and her sense of rhythm was not bad. Before long, she was able to keep up with the simple drum beats.

Xiao Yanzi learned even faster. She was naturally lively and active, and soon she was playing quite decently, even adding some fancy moves, drawing cheers from the people around.

Ziwei was gentler, playing softly, but it had its own unique charm.

The drum beats became faster and faster, and the three of them gradually entered the zone. Jiang Rao forgot about palace rules and etiquette, forgot her identity as Consort Chen, and beat the drums to her heart's content, a happy smile blooming on her face. The sunlight shone on her, beads of sweat seeped from her forehead, her cheeks were flushed from the exercise, and her eyes were shining brightly.

The Qianlong Emperor watched from the edge of the crowd, his eyes full of doting as he saw Jiang Rao’s joyful appearance.

Yongqi smiled in a low voice, "Imperial Father, the Madam plays really well."

The Qianlong Emperor nodded. "She learns everything quickly."

As they were speaking, the drum sound stopped abruptly. An old man stepped onto the stage and bowed, saying, "Dear fellow villagers, the waist drum performance ends here. Next is our Meihua Town’s annual 'Archery for Marriage' event. The rules remain the same—whoever hits the bullseye from a hundred paces away can take my granddaughter as his wife!"

The crowd below exploded. A young girl walked out from behind the stage, sixteen or seventeen years old, with almond eyes and peach-blossom cheeks. Although she was dressed in simple cloth and a wooden hairpin, she could not hide her beauty. She stood shyly behind the old man, lowering her head and fiddling with the corner of her clothes.

The old man ordered someone to set up an archery target and took out three bows and arrows. "Anyone under thirty who is unmarried can give it a try!"

Several young men were eager to try, but their archery skills were poor; they either missed the target or barely hit it, far from the bullseye.

Xiao Yanzi felt her hands itching and poked Yongqi. "Fifth... Young Master, go and try! Your archery is so good!"

Yongqi shook his head quickly. "No, no, this is not a joke to be made."

Erkang and Ertai also smiled without saying a word.

The old man asked three times, and no one responded. Just as he was about to announce that there were no takers this year, a crisp voice suddenly rang out from the crowd: "Let me try!"

Everyone looked over and saw it was a young lady—it was Xiao Yanzi.

The Qianlong Emperor frowned. "Nonsense!"

But Xiao Yanzi had already jumped onto the stage and bowed to the old man. "Old sir, can a woman try?"

The old man was stunned. "This... it has always been men..."

"What’s wrong with women?" Xiao Yanzi said righteously. "You didn't say women couldn't try! Besides, if I hit the target, I’ll just consider it finding a sister for your granddaughter, isn't that good?"

The crowd below burst into laughter. The young girl couldn't help but cover her mouth and laugh.

The old man was left speechless by her words and had no choice but to say, "Then... please, young lady."

Xiao Yanzi drew the bow and nocked an arrow, her posture surprisingly standard. Yongqi and the others knew she had some martial arts foundation, but they didn't know how her archery was. They saw her squint and aim, and as she released her hand—

The arrow broke through the air and hit the bullseye with a "thud"!

The whole place was silent for a moment, then erupted into cheers.

Xiao Yanzi was triumphant and was about to speak when a hoarse voice suddenly came from below the stage: "Good archery, young lady! However, I have a couplet. If you can answer it, only then will you truly be the winner."

Everyone looked over and saw an old man selling tea eggs. His hair and beard were white, his clothes were tattered, but there was a light of wisdom in his eyes.

The old man quickly said, "This is the old scholar in town; he is very learned."

Xiao Yanzi said readily, "Please give the couplet, old sir!"

The old scholar said slowly, "The first line is: 'Water-land islet, islet stops the boat, the boat moves but the islet does not.'"

Xiao Yanzi blinked. How could she answer this? Just as she was getting anxious, Ziwei had already walked onto the stage and whispered a few words in her ear.

Xiao Yanzi’s eyes lit up and she said loudly, "The second line is: 'Heavenly Heart Pavilion, pavilion drops the pigeon, the pigeon flies but the pavilion does not!'"

The old scholar’s eyes lit up: "A fine match! The young lady has another couplet: 'Driving a single flat-bottomed boat, rowing with two oars, setting three or four sails, carrying five or six guests, passing Seven-Mile Shoal, arriving at Eight-Mile Lake, having already left Jiujiang by ten miles.'"

This couplet was longer and more difficult. Xiaoyanzi looked to Ziwei for help. Ziwei pondered for a moment, then whispered a few words in her ear.

Xiaoyanzi said loudly: "The second line is: 'Opening a two-person small shop, setting one table, putting out seven or eight bowls, serving three or five guests, brewing Liu'an tea, paying fifty coins, and getting back four yuan with three dimes still owed!'"

Before the words had even faded, the whole crowd cheered. The old scholar clapped his hands and laughed: "Wonderful! Wonderful! The young lady’s wit is sharp; this old man is impressed!"

The old man and his granddaughter also stepped forward to express their thanks. Although this marriage proposal did not come to fruition, it resulted in a wonderful story.

Qianlong watched from below the stage, his eyes full of smiles. These two girls—one clever, one intelligent—were truly a perfect match.

Jiang Rao stood beside Qianlong, watching the vibrant Xiaoyanzi and the gentle, smiling Ziwei on the stage, feeling deeply moved. This was the charm of *My Fair Princess*; no matter how many times one watched it, one would always be touched by this vivid vitality.

After the excitement died down, the group returned to their carriages.

Xiaoyanzi was still excitedly talking about what had just happened: "Ziwei, you are truly amazing! I couldn't have matched that couplet even if I had tried for three days!"

Ziwei said softly: "It was your archery that was good; I was just joining in the fun."

Qianlong smiled: "Did you have a good time today?"

"Yes, very much!" Xiaoyanzi nodded repeatedly, then looked at Jiang Rao: "Madam, your drumming was also wonderful!"

Jiang Rao laughed: "It was the ladies in town who taught me well." She turned to Qianlong, her eyes shining: "Master, the common folk are truly interesting. It’s even livelier than in the palace... than at home during the New Year."

Qianlong knew she had almost let something slip, so he shook his head with a smile: "As long as you are happy. It is getting late, and we must continue our journey."

Everyone boarded the carriages again, and the convoy continued westward.

Inside the carriage, Jiang Rao leaned against Qianlong and whispered: "Master, today was truly happy."

Qianlong held her: "As long as you are happy. However," he said sternly, "you must not expose yourself like that again next time. Your status is different, after all."

Jiang Rao knew he was referring to the drumming and nodded obediently: "This concubine understands."

The convoy drove out of Meihua Town, leaving the lively drumbeats and laughter behind. Ahead, the mountain road wound its way forward, and she wondered what other scenery awaited them.

chapters.title: Seeing Injustice on the Road
chapters.content:
After the convoy left Meihua Town, it continued westward along the mountain road. The path grew narrower, with lush trees on both sides and the occasional sound of birds, making it even more secluded.

Inside the carriage, Jiang Rao leaned on Qianlong’s shoulder for a nap. Although she had enjoyed the waist-drum dance, she was indeed tired. Qianlong gently stroked her hair, his eyes filled with doting affection.

After traveling for about another hour, a commotion suddenly came from ahead.

"What is going on?" Qianlong lifted the carriage curtain.

They saw a group of people gathered at a bend in the mountain road. A pot-bellied middle-aged man dressed in silk was directing several men who looked like servants to push and shove an elderly couple. The old couple, dressed in rags, knelt on the ground, kowtowing incessantly.

"Master, please have mercy and give us a few more days! The harvest was poor this year, and we truly cannot pay that much rent!" The old man’s voice was hoarse and full of pleading.

The fat master kicked the old man away: "A grace period? If I give you a grace period, who will give me one? If you don't pay the rent today, I’ll take those few acres of poor land you have as collateral!"

Xiaoyanzi had already jumped off the carriage and squeezed into the crowd. Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai followed closely behind.

"Stop!" Xiaoyanzi shouted, "Bullying the elderly in broad daylight—what kind of skill is that!"

The fat master squinted at Xiaoyanzi. Seeing that she was dressed in fine clothes but looked like a maid, he didn't take her seriously: "Where did this wild girl come from, meddling in other people's business! This is my family matter; it’s not your place to interfere!"

"When one sees injustice on the road, anyone can intervene!" Xiaoyanzi put her hands on her hips: "Tell me, how much rent do they owe you?"

The fat master held up three fingers: "Three taels of silver! This has been overdue for three months!"

The old woman cried: "Young lady, it’s not that we don't want to pay, but there was a spring drought this year, and the harvest is only half of what it usually is. We two old folks rely on these few acres to survive. Please, Master Liang, have mercy and reduce the rent..."

"Reduce it?" Master Liang sneered, "Rules are rules! If you can't pay the rent, you pay with the land!"

Just as Xiaoyanzi was about to take out money, Ziwei stepped forward and said gently: "Sir, seeing that this elderly couple is frail and weak, could you please show some leniency? We are willing to pay the rent for them."

As she spoke, Ziwei took out three taels of silver and handed them over.

Master Liang took the silver and weighed it, but he was not satisfied: "This is only for three months of rent. According to the rules, overdue rent incurs interest. With principal and interest, it comes to five taels!"

"You!" Xiaoyanzi was furious: "You just said three taels, and now it’s five? This is extortion!"

Master Liang gave a cold, insincere smile: "The contract is written in black and white—overdue rent incurs compound interest. If you don't like it, go sue me at the county magistrate's office!"

The surrounding villagers whispered among themselves, but no one dared to step forward. It seemed this Master Liang had considerable influence in the area.

Qianlong saw everything clearly from inside the carriage, and his face darkened. He signaled for Ji Xiaolan to step forward.

Ji Xiaolan understood. He walked out of the crowd, stroked his beard, and said: "Sir, it is better to be forgiving when one can. The couple is advanced in years; why must you be so relentless?"

Seeing Ji Xiaolan’s distinguished demeanor, Master Liang restrained himself slightly but remained stubborn: "The old gentleman is mistaken. Paying debts is only right and proper. If I were to forgive everyone, how would I conduct my business?"

Just as they were at a stalemate, the sound of gongs clearing the way came from afar. An official sedan chair swayed toward them, and the bailiffs beside it shouted: "The County Magistrate is here—make way, make way—"

The crowd dispersed to clear a path. The sedan chair stopped, and a thin, gaunt man wearing a seventh-rank official uniform and sporting a goatee stepped out—it was the local county magistrate.

As soon as Master Liang saw the magistrate, he changed his expression, hurried over, and bowed: "Your Honor, you have arrived just in time! These unruly people are behind on their rent and have brought outsiders to cause trouble. You must uphold justice for me!"

The magistrate scanned the scene, his gaze lingering for a moment on Qianlong and his party. Seeing their fine clothes and distinguished air, he weighed the situation in his mind.

"What is going on?" the magistrate asked with a stern face.

The old man kowtowed hurriedly: "Your Honor, please see the truth! It is not that I do not want to pay, but the harvest this year was truly poor..."

"A poor harvest is no excuse!" the magistrate interrupted, "The contract is here; debts must be paid. Master Liang is a major taxpayer in this county; naturally, I must look after his affairs." He then looked at Qianlong and the others: "Who are you people? Why are you gathering here to cause trouble?"

Yongqi stepped forward, neither humble nor pushy: "Sir, we are just passing through. Seeing that the elderly couple is pitiful, we wanted to help. Master Liang is raising the price on the spot, turning three taels into five—this is truly unjust."

The magistrate narrowed his eyes: "Justice? I am the justice! If you continue to stir up trouble, don't blame me for being impolite!"

Xiaoyanzi was so angry she wanted to rush forward, but Erkang held her back.

At this moment, Qianlong slowly stepped out of the carriage. Although he was wearing the clothes of an ordinary wealthy merchant, the aura he had cultivated over years as an emperor made him naturally imposing.

The magistrate was startled when he saw him step out, sensing that this person had an extraordinary background.

"Magistrate," Qianlong spoke, his voice steady, "According to the *Great Qing Legal Code*, for private loans, the monthly interest shall not exceed three percent. For three months of arrears, the interest should not exceed three *qian*. Master Liang demanding two taels of interest is already a violation of the law. As a local official, not only do you fail to correct this, but you also aid in the wrongdoing. What kind of logic is that?"

The magistrate was left speechless and argued stubbornly: "You... who are you? How dare you question my judgment!"

"Who I am is not important," Qianlong said calmly, "What is important is that you have studied the classics and wear the court’s robes, yet you do not act for the people, but instead collude with corrupt merchants to oppress them. Can you sit securely in your official chair?"

The magistrate’s face changed drastically. Just as he was about to lash out, Master Liang shouted first: "How bold! Daring to be disrespectful to the Magistrate! Men, take them down!"

Several bailiffs stepped forward.

Erkang and Ertai immediately blocked Qianlong. Yongqi also shielded Xiaoyanzi and Ziwei.

"Wait!" Ji Xiaolan suddenly said in a loud voice, "Magistrate, do you recognize this?"

He took out a token, gleaming with gold, with the words "Imperial Attendant" engraved on it.

As soon as the magistrate saw the token, his legs went weak, and he fell to his knees with a thud: "I... this humble official was blind! I did not know that an official from the Imperial presence had arrived!"

Although Master Liang did not recognize the token, seeing the magistrate kneel, he knew he had caused a great disaster and knelt down as well, trembling all over.

The surrounding villagers, seeing this, knelt down one after another, whispering in shock.

Qianlong walked up to the magistrate, looking down at him: "Now, can you judge the case properly?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" The magistrate kowtowed like a pestle pounding garlic, "This official will certainly handle it impartially! Liang Youde has oppressed the people and raised prices on the spot. According to the law... according to the law, he shall be punished with thirty strokes of the cane and fined fifty taels of silver! The overdue rent shall be calculated based on the actual amount owed, and no interest shall be added!"

Master Liang said with a mournful face: "Your Honor..."

"Shut up!" the magistrate barked, "One more word, and the fine will be increased!"

Only then did Qianlong nod and look at the elderly couple: "Please rise. The rent you owe will be waived by this Master Liang. Furthermore, of the fifty taels he is fined, half will compensate you, and the other half will be distributed to other affected farmers in the village. Is that acceptable?"

The old couple expressed their deepest gratitude, kowtowing repeatedly.

With the matter settled, Qianlong and his party boarded their carriages again. The magistrate knelt and watched the convoy depart before wiping the cold sweat from his brow and kicking Master Liang: "You almost got me killed!"

The convoy continued forward.

Inside the carriage, Jiang Rao said softly: "Master was truly imposing just now."

Qianlong shook his head: "It was not being imposing; it was heartbreak. Under the Emperor’s feet, in the capital region, there are still such corrupt officials and heartless, wealthy bullies. If I hadn't seen it with my own eyes today, I..." He paused, "I would not have known the suffering of the people was this severe."

Jiang Rao took his hand: "Master has already upheld justice for the people. But the world is so large, I fear there are still many such cases."

Qianlong was silent for a moment, then suddenly said: "Ji Xiaolan."

"This subject is here," Ji Xiaolan’s voice came from outside the carriage.

"Make a note: After we return to the capital, thoroughly investigate the performance of officials in all counties of the capital region. Anyone found oppressing the people or engaging in corruption and breaking the law shall be punished without leniency."

"This subject obeys the decree."

The convoy turned around a mountain pass, and the view ahead suddenly opened up. In a wide valley, smoke curled from chimneys, and houses stood in orderly rows—it was another small town.

Ji Xiaolan reported from outside: "Master, ahead is Qingxi Town. It is getting late; shall we rest here?"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao and, seeing that she looked tired, said: "Let us rest here for the night."

The caravan entered Qingxi Town. The town was smaller than Meihua Town, yet it felt more tranquil. A clear stream flowed through the town, its waters murmuring, with weeping willows swaying along the banks.

They found a clean inn to stay in. Xiaoyanzi and Ziwei shared a room, Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai shared another, while the Qianlong Emperor and Jiang Rao naturally occupied the premium rooms. Ji Xiaolan and the imperial guards were distributed among the remaining rooms.

At dinner, everyone ate in the inn’s main hall. Although the meal was simple, everyone was hungry after the day’s events and ate with great relish.

Xiaoyanzi was still talking about what happened during the day: "That Master Liang is truly detestable! And that magistrate—you could tell at a glance he was no good! If it weren't for the Master being there, we really wouldn't have known what to do with them."

Yongqi smiled and said, "That is why the Em... why the Master brought us out—to see the true face of the Great Qing Empire."

Ziwei said softly, "It is just hard on the common people. If we hadn't encountered them today, who knows how much that old couple would have suffered."

Jiang Rao listened silently, feeling deeply moved. She knew this was merely the tip of the iceberg. Under the "Prosperous Age of Qianlong," there were still countless stories like this one.

After dinner, everyone returned to their rooms.

Once Jiang Rao had finished bathing, she sat by the window, combing her long hair. Outside, the moonlight was like water, the sound of the stream was constant, and the occasional bark of a dog only highlighted the stillness of the rural night.

Qianlong embraced her from behind: "What are you thinking about?"

"Thinking about today's events," Jiang Rao leaned into his arms. "Master, do you think there are many more common people in this world suffering like that, with no one to know?"

Qianlong remained silent for a long time before saying, "That is why I must come out to see, to listen, and to know. Rao'er," he turned her around, "you were smiling so happily when you were beating the drum in Meihua Town today. But in the palace, I rarely see you smile like that."

Jiang Rao looked up at him: "There are too many rules in the palace; your concubine does not dare."

"It is I who have constrained you," Qianlong sighed softly. "When we return to the palace, if you feel stifled, come to the Hall of Mental Cultivation to keep me company often. Go to the Imperial Garden or the Changchun Garden whenever you wish; you need not always be confined to the Yongshou Palace."

Moonlight filtered through the window paper, casting a glow over the two of them. From afar came the sound of the night watchman—it was the third watch of the Xu hour.

"Sleep," Qianlong said softly, "we must continue our journey tomorrow."

The candle was extinguished, leaving only moonlight in the room. Jiang Rao rested in Qianlong’s arms, listening to the stream outside, and gradually drifted off to sleep.

chapters.title: Scalding Fish Soup
chapters.content:
After resting for a night in Qingxi Town, the next morning, Qianlong ordered the caravan to delay their departure, wishing to stay in the small town for half a day longer to observe the lives of the people.

Though Qingxi Town was small, it was named for the clear stream that flowed through it. With its murmuring water, weeping willows on both banks, and several stone bridges spanning the stream, it possessed a certain charm reminiscent of the water towns of Jiangnan.

After breakfast, Qianlong took Jiang Rao for a stroll through the town, with Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai guarding them, and Xiaoyanzi, Ziwei, and Jin Suo following behind. The group was disguised as a wealthy family out for a pleasure trip, so they did not attract much attention.

Walking to the east end of the town, they saw a courtyard undergoing repairs. Several craftsmen were climbing up and down to patch the roof, and a middle-aged man in slightly worn official robes was also rolling up his sleeves, personally handing up tiles and mortar.

Ji Xiaolan whispered, "Master, this is Magistrate Sun of Qingxi Town. I inquired about him last night; he has an excellent reputation, is incorruptible, and often personally helps the impoverished repair their homes."

Qianlong nodded and stopped to watch.

He saw that although Magistrate Sun’s official robes were stained with mud and dust, his face was full of smiles, and he spoke kindly to the craftsmen and the commoners. An old woman in the courtyard brought out tea, thanking him repeatedly: "Thank you, honorable Magistrate! If it weren't for you, our dilapidated house would never have made it through this year's rainy season!"

Magistrate Sun took the coarse tea bowl and drank it in one gulp, laughing: "You are too kind, Mother Li. As a local official, it is only right that I resolve the worries of the people."

Xiaoyanzi was moved by the sight and turned to Qianlong: "Master, this magistrate is truly good! Shall we go and help, too?"

Before Qianlong could speak, Magistrate Sun noticed them. Seeing the group’s fine clothing and distinguished air, he quickly set down his tea bowl and stepped forward to bow: "Are you all passing through our town? I am Sun Wenzheng, the local magistrate. If there is anything you need help with, please do not hesitate to ask."

Qianlong returned the bow: "Magistrate Sun, you are too polite. We are just passing through, and seeing you personally helping the people repair their homes is truly admirable."

Sun Wenzheng laughed: "It is my duty; it is not worth mentioning. This Li family lost their son early, and only the elderly couple remains, unable to repair their home. Since I know of it, I naturally must take care of it."

As they spoke, a craftsman on the roof shouted: "Magistrate, we are short a few tiles over here!"

"Coming!" Sun Wenzheng responded and turned to help again.

Xiaoyanzi could no longer restrain herself. She rolled up her sleeves: "I’ll go too! When I was young in the acrobatic troupe, I was the best at climbing high and low!" Without waiting for anyone to react, she climbed the ladder in a few swift movements and reached the roof.

Yongqi said anxiously, "Be careful!"

Ziwei was also worried: "Xiaoyanzi, come down quickly!"

But Xiaoyanzi had already stood steady on the roof, triumphantly saying: "It’s fine! This roof isn't even as high as the eaves of the Shufang Studio!" She took the tiles handed up by the craftsman and began laying them down one by one, mimicking his technique, her movements surprisingly skillful.

Qianlong shook his head helplessly and said to Sun Wenzheng: "Forgive my daughter for being mischievous."

Sun Wenzheng smiled: "Your daughter is lively and cheerful; that is a good thing."

Jiang Rao looked up, but she felt somewhat disapproving. Xiaoyanzi was being far too reckless; for a young lady to be climbing up and down, what kind of decorum was that? But due to her status, she only frowned slightly and said nothing.

Just as she was thinking this, she suddenly heard a cry from the roof!

Everyone looked up to see Xiaoyanzi slip and tumble down from the roof!

"Xiaoyanzi!" Yongqi flew to catch her, but he was a step too late.

Xiaoyanzi fell straight down, landing squarely on the stone table in the courtyard—on the table sat a basin of scalding hot fish soup that Mother Li had just brought out!

"Ouch!" Xiaoyanzi let out a miserable shriek as she sat right into the soup basin.

The boiling fish soup splashed everywhere!

"Ah!" Jiang Rao was the closest and couldn't dodge in time. The hot soup splashed onto her arm, soaking her lotus-colored sleeve instantly, and a burning pain seared her skin.

She gasped, feeling both shocked and furious—that reckless Xiaoyanzi! Not only did she cause trouble for herself, but she dragged others into it!

"Rao'er!" Qianlong’s expression changed drastically, and he rushed over in a stride: "Where are you hurt?"

Jiang Rao’s eyes welled up with tears from the pain, but she endured it: "My... my arm..."

Qianlong carefully lifted her sleeve, revealing a patch of red on her fair forearm where several blisters had already formed. A flash of heartache and anger crossed his eyes as he turned to look at Xiaoyanzi.

Yongqi had already pulled Xiaoyanzi out of the soup basin. Xiaoyanzi was grimacing in pain, her clothes soaked from the waist down, with fish scales and green onions clinging to her, looking utterly wretched.

"It burns, it burns!" Xiaoyanzi cried out.

Ziwei hurried to check her injuries: "Quick! Take off those wet clothes!"

Mother Li was flustered: "That fish soup just came off the stove, it's very hot! Come inside quickly, I'll find some clothes for the young lady to change into!"

The scene was in chaos.

Qianlong couldn't spare a glance for Xiaoyanzi and instead helped Jiang Rao into the house, with Sun Wenzheng quickly leading them to another room. Ji Xiaolan had already sent someone to fetch the town doctor.

Inside the room, Qianlong personally cleaned Jiang Rao’s wound. The cool well water poured over the injury eased the pain slightly, but the blisters were shocking to behold.

Jiang Rao bit her lip, tears in her eyes, both from the pain and the anger. She couldn't help but whisper: "That Xiaoyanzi... she is too reckless! Not only did she fall, but she dragged others into it..."

Qianlong held her uninjured hand with heartache: "It is my fault for indulging her mischief. Does it hurt badly?"

"It hurts..." Jiang Rao did not try to be brave this time, leaning aggrievedly into his arms, "And my beautiful dress is ruined..."

Only then did Qianlong notice that her lotus-colored dress was one she had just had made before leaving the palace, and she loved it dearly. Now, the sleeve was covered in oil stains, and he feared it would never be clean again.

"We can make another dress; it is enough that you are unharmed," Qianlong soothed her softly. "The doctor will be here soon, and it won't hurt once the medicine is applied."

In the other room, Xiaoyanzi’s situation was more severe. She lay on the kang, and Ziwei carefully removed her wet clothes, revealing that her buttocks and thighs were bright red, covered in dense blisters.

Xiaoyanzi gasped in pain but still insisted: "I'm fine... I have thick skin..."

Yongqi was pacing anxiously outside the room, asking through the door: "How is it? Is the injury serious?"

"There are many blisters; I fear she will need to recover for quite some time," Ziwei’s voice was filled with heartache.

Just then, Erkang hurried in from outside, followed by two guards, each carrying a large bundle.

"Fifth Prince, the cotton has been bought!" Erkang panted, "As you ordered, I bought all the cotton from every pharmacy and fabric shop in town! A full thirty catties!"

Yongqi’s eyes lit up: "Bring it in quickly!"

Ziwei opened the door to take the cotton, and only then did Yongqi see the situation inside—Xiaoyanzi was lying on the kang, her injuries red and swollen, and Ziwei’s eyes were red, clearly having cried.

"Xiaoyanzi..." Yongqi was heartbroken.

"I'm fine..." Xiaoyanzi still tried to be tough, but her voice was already choked with tears.

Ziwei and Jin Suo, who had arrived upon hearing the news, layered the soft new cotton onto the kang and covered it with a clean sheet before helping Xiaoyanzi lie back down.

The cotton was soft and fluffy, and the injured areas no longer touched the hard kang directly; Xiaoyanzi finally felt a bit more comfortable and let out a long sigh of relief.

Meanwhile, the doctor had arrived. He examined Jiang Rao’s injury first, prescribed a cooling and detoxifying ointment, and instructed that it must not get wet and should be re-dressed daily.

Qianlong applied the medicine himself, his movements as gentle as if he were handling fragile porcelain. The ointment was cooling, and the pain eased slightly. Jiang Rao’s emotions calmed, but she still felt resentful toward Xiaoyanzi—if it weren't for her, how could she have suffered this unprovoked disaster?

The doctor then examined Xiaoyanzi and reported to Qianlong upon leaving: "That young lady’s injuries are more severe, but fortunately she is young and has a strong constitution. With regular dressing changes and bed rest for a few days, she should recover. However, she will likely have difficulty moving for the next few days."

Qianlong nodded: "Thank you, doctor."

Sun Wenzheng apologized repeatedly from the side: "It is all my negligence that caused the two young ladies to be injured..."

"It was just an accident," Qianlong waved his hand, but he glanced at Yongqi, "However, in the future, you must exercise more restraint; do not be so reckless again."

Yongqi lowered his head in shame: "Yes, Father is right to reprimand me."

That night, Xiaoyanzi could only lie on the cotton bed, and she even had to be fed. Jiang Rao had her hand wrapped in gauze, and Qianlong fed her dinner himself, a sight that made Xiaoyanzi feel incredibly envious.

"It’s good to be the Mistress, having the Master take care of you personally..." Xiaoyanzi muttered softly.

Ziwei fed her a spoonful of porridge and said softly: "Say less. If you hadn't been so reckless today, the Mistress wouldn't have been injured."

Xiaoyanzi pouted and said nothing more.

Jiang Rao felt her anger subside slightly after hearing this. She looked up at Qianlong and said softly, "My lord, will this injury leave a scar?"

"It will not," Qianlong said with certainty. "The doctor said that if you use the medicine on time and take care of it properly, it won't leave a scar. Even if it did... I have countless excellent scar-removal remedies in the palace; I will certainly restore you to your former self."

Only then was Jiang Rao relieved. She glanced at Xiaoyanzi again. Seeing her looking so pitiful as she lay in the pile of cotton, her heart softened further. Never mind, she hadn't done it on purpose.

After three days of recuperation, the wound on Jiang Rao's hand had scabbed over, and the pain had greatly diminished. Xiaoyanzi was also barely able to get out of bed, though she walked with a strange, limping gait.

That day, Sun Wenzheng came to the inn to visit and mentioned that there would be a market in town the next day, asking if everyone would like to go and see it.

Xiaoyanzi immediately perked up: "I want to go! I've been bored to death!"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao: "Do you want to go?"

Jiang Rao nodded: "It would be nice to walk around; staying in the inn all day is stifling."

So, the next day, the group went to the market. Since Xiaoyanzi had trouble walking, Yongqi found a wheelbarrow to push her in. Xiaoyanzi sat on the cart, feeling quite at ease.

The market in Qingxi Town was bustling. Although the items for sale were not expensive, everything had a rustic charm. Jiang Rao took a liking to a pair of small willow-woven baskets, and Qianlong bought them for her.

As they walked in front of a fabric stall, the stall owner, an elderly woman, saw the gauze wrapped around Jiang Rao's arm and asked with concern, "Young lady, what happened to your hand?"

Before Jiang Rao could answer, Xiaoyanzi blurted out, "It's my fault. I fell from the roof and knocked over the fish soup, splashing it on the lady..."

Her voice grew quieter as she spoke, clearly feeling ashamed.

Hearing this, the old woman took a small jar from under the stall: "This is my family's ancestral burn ointment; it is most effective. If you don't mind, take it and use it."

Jiang Rao accepted it and thanked her. Looking at Xiaoyanzi's guilty expression, the last bit of unhappiness in her heart dissipated.

"Forget it," she said softly, "just be more careful in the future."

Xiaoyanzi's eyes lit up: "The lady isn't angry with me anymore?"

"What use is there in being angry?" Jiang Rao teased. "Don't be so reckless next time."

"I promise!" Xiaoyanzi raised her hand to swear, but the movement was too sudden and pulled at her injury, causing her to cry out, "Ouch!"

Everyone laughed.

Two days later, Jiang Rao's wound had healed well; the gauze was removed, leaving only a faint red mark. Xiaoyanzi could also walk normally, though she still needed a soft cushion when sitting down.

Qianlong decided to continue the journey. On the day of departure, Sun Wenzheng brought the townspeople to see them off. Mother Li had specially cooked a pot of fish soup—this time it was warm, so it would never burn anyone again.

Yongqi looked at the thirty catties of cotton and felt troubled—if they took it, it would take up space; if they didn't, it would be a waste. In the end, it was loaded onto the carriage, with the excuse that it would serve as a cushion for Xiaoyanzi on the road.

As the carriage drove out of Qingxi Town, Xiaoyanzi leaned against the window, watching the town gradually recede, and suddenly said, "Qingxi Town is truly wonderful. Magistrate Sun is truly wonderful."

Ziwei said softly, "Yes. Although we were injured, meeting good people makes it all worth it."

Jiang Rao leaned on Qianlong's shoulder and whispered, "My lord, an official like Magistrate Sun should be given greater responsibilities."

Qianlong nodded: "I have already made arrangements."

The carriage pulled onto the main road, and Qingxi Town gradually disappeared from sight. But that warmth, that kindness between people, remained in everyone's hearts.

Xiaoyanzi suddenly remembered something and turned to ask Yongqi: "Fifth Prince, those cotton... how much silver did you spend?"

Yongqi smiled: "Not much. As long as you recover quickly, it's worth any amount."

Xiaoyanzi blushed and stopped talking.

Jiang Rao watched from the side and chuckled inwardly. This bickering pair was quite interesting.

Qianlong held her hand tightly: "Does it still hurt?"

"It doesn't hurt anymore," Jiang Rao shook her head, her eyes sparkling. "Where is the next stop?"

"Yuelao Town," Qianlong laughed. "I hear it's very effective for praying for marriage."

Jiang Rao pursed her lips and smiled, leaning into his embrace.

### Chapter 31: Yuelao Ties the Knot

The mountain road gradually leveled out, and the scenery became increasingly beautiful. After traveling for about two hours, another town appeared ahead. The stone tablet at the entrance was engraved with the three characters "Yuelao Town," the script ancient and weathered, suggesting it had been there for many years.

"Yuelao Town?" Xiaoyanzi poked her head out of the carriage, curious. "What an interesting name! Is Yuelao particularly effective here?"

Ji Xiaolan laughed from his horse: "The young lady guesses correctly. This Yuelao Town is famous for the Yuelao Temple within it, which is said to be extremely effective for those seeking marriage. Every first and fifteenth day of the lunar month, young men and women from a hundred miles around come here to pray for blessings and fate."

Hearing this, a trace of shyness flashed in Ziwei's eyes. Xiaoyanzi, however, was full of excitement: "Then let's go take a look! Perhaps..." She winked at Yongqi, "someone needs to pray for a good match!"

Yongqi's ears turned red under her gaze, and he coughed lightly: "Don't talk nonsense."

The caravan entered the town. Indeed, Yuelao Town was livelier than the previous two. Along both sides of the street, besides regular shops, there were many stalls selling red threads, marriage charms, and concentric locks. Among the pedestrians, there were many young men and women, all with expressions of anticipation.

In the center of the town stood the Yuelao Temple. Although not grand, it was bustling with incense. The square in front of the temple was even more crowded, filled with vendors selling flowers, fortune-tellers, and people writing marriage plaques—a dazzling array of sights.

Qianlong ordered the caravan to stop outside the temple and said to the group, "Since we are here, let's go in and take a look."

Jiang Rao had changed into a light pink dress today, covered by a pale green vest, with a pearl hairpin in her hair, making her look even more gentle. She took Qianlong's arm and followed the crowd into the temple, her eyes full of curiosity.

Xiaoyanzi had already pulled Ziwei ahead. Jin Suo followed closely behind, with Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai guarding them on the sides.

The main hall of the Yuelao Temple enshrined the statue of Yuelao, who looked kind and benevolent, holding a red thread in his hands. Smoke swirled from the incense burner in front of the statue, and offerings were piled high. Many young men and women were kneeling piously, whispering their wishes.

Xiaoyanzi imitated the others, kneeling down to kowtow three times, muttering to herself. Ziwei knelt beside her, closing her eyes in silent prayer with a devout expression.

Jiang Rao looked at the scene in the hall and felt moved. These young men and women, carrying beautiful expectations for marriage, came here to pray for Yuelao to tie the knot. And she... she looked up at Qianlong beside her, meeting his gentle gaze.

"Would you like to draw a lot?" Qianlong asked in a low voice.

Jiang Rao smiled: "I have already found a good match, why would I need to pray for one?"

The smile in Qianlong's eyes deepened, but he still pulled her to the bamboo tube: "Since we are here, let's draw one and see what Yuelao has to say."

Jiang Rao shook the tube as instructed, and a bamboo stick fell out. She picked it up and saw it was a "best of the best" lot. The inscription read: "A match made in heaven, a predestined union. Like the harmonious sound of the zither and flute, may you grow old together with one heart."

Qianlong took the inscription and read it, laughing: "Yuelao certainly knows how to speak."

As they were talking, Xiaoyanzi also drew a lot, but it was a "middle" lot. She pouted: "Why is it only a middle lot? Yuelao isn't giving me any face!"

Ziwei comforted her softly: "The inscription is just a metaphor; fate is ordained by heaven and cannot be forced."

"I want to see what the metaphor is!" Xiaoyanzi took the lot to the temple attendant to have it interpreted.

The attendant was an old man with white hair. He took the inscription, stroked his beard, and laughed: "This lot of yours, young lady, seems ordinary, but it actually hides a mystery. The inscription says: 'Meeting by chance, a serendipitous encounter. Treat others with sincerity, and fate will naturally gather.' This means that your fate is not found in deliberate seeking, but in unexpected encounters. Just treat people with sincerity, and a good match will come naturally."

Xiaoyanzi blinked: "That sounds... like it makes some sense."

Ziwei also drew a lot, which turned out to be a "best" lot: "When the golden wind and jade dew meet, it surpasses countless encounters in the world. If there was no fate in a previous life, wait for the next life to fulfill the wish."

The attendant looked at it and nodded: "This lot of yours, young lady, speaks of deep fate and heavy affection. If you meet the right person, cherish the present. Even if there are setbacks, they are destined from a previous life, and it will eventually be fulfilled."

Ziwei listened, lost in thought.

After drawing their lots, the group wandered around the temple. Behind the temple was a small garden with a massive ancient locust tree. The trunk required three people to encircle it, and its branches were lush and full, hung with red silk and wooden plaques, all praying for marriage.

"This is the Wishing Tree," Ji Xiaolan explained. "Write your wishes on a wooden plaque or red silk and hang it on the tree, and Yuelao will be able to see it."

Xiaoyanzi immediately perked up: "This is fun! I want to write one!"

The temple attendant had ready-made wooden plaques and writing materials. Xiaoyanzi was the first to rush over, picked up the brush, thought for a moment, and wrote: "May I win one heart, and never be parted until we grow old." After writing, she blushed and hung the plaque on the tree.

Ziwei also wrote one, but she turned her back to the group so no one could see. She wrote very slowly and carefully, and after finishing, she hung it carefully on a higher branch.

Yongqi, Erkang, and Ertai each wrote one as well. Yongqi's was simple: "May I protect one person's peace, with no regrets in this life." Erkang and Ertai's were even more subtle.

Qianlong watched, then picked up the brush and wrote one too. Jiang Rao leaned over to see, but he laughed and covered it: "Heavenly secrets must not be revealed."

Jiang Rao curled her lips and wrote one herself. She thought for a moment and wrote: "May your heart be like mine, and may we never fail our mutual longing." After writing, she handed the plaque to Qianlong: "My lord, please help me hang it higher."

Qianlong took it and reached up to hang the plaque on the highest branch. Sunlight filtered through the gaps in the leaves, and the characters on the plaque shimmered with golden light.

As everyone was chatting and laughing, they suddenly heard a commotion in front of the temple. They went out to look and saw a large circle of people gathered in the square. In the middle, a space had been cleared, and a girl in red was performing a sword dance.

The girl was about seventeen or eighteen, with delicate features and a vigorous posture. A long sword in her hand moved like a dragon playing with a phoenix, sometimes as light as a swallow, sometimes as strong as a pine, drawing bursts of applause from the onlookers.
