After finishing the sword routine, the girl stood with her sword, not even breathing hard. An old man stepped forward, cupped his hands, and said: "My daughter has made a fool of herself. Today is the day of Yuelao Town's 'Martial Arts Marriage Match.' Anyone under twenty-five who is unmarried may come up and try. Whoever can defeat my daughter may take her as his wife!"

So this was another tradition of Yuelao Town—the martial arts marriage match.

Several young men were eager to try and went up one after another, but none were the girl's match. After only three or five rounds, their weapons were knocked away, and they were defeated.

Xiaoyanzi's hands itched, and she wanted to go up, but was held back tightly by Yongqi: "You really cannot mess around with this!"

As they were speaking, a young man in fine clothes walked out of the crowd, holding a folding fan, looking arrogant: "Young lady, you have good skills. This young master will come and test you!"

This young man's skills were quite good; he fought with the girl for over twenty rounds and gradually gained the upper hand. The girl, after all, was weaker and began to show signs of fatigue.

Just as the girl was about to be defeated, a boy in plain clothes suddenly rushed out of the crowd and shouted: "Stop! This is a martial arts marriage match, stop at the point of contact! How can you use such heavy force!"

The silk-clad young man sneered, "Where did this poor brat come from? Mind your own business!"

The two were at odds and soon came to blows. Although the youth in plain clothes was dressed simply, his martial arts were solid. After only a dozen rounds, he knocked the silk-clad young man to the ground.

The young lady looked at the youth, a flash of admiration in her eyes. The old man stepped forward and asked, "How should I address this young hero?"

The youth cupped his hands in a salute: "I am Li Qingyun, son of a blacksmith in Zhenxi."

The old man nodded: "Young hero, your skills are extraordinary, and you possess a chivalrous heart; you are indeed a worthy match. Would you be willing to take my daughter as your wife?"

Li Qingyun looked at the young lady, who lowered her head in shyness. Blushing, he replied, "If I could gain the young lady's favor, it would be my great fortune."

A marriage was thus arranged, and the onlookers offered their congratulations one after another.

Qianlong watched from the crowd and nodded slightly: "This is indeed a fine story. A marriage by martial competition—it selects for character and skill rather than status or wealth. Very good."

Jiang Rao said softly, "I hope all lovers in the world may have their wishes fulfilled just like this."

By now, the sky was growing dark. Ji Xiaolan stepped forward to ask for instructions: "Master, shall we rest in Yuelao Town tonight?"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao and, seeing the fatigue on her face, said, "Let us rest here for the night."

They found an inn in the town. After dinner, Jiang Rao felt a bit stifled, so she went for a walk in the inn's backyard. The backyard bordered a stream; under the moonlight, the water shimmered with silver light, and the shadows of willow trees swayed on the opposite bank.

She stood alone by the stream, thinking of what she had seen at the Yuelao Temple during the day. The devout expressions of the young men and women, the dense wooden plaques on the wishing tree, and that young couple who had found their bond through the martial arts competition...

"What are you thinking about?" Qianlong's voice came from behind her.

Jiang Rao turned and saw him walking toward her, draped in an outer robe. She hurriedly said, "The night wind is chilly, why has Master come out?"

"I saw you weren't in the room, so I came to find you." Qianlong walked to her side and draped his robe over her shoulders. "Are you homesick?"

Jiang Rao shook her head: "I was just thinking that after seeing so many lovers seeking their fate today, Yuelao Town truly lives up to its name." She paused and looked up at him: "What did you write on the wishing tree today, Master?"

Qianlong laughed: "Didn't I say, heavenly secrets must not be revealed."

"Then..." A hint of playfulness flashed in Jiang Rao's eyes. "May I take a guess?"

"Go ahead."

"It must be something like 'peace for the nation and the people' or 'favorable weather for the crops'."

Qianlong shook his head: "Incorrect."

"Then... is it 'prosperous descendants and longevity'?"

"Also incorrect."

Jiang Rao thought and thought, but after guessing several times without success, she simply acted spoiled: "Master, tell me!"

Unable to resist her pestering, Qianlong whispered, "What I wrote was: 'I wish to be with you, morning and night, year after year.'"

Jiang Rao was stunned, and her eyes gradually welled up with moisture. She leaned into Qianlong's embrace and said softly, "Then, did you understand what I wrote, Master?"

"'May your heart be like mine, and never fail our longing,'" Qianlong recited the words from her wooden plaque. "I understood."

The moonlight was like water, and the stream murmured. The two stood in an embrace, while in the distance, the lights of the Yuelao Temple flickered in the night, as if the Old Man Under the Moon were truly in the clouds, tying the red threads for all the lovers in the world.

After a long while, Jiang Rao said softly, "Master, let us return to our room."

"Very well."

Back in the room, Jiang Rao attended to Qianlong as he changed. Under the candlelight, she unbuttoned his clothes with gentle movements. Qianlong took her hand: "Rao'er, are you happy on this tour?"

"I am." Jiang Rao looked up, her eyes filled with sincerity. "I have never been this happy. Seeing the world outside the palace, seeing the lives of ordinary people, seeing those sincere emotions... all of this makes me feel that I am truly, genuinely alive."

Qianlong gently stroked her face: "After we return to the palace, I will bring you out often."

"Really?"

"A sovereign never breaks his word."

Jiang Rao smiled, that smile exceptionally bright in the candlelight. Qianlong felt a stir in his heart and lowered his head to kiss her lips.

That night, Yuelao Town was exceptionally tranquil. Only the stream murmured, as if recounting the countless marriage vows made there over the centuries.

In a room at the inn, Little Swallow was leaning against the window, looking at the moon in the sky, and said to Ziwei, "Ziwei, do you think the Old Man Under the Moon is really efficacious?"

Ziwei said softly, "It is efficacious if your heart is sincere. As long as you treat others with a true heart, fate will always come."

"Then..." Little Swallow turned her head, her eyes sparkling. "Where do you think my fate will be?"

Ziwei smiled without answering, only gently holding her hand.

Outside the window, the moonlight was like water, spilling over the small town. The wishing tree in the Yuelao Temple swayed gently in the night breeze, and the wooden plaques filled with wishes bumped against each other, making faint sounds as if the Old Man Under the Moon were whispering his response.

The night deepened.

chapters.title: Seeing Injustice, Drawing a Sword to Help
chapters.content:
After lingering in Yuelao Town for a few days, the group continued westward.

The mountain road wound upward, growing higher as they traveled. Around noon, a mountain town appeared in the mountain pass ahead. Built against the mountain, layers of houses spread out along the terrain; viewed from afar, it even possessed a touch of ethereal beauty.

"Master, that is Lingshan Town ahead," Ji Xiaolan reported from outside the carriage. "This town is famous for the spiritual spring in the mountains. It is said the spring water is sweet and can cure illnesses and prolong life. There is also the Lingshan Temple in the town, which is very popular with pilgrims."

Qianlong lifted the carriage curtain to look. Indeed, there was a green mountain behind the town, wreathed in clouds and mist, truly possessing a spiritual and elegant air. He turned to ask Jiang Rao, "Would you like to go down and take a look?"

Jiang Rao nodded: "Since we are passing by, let us see what is so magical about this spiritual spring."

The carriage train stopped at the entrance of the town. Lingshan Town was busier than the previous towns; shops lined both sides of the street, mostly selling mountain goods, medicinal herbs, and jars for spring water. Among the passing pedestrians, there were many pilgrims who had come from afar to collect water.

As soon as they stepped out of the carriage, they saw a crowd gathered in front of a notice board at the town entrance, discussing animatedly.

Little Swallow, who loved to join in the excitement, pulled Ziwei to squeeze in and look. The notice read: "The daughter of Squire Zhao, the richest man in Lingshan Town, suddenly lost her voice three days ago. She refuses food and drink and is growing increasingly haggard. A reward of one thousand taels of silver to anyone who can cure her."

Standing next to the notice was a man who looked like a steward, saying to the onlookers, "My young mistress is sixteen years old. She is usually lively and cheerful; I do not know why she has suddenly become silent. We have invited doctors from a hundred miles around, but none can diagnose the cause. If any of you are masters of the arts, you might as well try."

Little Swallow's eyes lit up, and she turned to Qianlong: "Master! This is suspicious! Shall we see if we can help?"

Qianlong pondered for a moment: "It wouldn't hurt to take a look."

Thus, the group followed the steward to the Zhao residence. The Zhao residence was at the east end of the town—a grand house with high gates, truly the home of the richest man. Upon entering, they saw deep courtyards and luxurious furnishings, but everyone in the household wore a worried expression.

Squire Zhao was a stout, middle-aged man. Seeing the steward bring in a group of people, and although he saw they were dressed in fine clothes, he only offered a polite, perfunctory salute: "Greetings, everyone. My daughter's illness... sigh, it is not worth mentioning."

Little Swallow spoke quickly: "Squire, let us see the young lady! Perhaps we can help!"

Squire Zhao sized them up, seeing Qianlong's extraordinary bearing, Ji Xiaolan's scholarly elegance, and the heroic spirit of Yongqi and the others, so he nodded: "In that case, please follow me."

The group passed through several courtyards and arrived in front of a boudoir. After a maid announced them, they were led upstairs.

In the room, a young lady sat leaning against the window, dressed in a pale green dress. Her face was delicate and pretty, but her eyes were vacant, staring out the window without moving. This was Miss Zhao.

Ziwei said softly, "Miss Zhao, we are passing through and heard you were unwell, so we came to visit."

Miss Zhao seemed not to hear, still staring out the window.

Little Swallow walked up to her and waved her hand in front of her eyes: "Miss Zhao? Can you hear me?"

Miss Zhao's pupils moved slightly; she glanced at Little Swallow, but then turned back to the window.

Jiang Rao observed from the side and said softly, "The young lady seems to have something on her mind."

Qianlong asked Squire Zhao, "Was there anything unusual before the young lady fell ill?"

Squire Zhao sighed: "Three days ago, my daughter went to Lingshan Temple to burn incense. She became like this after she returned. She won't say anything when asked, and when we asked her maid, she only said everything was normal at the temple."

Ji Xiaolan stroked his beard and said, "May I take the young lady's pulse?"

Squire Zhao hurriedly said, "Please, sir."

Although Ji Xiaolan was not a doctor, he was learned and had dabbled in medical theory. After checking her pulse for a moment, he frowned: "The pulse is steady; there is no illness. This loss of speech is likely a sickness of the heart."

"A sickness of the heart?" Squire Zhao asked anxiously. "My daughter has been pampered since childhood; what kind of heart sickness could she have?"

Little Swallow's eyes darted, and she suddenly said, "Miss Zhao, did you meet someone at Lingshan Temple?"

Miss Zhao's body trembled slightly.

Seeing this, Ziwei gently added, "Was it a young gentleman?"

Miss Zhao turned her head, a flash of surprise in her eyes.

Little Swallow clapped her hands: "I guessed right! You must have met your beloved at the temple and fallen ill from lovesickness after returning!"

Squire Zhao was shocked: "What? This... how is this possible!"

Qianlong glared at Little Swallow: "Do not guess wildly."

Jiang Rao, however, walked closer to Miss Zhao and asked softly, "If it is inconvenient for you to speak, would you be willing to write it down?"

Miss Zhao looked at her, tears welling in her eyes, and finally nodded.

The maid hurriedly brought paper and a brush. Miss Zhao took up the brush, her hand trembling slightly, and wrote a few lines: "Three days ago at Lingshan Temple, I met a scholar named Liu Wenxuan. We talked happily and agreed to meet again at the temple tomorrow. I told my father upon returning home, but he forbade it, saying our families were not a match. My heart is broken."

Everyone read it and understood.

Squire Zhao read what his daughter had written, feeling both heartache and anger: "I have inquired about that Liu Wenxuan; he is nothing but a poor scholar. How could he be worthy of you!"

Miss Zhao wept, but still could not speak.

Little Swallow could not stand it and said to Squire Zhao, "Squire, is family status really that important? As long as two people love each other, what does it matter if he is a poor scholar? Look at the martial arts competition in Yuelao Town—didn't the blacksmith's son marry the martial artist's daughter?"

Yongqi coughed lightly: "Little Swallow..."

Qianlong, however, said, "What she says is not without reason." He looked at Squire Zhao: "Squire Zhao, for your daughter's illness, medicine is useless. The one who tied the knot must be the one to untie it. If you do not grant her wish, I fear..."

Squire Zhao sat down dejectedly: "But that Liu Wenxuan... I have sent people to inquire. Although he has some talent, he is penniless. How can he give Yu'er happiness?"

Ji Xiaolan said, "Squire, could you let that Liu Wenxuan come for a meeting? If he is truly a man of talent, he may not lack a future."

Squire Zhao hesitated for a long time, then finally nodded: "Very well. Steward, go and invite Master Liu."

Before long, the steward led in a scholar in a green robe. The scholar was in his early twenties, with a handsome face. Although his clothes were simple, he had a scholarly and elegant air. Upon entering the room, he first bowed to everyone, and when his gaze fell on Miss Zhao, his eyes were full of worry.

"Yu'er..." he whispered softly.

Miss Zhao heard his voice and shuddered. She turned her head, tears streaming down her face, her lips trembling until she finally managed to speak: "Wenxuan..."

Though the sound was faint, it caused everyone in the room to heave a sigh of relief.

Seeing that his daughter could speak again, Master Zhao was both joyful and moved.

Liu Wenxuan walked up to Miss Zhao and said gently, "When we parted at the temple that day, we agreed to meet the next. I waited for you all day, but when you didn't come, I was filled with unease. Today, I heard you were ill and was just coming to visit when I ran into your steward..."

Miss Zhao sobbed uncontrollably: "Father wouldn't allow it... He said your family is poor and you aren't worthy of me..."

Liu Wenxuan turned to Master Zhao and bowed deeply: "Master, though I am poor, I dare not be idle. I will certainly pass the provincial examination this autumn. If I achieve success in the future, I will never fail Yu'er's sincere heart."

The Qianlong Emperor spoke up: "Since Master Liu has such ambition, why not compose a poem on the spot to let Master Zhao see your talent?"

Liu Wenxuan nodded, pondered for a moment, and recited: "A jade maiden dwells on the spiritual mountain, bright and clear as the moon. I wish to be the gentle breeze that accompanies her, never to be parted. What does poverty matter when sincerity is as precious as gold? When the day comes that my name is inscribed on the roll, I shall return in red to welcome you home."

Though the poem was simple, the sentiment was genuine. Upon hearing it, Miss Zhao broke into a smile through her tears.

Master Zhao’s expression softened slightly, but he still said, "The poem is fine, but in the end, it is just empty words. If you are truly sincere, you must show it with real action."

Liu Wenxuan said earnestly, "How would you have me prove it, Master?"

The Qianlong Emperor suddenly said, "Master Zhao, why not let Master Liu stay in your manor for a time to focus on his studies? If he passes the provincial examination this autumn, you shall grant them their wish; if he fails, we can discuss it then. How about that?"

Seeing the Qianlong Emperor’s extraordinary bearing and the reasonableness of his words, Master Zhao nodded: "I shall follow the gentleman's advice."

With the matter temporarily resolved, Miss Zhao’s heartache was largely eased, and her spirits began to improve. Master Zhao invited everyone to dine, and during the meal, he thanked the Qianlong Emperor and the others repeatedly.

As they left the Zhao manor, Xiaoyanzi was still exclaiming: "Lovers finally becoming husband and wife—it's wonderful!"

Ziwei smiled: "It is. I hope Master Liu passes the exams this autumn and does not fail Miss Zhao’s devoted heart."

Jiang Rao, holding the Qianlong Emperor’s arm, whispered, "My lord has helped another couple find happiness today."

The Qianlong Emperor laughed: "It was merely giving a push to the current. What truly brought them together was their own sincerity."

The group wandered through the town a bit more and went to Ling Shan Temple to see the miraculous spring. The water was indeed clear and sweet. The monks in the temple said that drinking it often could clear the eyes and calm the mind.

Xiaoyanzi filled a flask, saying she wanted to take it back to the palace. Yongqi teased her: "The palace has plenty of Jade Spring water; it's even better than this."

But Xiaoyanzi insisted: "That's different! This is something we brought back from our incognito tour—it has meaning!"

In the evening, they stayed at the town inn.

After dinner, Jiang Rao brewed tea for the Qianlong Emperor in their room, using the miraculous spring water from earlier. As the tea fragrance filled the air, she said softly, "My lord, I have seen so many folk stories these past few days, and I have many thoughts."

The Qianlong Emperor took the teacup: "Tell me."

"In Meihua Town, I saw the joy of the common people; in Qingxi Town, the benevolence of an honest official; in Yuelao Town, the beauty of marriage; and today in Lingshan Town, the preciousness of true love." Jiang Rao’s eyes sparkled. "These are things one cannot see in the palace."

The Qianlong Emperor held her hand: "That is why I wanted to bring you out to see them. As the ruler of a nation, if one does not know the hardships of the people or understand their joys and sorrows, how can one govern?"

"My lord is wise." Jiang Rao leaned against his shoulder.

Outside the window, the night in Lingshan Town was quiet and peaceful. The distant bell of Ling Shan Temple rang out, its echoes lingering long.

In another room at the inn, Xiaoyanzi was saying to Ziwei: "Ziwei, do you think Miss Zhao and Master Liu will end up together?"

Ziwei said softly: "Lovers will naturally become husband and wife. Master Liu has talent, Miss Zhao has sincerity, and Master Zhao is not an unreasonable man. As long as Master Liu passes the examination this autumn, this marriage will be settled."

"That's good then." Xiaoyanzi let out a sigh of relief. "I just can't stand seeing lovers torn apart."

Yongqi, standing by, laughed: "You, you only ever worry about other people's business."

"So what?" Xiaoyanzi said righteously. "When you see injustice, you draw your sword to help!"

Everyone laughed.

chapters.title: Scumbag!
chapters.content:
The morning after the trip to Lingshan Town, the weather changed abruptly.

Yesterday had been clear and sunny, but overnight, the sky became overcast with thick clouds and a biting mountain wind. By the time the group set off, a fine drizzle had begun to fall.

"My lord, I fear this rain will grow heavier," Ji Xiaolan said, looking at the sky. "The mountain road ahead is steep; it may be dangerous to travel in the rain. Should we stay in Lingshan Town for another day?"

The Qianlong Emperor lifted the carriage curtain, saw the rain thickening and the mountain path turning to mud, and said, "Very well, safety first. We shall return to the inn in town for another day."

The carriage train turned back toward Lingshan Town. The rain grew heavier, and by the time they reached the inn, everyone’s clothes were half-soaked.

The innkeeper saw them return and hurried to arrange rooms. Jiang Rao had stayed by the spring for too long while gathering water yesterday, and she had felt a bit congested this morning; now, having been caught in the rain, she felt even more lightheaded. The Qianlong Emperor saw her poor complexion and touched her forehead; it was slightly feverish.

"Have you caught a cold?" The Qianlong Emperor frowned.

Jiang Rao forced herself to stay alert: "It's nothing, I'll be fine after a rest."

The Qianlong Emperor ordered someone to boil ginger soup and personally escorted her back to her room, instructing her to rest well. Jiang Rao was indeed exhausted, and after drinking the ginger soup, she fell into a deep sleep.

After settling Jiang Rao, the Qianlong Emperor returned to his own room to change. He, too, had been soaked while shielding Jiang Rao, and only now did he feel the chill seeping into his bones. He changed into dry clothes and was about to drink some hot tea to ward off the cold when he heard Xiaoyanzi’s voice outside: "My lord! Ziwei has boiled some cold-dispelling soup and brought it for you!"

He opened the door to see Xiaoyanzi carrying a tray, with Ziwei following behind. Ziwei held a steaming porcelain bowl in her hands.

"My lord, you were caught in the rain; drink a bowl of hot soup to warm yourself," Ziwei said softly.

The Qianlong Emperor took it. The soup was made with ginger strips and brown sugar, spicy and sweet. After one bowl, he indeed felt much warmer.

"You are very thoughtful," the Qianlong Emperor nodded at Ziwei.

Ziwei smiled: "It is only right."

The rain fell all day, turning into a torrential downpour by evening. The window lattices of the inn rattled under the rain, and the mountain wind howled, carrying the chill of late autumn.

During dinner, the Qianlong Emperor felt unwell; his head throbbed, and he felt cold. Thinking it was just fatigue from the day, he retired early.

Who would have thought he would develop a fever in the middle of the night?

At first, he only felt thirsty and called for water. Erkang, who was on night watch, heard the movement and entered. Seeing the Qianlong Emperor’s flushed face and touching his forehead, he found it frighteningly hot.

"The Emperor has a fever!" Erkang’s heart tightened, and he hurried to wake the others.

Yongqi and Ji Xiaolan rushed over. Xiaoyanzi and Ziwei also woke up upon hearing the news.

Jiang Rao had slept much of the day and was not sleeping soundly at night. Hearing the commotion outside, she asked Suxin: "What is it?"

Suxin had just returned from outside and whispered: "Your Majesty, the Emperor has a fever. The princes and princesses are all there taking care of him."

Upon hearing this, Jiang Rao hurriedly threw on a robe and got out of bed: "I'll go take a look."

"Your Majesty, you must not!" Suxin quickly blocked her. "You have also caught a cold; what if you pass the illness on? Besides, there are already many people taking care of the Emperor; your presence might only add to the chaos. It is better to rest well so you can take care of the Emperor when you are recovered."

Jiang Rao hesitated. She was indeed still dizzy and weak. On second thought, there were so many people with the Qianlong Emperor, and Ziwei was so attentive; her absence wouldn't matter, so she nodded: "Then go and check on him constantly, and tell me immediately if there is any news."

"This servant understands."

In the Qianlong Emperor’s room, it was already in chaos.

The Qianlong Emperor was delirious, drifting in and out of consciousness. Yongqi wanted to fetch a doctor, but was stopped by Ji Xiaolan: "Fifth Prince, it is the middle of the night, the rain is heavy, and the roads are slippery—how can you fetch one? Besides, the Emperor’s identity is special; it is not appropriate to disturb outsiders."

"Then what should we do?" Yongqi asked anxiously.

Ziwei had already brought warm water and was applying a damp cloth to the Qianlong Emperor’s forehead: "Let’s use physical cooling first. Xiaoyanzi, go to the kitchen and see if there is any white liquor; wiping the body with alcohol can help dissipate heat."

Xiaoyanzi went off to do as she was told.

Erkang and Ertai helped out, and Ji Xiaolan wrote a simple prescription, sending a guard out into the rain to fetch medicine from the town pharmacy—claiming only that their master had caught a cold.

Ziwei stayed by the bedside, changing the cold compress on the Qianlong Emperor’s forehead again and again. Her movements were gentle and attentive, and she checked his temperature from time to time.

In his delirium, the Qianlong Emperor felt only a cool sensation on his forehead, and someone was wiping his palms and neck with a warm cloth. The movements were so gentle and meticulous that they reminded him of many years ago, when another pair of hands had cared for him so devotedly during an illness...

In a daze, he opened his eyes and saw a delicate face, with gentle brows and eyes, looking at him with concern.

"Yuhe..." he whispered the name unconsciously, reaching out to grasp the hands that were wiping him.

Ziwei shuddered, and the cloth in her hand fell to the floor.

The Qianlong Emperor’s hands were scorching hot, gripping hers tightly with a force that caused her pain. His eyes were unfocused, and he murmured: "Yuhe... is it you... have you finally come to see me..."

The room fell into instant silence.

Erkang’s expression changed, and he stepped forward, not knowing what to do. Yongqi and Xiaoyanzi were also stunned.

Tears welled up in Ziwei’s eyes, her voice trembling: "Em... Emperor..."

"Don't go..." The Qianlong Emperor wouldn't let go of her hand. "I have searched for you for so many years... Yuhe..."

"Emperor, you have mistaken me for someone else..." Ziwei tried to pull her hand back, but he gripped it tighter.

At that moment, the door was pushed open gently.

Jiang Rao, unable to stay away, had finally forced herself to get up. Suxin supported her to the doorway, where she saw this jarring scene—the Qianlong Emperor tightly gripping Ziwei’s hand, calling out "Yuhe" with deep affection.

Jiang Rao felt as if she had been struck by lightning, standing frozen on the spot.

Erkang saw her first, his expression complex; he opened his mouth, but no sound came out.

The Qianlong Emperor was still muttering to himself, and Ziwei was already covered in tears. Xiaoyanzi looked back and forth between them, at a loss.

Jiang Rao felt a surge of anger rush straight to her head—just last night, this man had been holding her in intimacy, and today he was holding another woman’s hand and calling her "Yuhe"?!

A string of modern profanities exploded in her mind: Well done, you Qianlong! You scumbag! You big pig's trotter! You were all lovey-dovey with me last night, and today you’re in a feverish stupor grabbing another woman’s hand and calling for your "white moonlight"?!

Wait... Yuhe? Xia Yuhe?! Ziwei’s mother?!

Jiang Rao suddenly jolted, her memories as a transmigrator instantly returning—Ziwei was the Qianlong Emperor’s illegitimate daughter! Xia Yuhe was Ziwei’s biological mother!

So, the Qianlong Emperor was delirious from the fever and had mistaken Ziwei for Xia Yuhe?!

"Damn it!" Jiang Rao cursed inwardly. You’re holding your own daughter’s hand and calling out her mother’s name?! Qianlong, what kind of maneuver is this?! Even though Ziwei doesn't know you're her father yet, this behavior of yours... it's just unbelievable!

Wait... then what was I angry about just now? She suddenly realized, was I jealous of his daughter?!

But the next second, her rage flared up again—even if Ziwei is your daughter, you can't just hold a young woman's hand and call out her mother's name, can you?! What kind of father is this?! And you were with me last night... and today you do this?!

Jiang Rao’s face turned pale and then flushed, her whole body trembling with anger. Suxin quickly steadied her: "My Lady..."

"Let's go back." Jiang Rao’s voice was icy. She turned and walked away, her steps hurried and sharp.

Back in her room, she slammed the door shut and leaned against the door panel, gasping for air.

Suxin looked at her with concern: "My Lady, the Emperor was delirious from the fever, he was just talking nonsense..."

"Nonsense?" Jiang Rao sneered. "Can you hold another woman's hand and call her name just because you're delirious? Can you forget that you were holding me and whispering sweet nothings last night just because you're delirious?!"

The more she thought about it, the angrier she became, pacing back and forth in the room: "Men! They’re all just heartless pigs! I don't care if you're an emperor or a commoner, you're all the same! Eating from the bowl while eyeing what's in the pot! Last night you were all sweet and affectionate with me, and today you're calling someone else's name! Hah!"

Suxin was too scared to speak.

Jiang Rao sat down on the edge of the bed, her chest heaving. She was a modern woman who had traveled through time, raised with the values of monogamy. Although she had been a concubine for three years and was forced to accept the reality of polygamy, deep down, she still held a pure expectation for love. Qianlong’s exclusive favor over the past few years had almost made her forget—he was an emperor with three thousand beauties in his harem; how could she be the only one in his heart?

But seeing this scene with her own eyes, her heart still ached as if pricked by needles.

What was even more ridiculous was that she was jealous of his daughter!

Qianlong, you bastard! Jiang Rao continued to curse in her heart. You created a daughter from your own past romantic debts, and now look at the mess you've made! If Ziwei knew you were holding her hand and calling her mother's name, wouldn't she be disgusted to death?!

And me! What am I?! You were holding me while you slept last night, and today you put on this show for me?!

She grabbed a pillow and threw it hard onto the bed.

Meanwhile, in Qianlong’s room.

Ziwei finally pulled her hand away, and Qianlong gradually became more lucid. He opened his eyes, saw the room full of people, and frowned: "I... what happened?"

"Father has a fever," Yongqi said quickly. "How do you feel now?"

Qianlong propped himself up, his head still spinning: "It's nothing." He looked at Ziwei, seeing her eyes red and swollen, and asked, "Why are you crying?"

Ziwei lowered her head: "It's... it's nothing."

Qianlong looked at Erkang, whose expression was complex, wanting to say something but holding back.

"What exactly is going on?" Qianlong sensed something was wrong.

Ji Xiaolan smoothed things over: "The Emperor has just broken his fever and needs to rest. Miss Ziwei has been taking care of you for half the night and is tired too. Everyone, go and get some rest."

Only then did the group begin to file out.

Erkang, walking last, looked back at Qianlong once, but ultimately said nothing.

That night, everyone was preoccupied with their own thoughts, and no one slept well.

The next morning, the rain stopped.

Qianlong’s fever had broken, and his spirits were much better. At breakfast, however, Jiang Rao was nowhere to be seen.

"Where is the Madam?" he asked.

Suxin, who was serving nearby, said softly: "Reporting to Master, the Madam is feeling unwell and is resting in her room."

Qianlong remembered that Jiang Rao had also caught a cold yesterday, so he said: "I will go see her."

Arriving outside Jiang Rao’s room, he found the door closed. Qianlong knocked: "Rao'er, I’ve come to see you."

There was silence inside for a moment before Jiang Rao’s cold voice came through: "My illness has not yet passed, and I fear I might pass it on to you, Master. Please return."

Qianlong was stunned. This tone... it wasn't right.

"Rao'er, open the door." He knocked again.

The door opened. Jiang Rao stood inside, wearing her nightclothes, her long hair uncombed, her face indeed looking pale. She glanced at Qianlong, her eyes cold, devoid of the usual coquettish reliance.

"Is the Master feeling better?" she asked, her tone polite and distant.

Qianlong’s heart tightened: "I am better. How are you? Are you still feverish?"

"Thank you for your concern, Master, I am fine," Jiang Rao lowered her eyes. "You have just recovered from a serious illness, you should go back and rest. I wish to sleep a while longer."

As she spoke, she moved to close the door.

Qianlong reached out to block it: "Rao'er, what is wrong?"

Jiang Rao looked up at him, a trace of mockery flashing in her eyes: "What could be wrong with me? It is just a cold, I need to rest. Please return, Master."

*Scumbag!* she added in her heart.

The door closed.

Qianlong stood outside, his brows furrowed. He knew Jiang Rao too well; this was definitely not just a normal fit of temper.

Back in his room, he summoned Erkang: "When I had a fever last night, did something happen?"

Erkang hesitated for a moment, then whispered: "Emperor... when you were delirious with fever last night, you mistook Ziwei for someone else, held her hand, and called out... 'Yuhe'."

Qianlong was shaken to his core.

"At that time... the Madam happened to walk in and see it," Erkang’s voice dropped even lower.

Qianlong closed his eyes.

No wonder.

No wonder she was acting like this.

"I understand," he waved his hand. "You may go."

After Erkang left, Qianlong sat alone in his room for a long time, motionless.

Yuhe... he hadn't mentioned that name to anyone for many years. She was a woman he had met during his southern tour in his youth, gentle as water and overflowing with talent. They had a romance, but in the end... he had failed her.

Over the years, he had hidden her in the deepest part of his heart, thinking he had forgotten. But last night, in his illness, seeing Ziwei’s similar features, he had momentarily thought she had returned.

And this scene, of all things, was seen by Rao'er.

Qianlong rubbed his brow. He knew Rao'er’s temperament best; she seemed spoiled and willful, but she was actually sensitive and proud. She must have misunderstood.

He stood up and went to Jiang Rao’s room again.

This time, he pushed the door open and went straight in. Jiang Rao was sitting by the window, staring blankly. Seeing him enter, she only glanced at him before turning away.

Qianlong walked up to her, crouched down, and took her hand: "Rao'er, I was delirious with fever last night, everything I said was nonsense."

Jiang Rao pulled her hand back, sneering inwardly: *Nonsense? Can you call out your 'white moonlight's' name while talking nonsense? Can you hold a girl's hand and refuse to let go while talking nonsense? Qianlong, who are you trying to fool!*

But on the surface, she only said coldly: "What the Emperor says has nothing to do with me."

"Rao'er..." Qianlong took her hand again, "You are the only one in my heart."

*Pah!* Jiang Rao spat in her heart. *The only one in your heart? Then who is Yuhe? And who is Ziwei? Oh right, Ziwei is your daughter, but you don't know that yet! In your eyes, she's just a girl who looks like your old flame! How is this any different from those scumbags who look for substitutes?!*

The more she thought, the angrier she became, and her tone grew colder: "If I am the only one in the Emperor's heart, then who is 'Yuhe'? And who is Ziwei? Is the Emperor so special to Ziwei because she looks like that person?"

Qianlong was speechless.

"The Emperor need not explain," Jiang Rao turned her head away, her eyes brimming with tears she was struggling to hold back—this time, the hurt was real. "I understand now. The favor of these past few years was merely me basking in someone else's light. Now that the true owner has returned, I should naturally step aside."

"What nonsense are you talking!" Qianlong said anxiously. "Ziwei is not Yuhe! I am special to Ziwei because... there is another reason. But it is absolutely not what you imagine!"

"Then what is it?" Jiang Rao looked up at him, her eyes sharp.

Qianlong fell silent.

Seeing his silence, Jiang Rao’s heart grew even colder. She stood up: "Please return, Emperor. I wish to be alone."

*Alone to think about how to curse you! Scumbag!* she added in her heart.

"Rao'er..."

"Please return."

Qianlong looked at her stubborn back, knowing that whatever he said now, she wouldn't listen. He could only sigh, turn, and leave.

As the door closed, Jiang Rao’s tears finally fell.

It wasn't that she wouldn't let him have a past; she wasn't that petty. But his special treatment of Ziwei, his inability to forget "Yuhe," made her feel that her affection over the past few years was like a joke.

*Even though I know Ziwei is your daughter, you don't know that yet! You are currently holding the hand of a girl who looks like your old flame and calling her name! How is this any different from cheating?!*

*And... and you were with me last night...*

Jiang Rao grew angrier the more she thought about it, grabbing the pillow and throwing it again.

*Qianlong! You are just a scumbag! A heartless pig!*

What Jiang Rao didn't know was that at this moment, in Ziwei’s room, Ziwei was crying to Erkang: "Erkang, the Emperor... he called my mother's name... he recognized my mother..."

Erkang held her hand, his expression grave: "Ziwei, this matter... I'm afraid it's not simple."

chapters.title: Cold Feelings Amidst Mountains and Waters
chapters.content:
The next morning, the fog in Lingshan Town had not yet fully dispersed, and lively discussions could already be heard from downstairs in the inn.

When Jiang Rao woke up, Qianlong had already risen and was being dressed by Suxin. Since their argument yesterday, the two hadn't spoken a proper word. Jiang Rao lowered her eyes, got up, and walked silently to the vanity to comb her long hair, not saying a word.

Qianlong watched her in the mirror, noticing the faint dark circles under her eyes, clearly showing she hadn't slept well last night. He sighed inwardly, not knowing how to broach the subject.

While they were in silence, Xiaoyan's cheerful voice came from outside: "Master! Madam! Come downstairs quickly! The innkeeper says there is a place called 'Flying Cloud Ravine' ten miles outside the town, with excellent scenery, waterfalls, and deep pools—it's worth a look!"

Jiang Rao’s hand paused, then she continued combing.

Qianlong said: "Understood, we'll be down shortly."

After everyone finished breakfast, they gathered in the inn's lobby. Xiaoyan was excitedly asking the innkeeper about the route to Flying Cloud Ravine: "Is it really that beautiful? How big is the waterfall? Can you swim in the pool?"

The innkeeper laughed: "Miss, the waterfall at Flying Cloud Ravine isn't huge, but the water flows fast, cascading straight down from the cliff, often creating rainbows in the sunlight. The pool water is crystal clear, though it’s late autumn and the water is cold, so I'm afraid it might be too chilly for swimming."

Yongqi said: "Since it's not far, it might be nice to go see it. Father, what do you think?"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao: "Do you want to go?"

Jiang Rao hadn't wanted to go, but seeing everyone looking at her, she said coolly: "I will follow the Master's arrangements."

So, the group packed up simply and headed toward Flying Cloud Ravine.

Not long after leaving the town, they entered the forest. The mountain road grew steeper, but the scenery was indeed beautiful. In the autumn, the forest was painted in layers of color, red and yellow leaves intertwined, the mountain stream gurgled, and the air was fresh and moist.

After walking for about an hour, the roar of water could be heard. Turning a bend in the mountain, the view suddenly opened up—a waterfall like a silver ribbon cascaded down from a cliff dozens of zhang high, plunging into a deep pool below and splashing up a thousand piles of snow. Sunlight filtered through the gaps in the forest, casting a soft rainbow over the waterfall.

"How beautiful!" Ziwei couldn't help but exclaim.

Xiaoyanzi had already run to the edge of the pool, reaching out to test the water temperature: "Oh, it really is chilly!"

Jiang Rao stood slightly behind the others, watching the waterfall quietly. The mountain breeze blew, carrying the chill of water vapor, and she couldn't help but pull her cloak tighter. As she looked up, she met Qianlong’s gaze and quickly turned her face away.

Ji Xiaolan stroked his beard and said, "This scenery is tranquil; it is indeed a place for clearing one's mind."

Erkang, standing beside Ziwei, whispered, "Be careful, the stones by the pool are slippery."

The group walked along the path by the pool, admiring the surrounding scenery. The roar of the waterfall was constant, forcing them to raise their voices to speak. Xiaoyanzi, being the most lively, pulled Yongqi toward the waterfall, saying she wanted to feel the mist.

Jiang Rao walked slowly and gradually fell behind. Qianlong slowed his pace, waiting for her to catch up.

"Still angry with me?" he asked in a low voice.

Jiang Rao did not answer, only looking at the distant waterfall.

Qianlong sighed softly: "Regarding what happened that night, I will give you an explanation."

"There is no need for you to explain, Master," Jiang Rao said in a flat tone. "I understand everything."

"You don't understand." Qianlong took her hand, but she gently pulled it away.

"What I understand is this," Jiang Rao looked up at him, her eyes devoid of emotion, "you are the Son of Heaven. Your heart holds the empire, the people, and naturally... old acquaintances. I should not expect too much."

The words were polite, yet every syllable was barbed. Qianlong frowned: "Rao'er, must you speak this way?"

"Then how would you like me to speak, Master?" Jiang Rao countered. "Pretend nothing happened? Or happily accept that you hold someone else in your heart?"

"Do you not know who I hold in my heart?"

"I thought I knew," Jiang Rao smiled, but the smile did not reach her eyes. "Now, I am not so sure."

As the two stood in a stalemate, Xiaoyanzi’s exclamation came from ahead. Everyone hurried over to find her crouching on a large rock by the pool, pointing into the water: "Look! Fish! Such big fish!"

Indeed, the pool was clear, and several fat fish could be seen swimming about.

Yongqi laughed: "If you want to catch them, I’ll go find some fishing gear."

"No need, no need!" Xiaoyanzi rolled up her sleeves. "I’ll catch them myself!"

As she spoke, she reached into the water, naturally grabbing nothing but splashing herself all over. Everyone laughed, and the atmosphere finally lightened a little.

Qianlong watched Xiaoyanzi’s antics, then looked at the still-cold Jiang Rao beside him, feeling a sense of frustration. He turned and walked toward the other side of the waterfall, wanting to be alone.

Seeing this, Erkang signaled for Yongqi to follow. Just as Yongqi was about to move, Qianlong waved his hand: "No need to follow. I want to walk alone."

On the other side of the waterfall, a small path led to higher ground, and Qianlong walked up the stone steps. The sound of water faded, and the forest was quiet, save for the sound of birds. He reached a platform and looked down at the deep pool and the others, his thoughts in turmoil.

Yuhe... Ziwei.

He stood for a long time. The mountain breeze blew, carrying the chill of late autumn. He hadn't worn extra clothing when he came out, and only now did he feel the cold. Just as he was about to return, he saw Jiang Rao walking up the path, standing not far below, looking up at the waterfall in a daze.

She was wearing a moon-white dress today, covered by a pale green cloak. The mountain breeze stirred her sleeves, making her silhouette appear frail. Qianlong’s heart softened, and he walked down: "Why did you come up?"

Jiang Rao seemed startled. Turning to see him, she curtsied: "I saw that you had not returned for a long time, Master, so I came up to check."

The words were proper, yet distant. Qianlong said: "I am fine, just walking."

The two stood side by side, looking at the waterfall. The roar of the water only made the silence feel more oppressive.

"I know what you are angry about," Qianlong said in a low voice. "Angry that I held Ziwei’s hand while I was ill, angry that I called out another person’s name. But it truly... was not what you think."

"Then what was it like?" Jiang Rao finally turned to look at him. "Do you dare say that when you looked at Ziwei, you did not think of someone else?"

Qianlong was silent.

This silence was like a knife, stabbing into Jiang Rao’s heart. She smiled, though tears welled in her eyes: "Look, you cannot deny it yourself."

"Rao'er..."

"I am tired, I will head back first." Jiang Rao turned to leave.

Qianlong grabbed her: "Don't go."

Jiang Rao stood motionless, her back to him, her shoulders trembling slightly.

Qianlong embraced her from behind, pulling her into his arms. Jiang Rao struggled, but he held her tighter: "Don't move... let me hold you for a while."

His breath was warm, his chest solid. Jiang Rao stiffened for a moment, then finally softened, tears falling silently.

"It is my fault," Qianlong whispered in her ear. "But you must believe me, the most important person in my heart is you."

Jiang Rao closed her eyes, her tears flowing more heavily. Should she believe him? Could she?

The two remained in each other's arms for a long time, until the mountain breeze grew colder. Qianlong gently let her go and pulled her cloak around her: "Let’s go down the mountain; the wind is picking up."

Returning to the pool, the others were already preparing to leave. Xiaoyanzi was still reluctant: "This place is so nice, can we come again?"

Yongqi laughed: "You can come whenever you like, just don't think about catching fish again."

On the way back, although Qianlong and Jiang Rao did not say much, the atmosphere had eased considerably. Jiang Rao was still preoccupied, but she was no longer deliberately cold.

By the time they returned to the inn in the evening, Qianlong felt unwell. Having been exposed to the mountain wind during the day, he now had a dull headache and felt cold. He didn't make a fuss and went to rest early.

At night, he developed a fever again.

It was not as severe as the last time, but he was burning up nonetheless. Ertai was on duty and hurried to call for help. Yongqi and Ji Xiaolan came to check on him, and Ziwei and Xiaoyanzi also got up.

Jiang Rao was a light sleeper; hearing the commotion, she got up and asked Suxin: "What is it again?"

"My Lady, the Emperor has a fever again," Suxin whispered. "Perhaps he caught a chill in the mountains today."

Jiang Rao’s heart tightened, and she put on a robe and got out of bed: "I will go see."

This time, she did not hesitate. Arriving in Qianlong’s room, she saw Yongqi feeding him water while Ziwei wrung out a towel nearby. Seeing her enter, Yongqi quickly said: "Madam, Father has caught a chill again."

Jiang Rao walked to the bedside. Qianlong’s face was flushed, his eyes closed, his brows slightly furrowed. She reached out to test his forehead; it was indeed scorching hot.

"Where is the medicine?" she asked.

"Master Ji has already prescribed a decoction, and someone has gone to brew it," Yongqi said.

Jiang Rao took the wet towel from Ziwei’s hand, soaked it in cold water again, and placed it on Qianlong’s forehead. Her movements were gentle and meticulous, a complete change from the day before.

Ziwei watched from the side and said softly: "Madam, let me..."

"No need," Jiang Rao said calmly. "You go and rest, I am here."

Ziwei wanted to say more but looked at Erkang. Erkang shook his head slightly at her, so she stopped insisting and withdrew with Xiaoyanzi and the others.

Only Jiang Rao and the unconscious Qianlong remained in the room. She sat by the bed, changing the towel again and again, wiping the cold sweat from his forehead. In the candlelight, his face looked haggard; the majesty of the emperor had faded, and he was now just a sick man.

As Jiang Rao watched him, the anger in her heart gradually dissipated, leaving only heartache.

What am I angry about? she thought with a bitter smile. He is an emperor; it is normal for him to have a past. I clearly know the whole truth, yet I still eat this inexplicable vinegar...

But... but my heart still hurts.

She gently took Qianlong’s hand. His hand was scorching, yet he gripped hers tightly in return.

Qianlong opened his eyes in a daze, his vision blurred, but he could vaguely see a figure by the bed. He murmured: "Rao'er..."

"Yes, I am here," Jiang Rao replied softly.

"Don't go..." he gripped her hand tighter.

"I won't," Jiang Rao tucked the quilt around him. "I am here with you, Master."

Qianlong seemed reassured and fell into a deep sleep again.

Jiang Rao kept watch for half the night until the medicine was ready, carefully feeding it to him. In the second half of the night, the fever gradually subsided, and Qianlong slept more peacefully. Only then did Jiang Rao lean against the bedpost and close her eyes for a nap.

As dawn approached, Qianlong woke up. Seeing Jiang Rao asleep by the bedside, one hand still holding his, he felt a warmth in his heart and gently wrapped her hand in his palm.

Jiang Rao woke up with a start. Seeing he was awake, she hurriedly asked: "How do you feel, Master? Is the fever gone?"

"Much better," Qianlong’s voice was hoarse. "Did you watch over me all night?"

Jiang Rao nodded and stood up to pour him water. Qianlong watched her busy back and said softly: "You have worked hard."

Jiang Rao paused, her back to him, and whispered: "As long as you get well soon, Master, it is no hardship."

Qianlong knew that her knot of resentment had not fully unraveled, but this care was a sign of softening. He said no more, simply keeping this affection in his heart.

After daybreak, when the others learned of Qianlong’s condition, they all came to visit. Xiaoyanzi was boisterous: "How did the Master get sick again! It must have been the wind at Feiyunjian yesterday!"

Ji Xiaolan said: "The mountain wind in autumn is invasive, and the Master has only just recovered from a major illness; it is our negligence."

Qianlong waved his hand: "It is no matter, a day or two of rest will suffice."

And so, the journey was delayed once more.

Jiang Rao spent her days in the room taking care of him, feeding him medicine and meals with meticulous care. However, she still did not speak much, and there was always a layer of distance between them.

chapters.title: Forget it... Forget it
chapters.content:
On the third day of Qianlong’s recuperation at the inn, a drizzling autumn rain began to fall outside.

The fine threads of rain tapped against the window lattice, shrouding Lingshan Town in a hazy mist. Jiang Rao pushed open the window, and the moist air rushed in, carrying the unique fragrance of grass and trees from the mountains.

"Madam, the medicine is ready," Suxin said as she entered with a bowl.

Jiang Rao took it and walked to the bedside. Qianlong was leaning against the headboard reading a book; seeing her, he set it aside.

"How do you feel today?" Jiang Rao tested the temperature of his forehead; it had returned to normal.

"Much better." Qianlong took the bowl and drank it in one gulp, not even frowning.

Jiang Rao offered him a candied fruit, but he shook his head: "No need, the medicine is not bitter." He looked at her, his gaze gentle. "You have worked hard these past few days."

"This is what I should do," Jiang Rao said, lowering her eyes as she tidied up the bowl.

Xiaoyanzi’s laughter came from outside; she seemed to be teasing Yongqi again. Qianlong said: "They have been cooped up for days, too. When the rain stops, I will take you all to see Lingshan Temple. I hear their vegetarian meals are excellent."

Jiang Rao nodded: "Whatever you arrange, Master."

There was still a layer of formality between them, but compared to the coldness of the previous days, it had eased significantly. Jiang Rao understood in her heart that her jealousy was truly unreasonable—but knowing it was one thing, and being able to turn her emotions around was another.

Jiang Rao, oh Jiang Rao, she scolded herself inwardly, you are a modern person who traveled back in time, how are you even more feudal than the people of the ancient era?

Yet another voice countered: But he doesn't know that she is his daughter right now! In his eyes, she is just a girl who looks like his old flame! When he held her hand and called out her mother's name, what was he thinking?

Two trains of thought clashed in her mind, leaving her feeling agitated and confused.

The rain fell for an entire day and only began to subside toward evening. The setting sun peeked through the gaps in the clouds, dyeing the wet streets and alleys in gold.

Xiao Yanzi ran upstairs, excited, "Master! Madam! The rain has stopped! Let's go for a stroll in the street? I heard the Lingshan Town night market is very lively; they sell mountain goods and even have opera performances!"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao: "Do you want to go?"

Jiang Rao didn't really want to go, but seeing the anticipation in Xiao Yanzi's eyes, she said, "A walk would be nice."

The group left the inn. The town after the rain was exceptionally fresh; the bluestone path reflected the sky, and water still dripped from the eaves. The night market was indeed lively, with stalls lining the street, mostly selling mountain goods—mushrooms, bamboo shoots, herbs, and hand-woven bamboo ware.

Xiao Yanzi looked here and there, picking up a bamboo cricket cage one moment and taking a fancy to an oil-paper umbrella the next. Yongqi followed behind her, ready to pay at any moment.

Ziwei and Erkang walked a little further back, whispering to each other, a gentle smile on Ziwei's face. Jiang Rao watched them, a sudden wave of emotion washing over her.

Just as she was thinking, Qianlong walked up to a stall selling jade ornaments and picked up a white jade hairpin. The hairpin was pure white, carved into the shape of an orchid, simple yet elegant.

"Do you like it?" he asked Jiang Rao.

Jiang Rao took a look: "It's quite nice."

Qianlong bought it and personally pinned it into her hair. As the cold jade touched her hair, Jiang Rao trembled slightly.

"It suits you very well," Qianlong said, examining her with a smile in his eyes.

Jiang Rao touched the hairpin and whispered, "Thank you, Master."

The two continued walking and passed a sugar painting stall. Xiao Yanzi was pestering the vendor to draw a large phoenix; Ziwei asked for a butterfly, and Jin Suo asked for a flower.

Seeing Qianlong’s extraordinary bearing, the vendor smiled and said, "Sir, would you like one too? How about a pair of mandarin ducks for your lady?"

Qianlong looked at Jiang Rao: "Do you want one?"

Jiang Rao initially wanted to say no, but seeing the vendor had already scooped up the syrup, she nodded.

Golden syrup flowed onto the iron plate, and in a moment, a pair of intertwined mandarin ducks took shape. The vendor fixed them with a bamboo skewer and handed it to Jiang Rao.

The mandarin ducks were nestled together, sweet and affectionate. Jiang Rao took it, but her heart was filled with mixed feelings.

"Is Madam not eating?" Xiao Yanzi had already bitten off half of her phoenix.

Jiang Rao took a small bite; the sugar was very sweet, cloyingly so. She ate slowly while Qianlong watched her from the side, his gaze tender.

At the end of the night market was a small stage where local opera was being performed. Although she couldn't understand the lyrics, the melody was melodious and the costumes were gorgeous, making it quite a pleasant sight. The group stood under the stage to watch for a while, and Xiao Yanzi even mimicked the gestures of the lead actress, making Yongqi laugh.

By the time they returned to the inn, the moon was high in the sky.

Jiang Rao served Qianlong as he changed his clothes. Neither of them spoke, and only the chirping of autumn insects could be heard outside the window. The candlelight flickered, casting swaying shadows on the wall.

Jiang Rao leaned against his chest, smelling the faint scent of medicine and ambergris on him, and the lingering resentment in her heart finally began to dissipate.

*Forget it,* she thought. *He is the Emperor, and I am a concubine. This relationship was never equal to begin with; all I can ask for is a sincere heart. Since he is willing to give me this sincerity, why should I dwell on so much?*

That night, the two slept in each other's arms. The estrangement of many days finally melted away quietly in the dampness of the autumn rain.

The next morning, Qianlong’s health had improved significantly, and he decided to continue the journey.

Before leaving Lingshan Town, Master Zhao brought his daughter and Liu Wenxuan to see them off. Liu Wenxuan had spent the last few days studying hard behind closed doors at the Zhao residence; his complexion had improved, and his eyes were more spirited.

"This student will certainly not fail your expectations," he said with a solemn bow.

Zhao Yu'er stood behind her father, glancing shyly at Liu Wenxuan, her eyes filled with affection.

Qianlong nodded: "I hope you place high in the imperial examinations and do not fail your lady."

The carriage convoy drove out of Lingshan Town, continuing westward along the mountain road. The autumn sun was warm but not scorching, and the mountain scenery was colorful and picturesque.

Xiao Yanzi chattered in the carriage about what she had seen the night before, while Ziwei listened with a smile, occasionally adding a few words. Yongqi and Erkang rode ahead, and Ji Xiaolan sat in another carriage, stroking his beard as he looked at the scenery along the way.

Jiang Rao leaned on Qianlong’s shoulder, watching the passing scenery outside the window, her heart at peace.

"Where is the next stop?" she asked softly.

"Qinghe Town," Qianlong said. "I heard the local customs there are simple and honest, and the scenery is also beautiful."

Jiang Rao nodded, then suddenly remembered something: "Master, that jade hairpin... it's very beautiful."

Qianlong smiled and squeezed her hand: "As long as you like it."

The carriage bumped along, leaving Lingshan Town behind. The disturbances of those rainy nights, the tenderness during his illness, and the sweetness of the night market all became memories.

chapters.title: Waves Rise in Qinghe
chapters.content:
The afternoon sun spilled in through the carriage window, warm and cozy. Jiang Rao leaned on Qianlong’s shoulder, toying with the white jade hairpin in her hand, its surface glowing with a warm luster in the light.

"Master," she spoke softly, "what kind of place is Qinghe Town?"

Qianlong held her hand, his fingertips gently rubbing the back of her hand: "This is my first time going there too. I only heard that a clear river runs through the town, with weeping willows planted on both banks, and in autumn, the reed catkins look like snow; the scenery is quite good." He paused, "What is even rarer is that it is said that all the successive magistrates of Qinghe have had good reputations, and the people live and work in peace."

Jiang Rao looked up at him: "Master, this trip was originally meant to see places like this, right? To see the true state of a prosperous and peaceful country."

Qianlong nodded: "Indeed. Meihua Town, Yuelao Town, Lingshan Town—each has its own characteristics, but they have all allowed me to see the hardships of the common people. If Qinghe Town is truly as rumored, it would be a great comfort to me."

As they were speaking, the carriage suddenly slowed down. Ji Xiaolan’s voice came from outside: "Master, there is a tea shed ahead; would you like to stop and rest your feet?"

Qianlong lifted the carriage curtain to look; the sun was indeed leaning toward the west, so he said, "Very well, let's rest for a quarter of an hour before moving on."

The tea shed was simple but kept clean. The proprietress was a woman in her forties, who nimbly served tea and a few coarse snacks. Xiao Yanzi was already hungry and grabbed a sesame cake to munch on. Yongqi smiled and handed her tea from the side: "Slow down, don't choke."

Jiang Rao and Qianlong sat in a seat near the back, while Ziwei and Erkang sat at the neighboring table. Ji Xiaolan and the coachmen sat at another.

After serving the tea, the proprietress stood to the side, wiping her hands on her apron, and smiled as she struck up a conversation: "Are you gentlemen and ladies heading to Qinghe Town?"

Qianlong nodded: "Exactly. Is the proprietress familiar with Qinghe Town?"

"Familiar! How could I not be!" The proprietress perked up. "My maiden home is right next to Qinghe Town. Speaking of this Qinghe Town, it has really changed over the years."

"Oh?" Qianlong raised an eyebrow. "Changed for the better or for the worse?"

The proprietress lowered her voice: "That... is hard to say. Qinghe Town used to be truly good, with happy people and light taxes. But ever since the new magistrate arrived three years ago, tsk tsk..." She shook her head and didn't continue.

Qianlong and Ji Xiaolan exchanged a look. Ji Xiaolan understood and took over: "Proprietress, please speak freely. We are just passing merchants, just listening to gossip."

The proprietress looked around, and seeing there was no one else in the tea shed, she whispered: "The new magistrate's surname is Wang, called Wang Youcai. He was diligent when he first arrived, but he changed in less than half a year. Not only did he increase taxes and levies, but he also indulged his brother-in-law, Liu Fugui, to run rampant in the town. Forcibly buying land, bullying the people—he does everything."

Xiao Yanzi was filled with righteous indignation: "So evil? Does no one manage him?"

"Who would manage him?" The proprietress sighed. "Magistrate Wang has connections above him; I heard he has a backer in the capital. The common people have nowhere to file a complaint and can only endure it."

Ziwei frowned: "Is there really no one who can deal with him?"

"Unless..." the proprietress’s voice dropped even lower, "unless a high-ranking official comes from the capital. But in a small place like Qinghe Town, how could we ever disturb the great masters of the capital?"

Qianlong’s expression was calm, revealing no emotion. He picked up his teacup and took a sip before saying, "Thank you for telling us, proprietress. We have rested enough; it is time to go."

After paying for the tea, everyone got back into the carriage. As the carriage drove away from the tea shed, the atmosphere inside became heavy.

Jiang Rao looked at Qianlong’s tightly pursed lips and said softly, "Master..."

"I heard it," Qianlong interrupted her, a flash of severity in his eyes. "If what the proprietress said is true, I will not let either Wang Youcai or Liu Fugui off."

He turned to look out the window. The autumn fields were golden; it should have been a season of harvest and joy, but if the people worked hard only to be exploited by corrupt officials, this gold became a glaring irony.

"Ji Xiaolan," Qianlong called out.

Ji Xiaolan responded from outside the carriage: "This subject is here."

"After arriving in Qinghe Town, you go and inquire in secret first to verify the words of the tea shed proprietress. If it is true..." Qianlong’s voice turned colder, "I will meet this Magistrate Wang myself."

"This subject obeys the decree."

Jiang Rao held Qianlong’s hand: "Master, do not get angry; your health has just improved."

Qianlong held her hand back, his grip somewhat firm: "Rao'er, do you know what I hate the most?"

"Corrupt officials who bully the people."

"Correct." A look of pain flashed in Qianlong’s eyes. "Sitting in that position, I read memorials every day, and all I see is 'a prosperous country and peaceful people' and 'favorable weather.' But if I hadn't come out to see this for myself, how would I know how many people are suffering under this facade of peace?"

Jiang Rao was moved. As a time-traveler, she had read history books and knew that the Qianlong era was indeed called a golden age, but she also knew that this era was not without shadows. However, hearing Qianlong say these words himself and seeing the genuine pain in his eyes, she truly felt—this man really wanted to be a good emperor.

The convoy continued forward, and by the end of the Shen hour (around 5 PM), they arrived at Qinghe Town.

There was indeed a stone tablet at the entrance of the town, engraved with the three large characters "Qinghe Town." A clear river ran through the town, with several stone bridges spanning it, and weeping willows lined the banks; the scenery was indeed beautiful. However...

Jiang Rao frowned slightly. There were not many pedestrians on the street, and most of them were in a hurry, with worried expressions on their faces. Although the shops on both sides were open, they were deserted. This was far from the "simple customs and people living and working in peace" she had imagined.

The convoy stopped at the largest inn in the town, "Qinghe Inn." The innkeeper was a thin, middle-aged man. Seeing the extraordinary bearing of their group, he hurried to greet them attentively. Yet, there was always a sense of caution in his smile.

While arranging the rooms, Ji Xiaolan asked as if offhandedly, "Innkeeper, is there any fresh news in town? Our master enjoys hearing about local happenings."

The innkeeper’s smile stiffened. "Fresh news... no, none at all. The town is very peaceful."

"But I heard," Ji Xiaolan said, stroking his beard, "that the local Master Liu is quite an interesting character?"

The innkeeper’s expression changed. He looked around and lowered his voice: "Sir, you’d best not mention Master Liu. That is... that is Magistrate Wang’s brother-in-law. No one in town dares to cross him." He paused, then added, "If you are just passing through, stay the night and be on your way. Don’t go looking for trouble."

The message was clear enough.

Upstairs, Qianlong stood by the window of the guest room, looking out at the cold, quiet street with a solemn expression. Ji Xiaolan entered to report: "Master, I have asked several people, and the situation is exactly as the tea stall owner described. Wang Youcai is raising taxes to hoard wealth, and Liu Fugui is seizing land and bullying the markets. The people are suffering miserably."

"Is there concrete evidence?"

"There is." Ji Xiaolan took a stack of papers from his sleeve. "These are petitions that several commoners secretly pressed into my hands when I went to the teahouse just now. They heard there were merchants from the capital, and they are holding onto a glimmer of hope..."

Qianlong took the petitions and flipped through them page by page. The more he read, the darker his expression became. The incidents written in the petitions—one after another—were shocking: seizing fertile land, driving people to their deaths, forcibly abducting women, and setting up private torture chambers...

"A fine Wang Youcai! A fine Liu Fugui!" Qianlong slammed the petitions onto the table. "Tomorrow, I am going to the county office!"

"Master, please think twice," Ji Xiaolan advised. "Wang Youcai has been operating here for three years and is deeply entrenched. If you reveal your identity directly, I fear he may act out of desperation."

Qianlong sneered. "Then what is your suggestion?"

"Perhaps," Ji Xiaolan mused, "we should visit as wealthy merchants tomorrow to test the waters. It will not be too late to reveal your identity once we have obtained conclusive evidence."

Qianlong pondered for a moment and nodded. "We shall do as you say. Erkang, go prepare a generous gift. Tomorrow, I shall 'pay a visit' to Magistrate Wang."

"As you command."

Jiang Rao had been listening from the side and spoke up only then: "The master is going to the county office tomorrow?"

"Yes." Qianlong held her hand. "Don't worry, I have a plan."

"That is not what concerns me," Jiang Rao shook her head. "I was wondering... may I accompany you tomorrow?"

Qianlong was startled. "What for? A place like the county office..."

"I want to see it with my own eyes." Jiang Rao looked up at him, her eyes shining with determination. "To see what these corrupt officials, of whom the people speak, truly look like. And to see how the master... upholds justice for the people."

Qianlong looked at her for a long time, then slowly nodded. "Very well. You shall come with me tomorrow."

That night, Qinghe Town was exceptionally quiet. Jiang Rao lay beside Qianlong, but could not fall asleep for a long time. The moonlight outside was cold, spilling in through the window paper and casting mottled shadows on the floor.

She thought of the terrified yet expectant eyes of the commoners who had secretly slipped them the petitions, and the fearful look on the innkeeper’s face when he spoke of Liu Fugui. This town seemed peaceful, but what kind of undercurrents were surging beneath the surface?

"Can't sleep?" Qianlong’s voice sounded in her ear.

"Yes." Jiang Rao turned over to face him. "Master, tell me... in this world, how many more Qinghe Towns are there? How many more Wang Youcais and Liu Fuguis?"

Qianlong was silent for a moment before saying, "I do not know. But since I have seen this one, I will see it through to the end."

"And what about the ones you cannot see?"

"That is why I have come out to look." Qianlong pulled her into his arms. "This incognito tour has shown me so much that I could not see from within the palace. Upon returning to the capital, I will reform the laws, reorganize the civil service, and purge corruption. Though I may not be able to eradicate it entirely, I will do what I can, bit by bit."

The moonlight flowed silently, and the night grew deeper.

In another room at the inn, Xiaoyanzi was leaning against the window, looking out at the cold street. She said to Ziwei, "Ziwei, I keep feeling like this town is strange. There are hardly any people on the street; it’s completely devoid of life."

Ziwei was embroidering under the lamp and looked up at her words. "You felt it too? Today at the teahouse, I saw that the people all spoke with such caution, as if they were afraid of something."

"They must be afraid of that Master Liu!" Xiaoyanzi said indignantly. "When I see him, I’ll have to teach him a lesson!"

Yongqi pushed the door open and happened to hear this. He quickly said, "Xiaoyanzi, don't do anything reckless! The master has his own plans; we must follow his instructions."

Xiaoyanzi pouted. "I know. I’m just so angry."

Erkang followed Yongqi inside, his expression solemn. "Fifth Prince, just now Master Ji said that the master intends to go to the county office tomorrow. We must be prepared, just in case."

Yongqi nodded. "I understand. Ertai has already gone to make arrangements; there will be people protecting the county office from the shadows tomorrow."

Ziwei set down her embroidery hoop, worried. "Will everything be alright?"

"Don't worry," Erkang held her hand. "With us here, we will never let anything happen to the master and the lady."

chapters.title: Deeply Hidden
chapters.content:
The next morning, Qinghe Town was shrouded in a light mist. When Qianlong rose, Jiang Rao was already awake, sitting on the edge of the bed wrapped in a quilt, her dark hair disheveled over her shoulders, her eyes still hazy with sleep.

"Awake?" Qianlong sat on the edge of the bed and reached out to smooth her hair.

Jiang Rao rubbed her eyes and let out a small yawn, then suddenly leaned close to Qianlong, wrinkling her nose to sniff. "The master still smells like medicine... you didn't drink it properly last night, did you?"

This sudden, charmingly naive questioning caught Qianlong off guard, and he laughed. "I drank it, why wouldn't I?"

"Then why is there still a smell of medicine?" Jiang Rao was relentless. She crawled over and draped herself across his back, sniffing like a little cat. "You must have only drunk half and secretly poured the rest away!"

Qianlong was amused by her behavior and reached back to pull her into his arms. "I am not a child; why would I pour away medicine?"

"That's hard to say." Jiang Rao found a comfortable spot in his arms, poking his chest with her finger. "When I was little and sick, I would always secretly pour my medicine into the flower pot. Later, that pot of orchids withered."

Qianlong caught her mischievous finger. "So you are here to check if I poured away my medicine?"

"Exactly!" Jiang Rao nodded righteously, her eyes sparkling. "I am 'Madam Ai' now, I have to look after the master and not let you be willful." As she spoke, she suddenly thought of something and struggled out of Qianlong's arms. "Right, we are going to the county office today, I must dress properly so as not to lose face for the master."

She jumped off the bed and ran barefoot to the clothing trunk, starting to rummage through it. Qianlong looked at her slender back and bare ankles, frowning. "The floor is cold, put on your shoes."

"Just a moment." Jiang Rao didn't look back, pulling out two garments to compare. "Master, do you think this water-red one is better, or this lotus-root-pink one?"

Qianlong walked behind her, picked up her embroidered shoes, and crouched down to hold her ankles. "Lift your feet."

Jiang Rao was startled and obediently lifted her feet for him to put on her shoes. Qianlong’s hands were warm, and both of them shivered when they touched her slightly cool insteps. He kept his head down, gently putting on her shoes, before standing up to answer her question: "The water-red one, it suits you."

"The master thinks water-red is better too?" Jiang Rao’s eyes curved into crescents. She immediately hugged the water-red qipao to her chest, then remembered something. "But will water-red be too flashy? It’s like going to a wedding feast... The lotus-root-pink is more dignified, but will it be too plain? The master is going to handle official business, if I am too plain, it might seem like I don't take it seriously..."

She stood there holding the two garments, torn and frowning. Her conflicted little expression made Qianlong’s heart soften completely.

"Bring both." He took the garments from her. "Wear the lotus-root-pink when we first go to the county office; it looks dignified. If we need to walk around town later, you can change into the water-red one."

"Right!" Jiang Rao’s eyes lit up. "The master is so smart!" She stood on tiptoe and kissed Qianlong on the cheek, then happily ran back to the vanity. "Then I shall start getting ready!"

Qianlong touched the spot on his cheek where she had kissed him, shaking his head with a smile. The coldness and distance of the past few days seemed to have never existed; she had returned to being that charming and lively young woman.

At breakfast, when everyone saw Jiang Rao’s radiant appearance, they all breathed a sigh of relief. Xiaoyanzi bit into a bun and mumbled, "The lady is in such a good mood today!"

Jiang Rao was sipping her porridge, and at these words, she looked up and winked at Xiaoyanzi. "I am going to 'act' with the master today, so naturally I must be in high spirits." She said, leaning into Qianlong’s ear and whispering in a "secret" voice that everyone could hear: "Master, is our 'script' ready? I have been memorizing my lines for a long time."

Qianlong was amused by her feigned mysteriousness and cooperated by lowering his voice: "It is ready. You just need to play the part of 'Madam Ai' well."

"And what if I don't play it well?" Jiang Rao tilted her head, looking "worried."

"If you don't play it well..." Qianlong deliberately mused, "then when we return, I will punish you by making you embroider ten pouches for me."

"Ten?!" Jiang Rao exclaimed. "When would I finish that? My fingers would be pricked through!" She held out her slender hands, looking aggrieved.

Everyone laughed, and even the usually serious Ji Xiaolan stroked his beard and smiled.

After breakfast, the group headed to the county office. Jiang Rao was indeed wearing the lotus-root-pink qipao embroidered with lotus vines, covered by a moon-white vest. A white jade hairpin given to her by Qianlong was tucked into her hair, making her look both dignified and spirited. She held Qianlong’s arm, walking with a light step, occasionally turning her head to whisper to him, her eyes full of charm.

Upon arriving at the county office, after the bailiffs announced them, Wang Youcai received them in the flower hall. Seeing Qianlong and his group enter, he did not stand up, but only stroked his beard and smiled: "Master Ai, you have come from afar; I apologize for not welcoming you sooner."

His attitude was every bit that of an arrogant official.

Qianlong wore a smile, cupped his hands to exchange pleasantries, and signaled for Ji Xiaolan to present the gifts. Wang Youcai glanced at them, a flash of disdain in his eyes, but he still had his men accept them.

Jiang Rao sat beside Qianlong, eyes downcast, appearing quiet and demure. But when the maid served tea, she picked up the cup and gently stirred the floating leaves with the lid, then suddenly gave a soft "Oh."

"What is it?" Qianlong turned to look at her.

Jiang Rao furrowed her delicate brows, looking at the emerald-green tea in the cup, and muttered softly: "This tea... why is it from a previous harvest?"

Wang Youcai’s expression changed slightly. "Madam is joking, this is new tea."

"Is it?" Jiang Rao tilted her head, looking innocent. "But I often drink Longjing in the capital, and the aroma of new tea should be crisp and clear. This tea’s fragrance is a bit murky..." She took a small sip, then wrinkled her face. "And it’s a bit astringent."

She looked for all the world like a pampered lady from a wealthy family, one accustomed to luxury and picky about her food and drink. Yet, the implication in her words made Wang Youcai’s heart skip a beat—one who could distinguish aged Longjing tea was no ordinary merchant’s wife.

Qianlong seized the moment to smooth things over: "My wife is spoiled; I hope Magistrate Wang will forgive her."

Wang Youcai gave a dry laugh. "Not at all, not at all. The Madam has excellent taste." He cast a few more glances at Jiang Rao, his suspicions deepening.

As they spoke, a commotion arose outside. A bailiff came to report that a woman was seeking to file a complaint. Just as Wang Youcai was about to have her chased away, Qianlong interjected: "Since we’ve encountered this, why not let us broaden our horizons? I, too, would like to see how Magistrate Wang handles a case."

Left with no choice, Wang Youcai had no option but to hold court.
